definition_zh: 由……组成；由……构成；由（材料）制成；由（人员）组成；含有（化学成分）；由（地层）构成；由（部分）构成；由（词汇、物种）构成
definition_en: to consist of particular materials, parts, members or elements that together make up the whole
core_image: 一只陶罐被轻轻敲开，断口露出三层颜色不同的泥料，每一层都能单独叫出名字
scene: 修复师把碎陶片按颜色和颗粒分成几堆，摆在白纸上，再一层层拼回罐身，最后指出它由三种泥料烧成。 The ancient jar can be composed of three distinct clay layers.
sceneCN: 修复师在案上拼合陶片（第 1 个义项：由材料组成）；句意为这只古罐可能由三层不同的泥料构成。图中可辨识物件：陶片、白纸、放大镜、颜色标签。

be composed of stone and timber

由同一拉丁分词而来，义为「复合的；复合材料」

senses.title: Made of materials
senses.definition: to be made from particular materials that are mixed or combined
senses.definitionCN: 由若干被混合或结合起来的特定材料制成
senses.example: The mortar can be composed of sand, lime and water.
senses.exampleCN: 这种砂浆可以由砂、石灰与水组成。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to place things together, so the phrase begins with material laid beside material.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为把东西放在一起，因此该短语从材料与材料并排摆放开始。

senses.title: Parts forming a whole
senses.definition: to consist of separate parts that together make one complete structure
senses.definitionCN: 由若干分开的部分组成，这些部分合起来构成一个完整结构
senses.example: The roof can be composed of six prefabricated panels.
senses.exampleCN: 这个屋顶可以由六块预制板构成。
senses.why: Placing parts together is the literal picture, and the finished structure is the result of that placement.
senses.whyCN: 把部件放在一起就是字面画面，而完成的结构正是这种摆放的结果。

senses.title: People forming a body
senses.titleCN: 人员组成团队或委员会
senses.definition: to consist of named members who together form a team, board or committee
senses.definitionCN: 由指明的成员组成，他们合起来构成团队、董事会或委员会
senses.example: The review board can be composed of five independent experts.
senses.exampleCN: 评审委员会可以由五位独立专家组成。
senses.why: A committee is a whole assembled from people, so the same verb that builds objects also builds bodies.
senses.whyCN: 委员会是由人装配成的整体，因此造物的动词也用来造组织。

senses.title: Chemical composition
senses.definition: to consist of chemical elements or compounds in fixed proportions
senses.definitionCN: 由按一定比例存在的化学元素或化合物构成
senses.example: The mineral can be composed of calcium carbonate and traces of iron.
senses.exampleCN: 这种矿物可以由碳酸钙与微量铁构成。
senses.why: Chemistry lists ingredients the way a recipe does, and the phrase names that list.
senses.whyCN: 化学像食谱一样列出成分，这个短语指的就是这份清单。

senses.title: Layered rock or strata
senses.definition: to consist of beds or layers stacked in a definite order
senses.definitionCN: 由按确定次序叠置的层或岩层构成
senses.example: The cliff face can be composed of alternating shale and sandstone beds.
senses.exampleCN: 这处崖面可以由页岩与砂岩层交替构成。
senses.why: Geology reads a cliff as a stack of placed layers, which is the Latin verb taken literally.
senses.whyCN: 地质学把崖壁读成一叠摆放好的层，这正是那个拉丁动词的字面用法。

senses.title: Structure of a work
senses.definition: to consist of sections or movements arranged into a larger artistic whole
senses.definitionCN: 由若干段落或乐章排列成一个更大的艺术整体
senses.example: The symphony can be composed of four contrasting movements.
senses.exampleCN: 这部交响曲可以由四个对比鲜明的乐章构成。
senses.why: To compose music and to compose a whole use the same arranging gesture, so structure and creation share the phrase.
senses.whyCN: 谱写音乐与组合整体使用同一个排列动作，因此结构与创作共用这个短语。

senses.title: Words forming a corpus
senses.definition: to consist of texts or words collected into a body of language data
senses.definitionCN: 由收集起来构成语言数据总体的文本或词语组成
senses.example: The learner corpus can be composed of essays written by secondary students.
senses.exampleCN: 这个学习者语料库可以由中学生撰写的文章构成。
senses.why: A corpus is a body built from many texts, and the phrase treats each text as a placed piece.
senses.whyCN: 语料库是由许多文本建成的整体，这个短语把每篇文本当作摆放进去的一块。

senses.title: Members of an ecological community
senses.definition: to consist of species or populations that together form a community
senses.definitionCN: 由若干物种或种群组成，它们合起来构成一个群落
senses.example: The reef community can be composed of corals, algae and grazing fish.
senses.exampleCN: 这个珊瑚礁群落可以由珊瑚、藻类与食草鱼类组成。
senses.why: An ecosystem is an assembly of living parts, so the phrase extends the placed-together image to species.
senses.whyCN: 生态系统是活体部件的装配，于是该短语把「放在一起」的画面扩展到物种。

intro.en: Compose comes from Latin componere, to put together, from com-, together, and ponere, to place. Its past participle compositus passed through French composer into English, and the passive frame be composed of was added later.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语「componere」「组合」，由「com-」「一起」与「ponere」「放置」构成。其过去分词「compositus」经法语「composer」进入英语，后来再加上被动框架「be composed of」。

items.en: Ponere meant to place, put or set something down, and it supplied the core of the verb.
items.cn: 「ponere」意为放置、放下或安置，是该动词的核心。

items.en: The prefix com- meant together or with, and it took the form com- before a p.
items.cn: 前缀「com-」意为一起或共同，在「p」之前取「com-」这一形式。

items.en: Putting com- before ponere produced componere, to place things together and so to arrange or compose.
items.cn: 把「com-」放在「ponere」前得到「componere」，意为把东西放在一起，进而指排列或组合。

items.en: The past participle compositus meant put together or arranged, and English took that shape for the adjective composed.
items.cn: 过去分词「compositus」意为已组合的、已排列的，英语的形容词「composed」就取了这个形状。

items.en: The verb passed through French composer, which still meant to put together and also to produce a work.
items.cn: 这个动词经法语「composer」传入，仍指把东西放在一起，也指创作作品。

items.en: English compose covers making up a whole, writing a text and writing music, all from the same placing-together image.
items.cn: 英语「compose」既指构成整体，也指写作与作曲，都来自同一个「放在一起」的画面。

note.en: The first group looks like compose and shares its root; the second group contrasts three ways of linking things: composed of names the parts that make a whole, characterized by names the mark that identifies it, and associated with reports only a statistical or accompanying link.
note.cn: 第一组与「compose」形近且同源；第二组对照三种连接方式：「composed of」指出构成整体的各个部分，「characterized by」指出识别事物的标志，「associated with」只表示统计或伴随的联系。

entries.definition: To make up a whole, to arrange parts, or to write a text or a piece of music.
entries.definitionCN: 指构成整体、排列部分，或写作、作曲。

entries.definition: The act of putting parts together, the resulting structure, or a written work.
entries.definitionCN: 指把部分组合起来的行为、由此形成的结构，或一篇作品。

entries.definition: A person who writes music, one who arranges parts into a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指创作音乐的人，即把部分排列成整体的人。

entries.definition: One of the parts that together make up a larger whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指合起来构成更大整体的部件之一。

entries.definition: Made of separate parts combined into one, or such a combined material.
entries.definitionCN: 指由分开的部分合成一体的，也指这样的合成材料。

entries.definition: To be made up of parts; it comes from a different Latin verb meaning to stand, so it is not the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 指由部分组成；它来自另一个意为「站立」的拉丁动词，并非同一词源。

entries.definition: To include or be made up of; it comes from a Latin verb meaning to grasp together, a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 指包含或由……构成；它来自一个意为「抓在一起」的拉丁动词，词源不同。

entries.definition: To be formed from parts, the plain everyday version of the same idea.
entries.definitionCN: 指由部分组成，是同一意思的日常平实说法。

entries.definition: To be linked to something, often statistically; it does not say what the thing is made of.
entries.definitionCN: 指与某事物相联系，常是统计上的；它并不说明事物由什么构成。

entries.definition: To have a defining mark; it names an identifying feature, not the parts.
entries.definitionCN: 指具有定义性标志；它说明识别特征，而非组成部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the literal placing-together picture and the many wholes the phrase can inventory.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用字面上「放在一起」的画面，以及该短语能清点出的各种整体。

normal.en: Com- means together and ponere means to place, so compose is literally to place together.
normal.cn: 「com-」意为一起，「ponere」意为放置，因此「compose」字面上就是把东西放在一起。

normal.en: Composition, composer, component and composite all keep the same placed-together picture.
normal.cn: 「composition」「composer」「component」「composite」都保留着同一个「放在一起」的画面。

normal.en: A committee is composed of members, a cake is composed of layers, and a poem is composed of lines.
normal.cn: 委员会由成员组成，蛋糕由层组成，诗由行组成。

normal.en: Be composed of names the parts; it does not name the mark that identifies them.
normal.cn: 「be composed of」点出部分，并不点出识别这些部分的标志。

normal.en: Consist of and comprise are close in meaning but come from different Latin verbs.
normal.cn: 「consist of」与「comprise」意思接近，却来自不同的拉丁动词。

abstract.en: A whole is a promise that its parts can be listed, and the phrase keeps that promise.
abstract.cn: 整体是一种承诺，承诺它的部分可以被列出来，而这个短语兑现了这份承诺。

abstract.en: The same word builds a jar from clay, a board from people and a reef from species.
abstract.cn: 同一个词用陶土造罐、用人组成委员会、用物种组成珊瑚礁。

abstract.en: Composition is neither a feature nor a statistical link; it is the inventory of what is inside.
abstract.cn: 构成既不是特征，也不是统计联系；它是内部东西的清单。

examples.en: The wall can be composed of local stone and lime mortar.
examples.cn: 这面墙可以由本地石料与石灰砂浆构成。

examples.en: The committee can be composed of teachers, parents and doctors.
examples.cn: 这个委员会可以由教师、家长与医生组成。

examples.en: The atmosphere can be composed of several layers with different temperatures.
examples.cn: 大气可以由若干温度不同的层构成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「比 康剖兹德 欧夫」——把几块料放进一只罐里，再数清里面有几样：由……组成

root: 拉丁语「com-」「一起」加「ponere」「放置」构成「componere」「组合」，过去分词「compositus」，经法语「composer」进入英语，再加被动框架「be composed of」。要注意：它与「comprise」（来自「comprehendere」「抓在一起」）和「consist」（来自「sistere」「站立」）形近而来源不同，不可混为一谈。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the same inventory: material, parts, members, elements, layers, movements, texts and species are all counted as what the whole contains.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项遵循同一份清单：材料、部件、成员、元素、岩层、乐章、文本与物种都被算作整体所含的内容。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a jar is broken open and three coloured clay layers are counted one by one inside the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：陶罐被敲开，罐壁里三层颜色不同的泥料被一层层数出来。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL MIX: clay, sand or chemical elements named as what the thing contains.
branches.cn: 材料配比：陶土、砂石或化学元素，用来说明事物含有什么。

branches.en: THE LAYERED WHOLE: prefabricated panels or rock beds stacked into a structure.
branches.cn: 层叠整体：预制板或岩层叠合成一个结构。

branches.en: THE MEMBER BODY: a board of people or a community of species that fills the whole.
branches.cn: 成员整体：由人组成的委员会，或由物种组成的群落。

branches.en: THE BUILT WORK: movements of a symphony arranged into a larger composition.
branches.cn: 构建的作品：交响曲的乐章排列成更大的作品。

branches.en: THE WORD INVENTORY: a corpus filled by essays from many writers.
branches.cn: 词汇清单：由众多作者的文章填充起来的语料库。

intro.en: The phrase is a Latin verb of placing, fitted with an English passive frame; its parts are com-, ponere and the participle ending.
intro.cn: 这个短语是一个表示「放置」的拉丁动词，装上英语被动框架；其构件是「com-」「ponere」与分词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies ponere, com- and componere with its participle compositus; French passes the verb on, and English adds compose and its family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「ponere」「com-」与「componere」及其分词「compositus」；法语把动词传下来，英语再加上「compose」及其同族词。

items.example: The verb names the act of laying something in position.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指把某物放在某一位置的动作。

items.example: The prefix adds the idea of several things meeting.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀加上若干事物会合的意思。

items.structure: Latin verb from com- and ponere
items.example: The verb places parts side by side into one thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把部件并排摆成一个东西。

items.example: The participle describes the finished whole.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词描述已完成组合的整体。

items.example: The English verb covers both structure and creation.
items.exampleCN: 这个英语动词既指结构，也指创作。

items.meaning: the way parts are put together
items.example: The noun names the arrangement and its result.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指排列方式及其结果。

items.example: The ending names the person who arranges the parts.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾指排列部件的人。

items.structure: English noun from the same stem
items.meaning: a part of a larger whole
items.example: Each component can be named separately.
items.exampleCN: 每个部件都能单独命名。

items.example: The word describes a whole built from separate pieces.
items.exampleCN: 这个词描述由分开的块件建成的整体。

items.example: It names a substance made by combining others.

definition_zh: 拟态行为；模仿行为
definition_en: behavior in which an organism copies the appearance, signals or movements of another, or in which a person copies another's actions
core_image: 一只鸟跟着另一只鸟点头、转身，节奏几乎同步
scene: 观察站里，两只鸟轮流发出同一种叫声，动作一前一后完全对应。 Researchers recorded mimicry behavior in pairs of birds that alternated the same call.
sceneCN: 这里 mimicry behavior 指「个体复制同类动作或信号的整套行为」（第 1 个义项：动物通过模仿他者的动作、姿态或叫声而获得某种功能）；句意为研究者记录了一对鸟轮流发出同一种叫声的拟态行为。图中可辨识物件：观察站、两只鸟、同步的抬头动作、录音设备。

pos.zh: 拟态行为；模仿行为（不可数；指具体事例时可用复数 mimicry behaviors）

collocations.zh: 成对个体间的模仿行为

senses.title: Animal resemblance in action
senses.definition: the actions by which one animal copies another's appearance, posture or signals in order to survive
senses.definitionCN: 一种动物复制另一种动物的外观、姿态或信号以求生存的行为
senses.example: Researchers recorded mimicry behavior in pairs of birds that alternated the same call.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者记录了一对鸟轮流发出同一种叫声的拟态行为。
senses.why: The compound names behaviour that carries out mimicry: the resemblance is not just a pattern on the body but something the animal does.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词命名的是实施拟态的行为：相似不只在体表图案上，也体现在动物所做的动作上。

senses.title: Social copying of posture and speech
senses.titleCN: 社交中的姿态与语调趋同
senses.definition: the unconscious or deliberate copying of another person's posture, gesture or speech style during interaction
senses.definitionCN: 互动中无意或有意复制他人的姿态、手势或说话风格
senses.example: Social mimicry behavior increases when two people feel rapport.
senses.exampleCN: 两人感到投缘时，社交模仿行为会增多。
senses.why: Human interaction repeats the animal pattern: copying a posture signals that the copier belongs.
senses.whyCN: 人类互动重复了动物的模式：复制姿态等于发出归属信号。

senses.title: Courtship copying of signals
senses.definition: the copying of courtship displays or signals by a rival or a satellite male
senses.definitionCN: 竞争对手或卫星雄体复制求偶展示或信号的行为
senses.example: Satellite males use mimicry behavior to approach females guarded by a larger rival.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星雄体用拟态行为接近被更大对手守护的雌性。
senses.why: In courtship the copied signal grants access, so copying becomes a reproductive tactic.
senses.whyCN: 在求偶中，被复制的信号能带来接近机会，于是复制成了繁殖策略。

senses.title: Aggressive mimicry behavior
senses.definition: behavior that copies a harmless or attractive signal in order to lure prey within reach
senses.definitionCN: 复制无害或诱人的信号，把猎物引到可及范围内的行为
senses.example: The spider's aggressive mimicry behavior imitates a mate's vibration on the web.
senses.exampleCN: 这只蜘蛛的攻击性拟态行为模仿网上配偶的振动。
senses.why: The copy is bait: the predator performs the signal that the prey wants to find.
senses.whyCN: 复制品是诱饵：捕食者表演出猎物想找到的那个信号。

senses.title: Vocal mimicry behavior
senses.definition: the copying of calls, songs or environmental sounds by an animal
senses.definitionCN: 动物复制鸣叫、歌声或环境声音的行为
senses.example: Vocal mimicry behavior lets the parrot join a household's soundscape.
senses.exampleCN: 声音模仿行为让鹦鹉融入家中的声音环境。
senses.why: When the copied channel is sound, the same behavioural label applies without any change of logic.
senses.whyCN: 当被复制的渠道是声音时，同一个行为标签照旧适用，逻辑不变。

senses.title: Copying that builds rapport
senses.definition: the use of matched gestures, rhythm or wording to make another person feel understood
senses.definitionCN: 用相合的手势、节奏或措辞让对方感到被理解
senses.example: A counsellor's gentle mimicry behavior can put a nervous client at ease.
senses.exampleCN: 咨询师温和的模仿行为能让紧张的来访者放松。
senses.why: Copying reduces distance; the behaviour is read as agreement rather than as imitation.
senses.whyCN: 复制缩短距离；这种行为被读作认同，而不是被看作模仿。

senses.title: Copying as a research variable
senses.titleCN: 作为研究变量的模仿行为
senses.definition: the measurable copying of movements or timing that psychologists code in interaction studies
senses.definitionCN: 心理学家在互动研究中编码的可测量动作或时序复制
senses.example: The team coded mimicry behavior frame by frame from the video.
senses.exampleCN: 团队逐帧编码视频中的模仿行为。
senses.why: Once behaviour is measured, the phrase becomes a countable variable rather than a description.
senses.whyCN: 一旦行为被测量，这个短语就成了可计数的变量，而不再是描述。

senses.title: Imitation by machines or avatars
senses.titleCN: 机器或虚拟形象的模仿行为
senses.definition: the reproduction of human movements or speech by a robot, avatar or generative system
senses.definitionCN: 机器人、虚拟形象或生成系统复制人类动作或言语的行为
senses.example: The avatar's mimicry behavior made the interview feel strangely natural.
senses.exampleCN: 虚拟形象的模仿行为让这场面试显得异样地自然。
senses.why: The newest extension moves the compound from organisms to systems that learn to copy people.
senses.whyCN: 最新的引申把这个复合词从生物移到学会复制人的系统上。

intro.en: Mimicry behavior is an English compound of two learned words: mimicry from Greek mimos through Latin and French, and behavior from the native verb behave, of uncertain formation.
intro.cn: mimicry behavior 是由两个学术词构成的英语复合词：mimicry 出自希腊 mimos，经拉丁语与法语传入；behavior 出自本族动词 behave，其构词方式存疑。

items.en: Greek mimos 'imitator' and its adjective mimikos underlie mimicry.
items.cn: 希腊 mimos「模仿者」及其形容词 mimikos 是 mimicry 的基础。

items.en: Latin mimus and mimicus are Greek loans; French mimique then passed the adjective into English.
items.cn: 拉丁 mimus 与 mimicus 是希腊语借词；法语 mimique 随后把这个形容词带入英语。

items.en: Behavior derives from behave, first recorded in the sixteenth century as be- plus have, meaning 'to conduct oneself'.
items.cn: behavior 来自 behave，16 世纪首次记录，由 be- 加 have 构成，意为「持身、举止」。

items.en: The compound mimicry behavior is a twentieth-century formation of technical English, built from two existing nouns rather than from a single root.
items.cn: 复合词 mimicry behavior 是 20 世纪技术英语的构词，由两个既有名词组合，而非出自单一词根。

items.en: Ethologists and psychologists standardized the phrase when copying became a measured variable rather than an anecdote.
items.cn: 当复制成为可测量的变量而非轶事时，动物行为学家与心理学家把这个短语固定下来。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first use of the full compound is unrecorded, and the formation of behave is debated, with French influence suspected but not proved. The Greek root itself is secure.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：完整复合词的最早使用无记录；behave 的构词方式有争议，所疑的法语影响未被证实；希腊词根本身可靠。

note.en: Group one separates the compound from its two source nouns and its spelling variants; group two separates kinds of copying behaviour by function.
note.cn: 第一组把该复合词与它的两个来源名词及拼写变体分开；第二组按功能区分不同类型的复制行为。

entries.definition: The resemblance or practice itself; mimicry behavior names the actions that produce or use it.
entries.definitionCN: 指相似本身或这种做法；mimicry behavior 指产生或运用它的具体动作。

entries.definition: Any conduct; the compound narrows it to conduct that copies.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何举止；复合词把它收窄为复制性的举止。

entries.definition: The same term in British spelling, or a plural counting specific instances.
entries.definitionCN: 同一术语的英式拼写，或指具体事例的复数形式。

entries.definition: A looser variant built on the verb mimic; the fixed technical term uses the noun mimicry.
entries.definitionCN: 以动词 mimic 为基础的较松散变体；固定技术术语用名词 mimicry。

entries.definition: Copying posture and speech to build rapport; it is one kind of mimicry behavior, not the whole class.
entries.definitionCN: 指通过复制姿态与言语建立亲近感；它只是拟态行为的一类。

entries.definition: Imitation treated as a general process in art or biology, without reference to measured actions.
entries.definitionCN: 把模仿当作艺术或生物中的普遍过程，不涉及可测量的动作。

entries.definition: The everyday word for reproducing something; it makes no claim about signals or survival value.
entries.definitionCN: 日常用词，泛指复制；不涉及信号或生存价值。

entries.definition: One staged instance of copying; mimicry behavior covers the whole recurring pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 指一次具体的模仿展示；mimicry behavior 指整套反复出现的行为模式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real source nouns, the real spelling variants, and the way ethology and psychology actually use the phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的来源名词、真实的拼写变体，以及动物行为学与心理学实际使用该短语的方式。

normal.en: mimicry plus behavior: the doing of imitation.
normal.cn: mimicry 加 behavior：模仿这件事的实施。

normal.en: The family runs mimicry, mimic, mimetic, behavior, behavioral.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mimicry、mimic、mimetic、behavior、behavioral。

normal.en: American spelling behavior, British behaviour.
normal.cn: 美式拼写 behavior，英式拼写 behaviour。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: animal mimicry behavior, social mimicry behavior, vocal mimicry behavior.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 animal mimicry behavior、social mimicry behavior、vocal mimicry behavior。

normal.en: The phrase is countable only when it means individual cases.
normal.cn: 只有指具体个案时，这个短语才可数。

abstract.en: Picture two birds nodding in turn like two pendulums sharing one beat.
abstract.cn: 想象两只鸟轮流点头，像两个共享同一节拍的单摆。

abstract.en: Picture a conversation in which one person slowly adopts the other's rhythm.
abstract.cn: 想象一段对话，其中一人慢慢采用了另一人的节奏。

abstract.en: Picture a lure that performs the exact vibration a spider's prey expects.
abstract.cn: 想象一个诱饵，表演出蜘蛛猎物正期待的那种振动。

examples.en: The study links mimicry behavior to the survival of the brood.
examples.cn: 这项研究把拟态行为与整窝幼体的存活联系起来。

examples.en: Social mimicry behavior is strongest among people who already agree.
examples.cn: 社交模仿行为在本来意见相合的人之间最强。

examples.en: The robot's mimicry behavior was judged natural by most viewers.
examples.cn: 多数观看者认为这台机器人的模仿行为很自然。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mimicry（模仿）+ behavior（行为）」——做出来的模仿 → 拟态行为；模仿行为

root: 希腊 mimos「模仿者」→ 拉丁 mimus、mimicus → 法语 mimique → 英语 mimicry；behavior 由本族动词 behave（be- + have）派生；整个短语为 20 世纪英语复合词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses take one copied action through its uses: survival resemblance, social bonding, courtship, luring prey, voice, rapport, measurement, and finally machines that copy people.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一种复制动作依次放进不同用途：生存相似、社交联结、求偶、诱捕、声音、亲近感、测量，最后是复制人的机器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two birds nodding in turn, one beat apart, until their rhythms lock.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只鸟轮流点头，相差一拍，直到节奏锁合。

branches.en: SURVIVAL USE: resemblance, courtship access and luring all depend on the copy being believed.
branches.cn: 生存用途：相似、求偶接近与诱捕都依赖复制品被相信。

branches.en: SOCIAL USE: copied posture and rhythm turn strangers into allies.
branches.cn: 社交用途：被复制的姿态与节奏把陌生人变成同盟。

branches.en: VOICE: the copied channel is sound rather than sight.
branches.cn: 声音：被复制的渠道是听觉而非视觉。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: behaviour is coded frame by frame as data.
branches.cn: 测量：行为被逐帧编码成数据。

branches.en: MACHINE COPY: systems learn to reproduce human conduct.
branches.cn: 机器复制：系统学会复现人类举止。

intro.en: The phrase is a compound of a Greek-derived noun and a native-derived noun of behaviour; there is no single root or prefix to divide.
intro.cn: 这个短语是希腊来源名词与本族来源行为名词的复合，无法再分成单一词根加词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin contributes only mimus and mimicus, both Greek loans; behave is native Germanic and has no Latin etymon.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语只贡献 mimus 与 mimicus，两者都是希腊语借词；behave 属本族日耳曼语，没有拉丁词源。

items.example: Mimicry is the older noun.
items.exampleCN: mimicry 是更早的名词。

items.example: Behavior can be observed and counted.
items.exampleCN: 行为可以被观察和计数。

items.example: The animals behave differently in pairs.
items.exampleCN: 这些动物成对时行为不同。

items.example: Behavioral studies code the timing of gestures.
items.exampleCN: 行为研究编码手势的时序。

items.example: The young mimic the old.
items.exampleCN: 年幼者模仿年长者。

items.example: Mimetic signals are easy to copy.
items.exampleCN: 模仿性信号容易被复制。

items.example: Mimesis names the process, not the act.
items.exampleCN: mimesis 命名过程，而非具体动作。

items.example: Mimicry behavior was coded from video.
items.exampleCN: 拟态行为已从视频中被编码。

items.example: The paper lists three mimicry behaviours.
items.exampleCN: 论文列出了三种拟态行为。

definition_zh: 文化适应；文化调适；为适应新环境而对习俗、技术与制度所作的调整
definition_en: the process by which a group or an individual adjusts customs, techniques and institutions to a new setting
core_image: 一群人在新的气候里把旧屋加高、把旧食谱换掉、把旧歌改调，屋梁上留下每一次改动的凿痕
scene: 移民社区在北方落脚后把屋顶加厚、把腌菜换成熏鱼， An exhibit shows how cultural adaptation reshaped the kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里 cultural adaptation 指「群体为适应新环境而对习俗与技术所作的调整」（第 1 个义项：整体文化调适过程）；句意为展览呈现这种文化适应如何改变了厨房的样子。图中可辨识物件：加厚的屋顶、熏鱼架、旧腌菜坛、展签。

pos.zh: 文化适应；文化调适（不可数）；一次具体的文化调适（可数）

collocations.phrase: cultural adaptation to a new climate

derivatives.zh: 文化涵化；跨文化接触中的文化改变
在文化方面；从文化角度
文化习得；在自身文化中的社会化

senses.title: A group adjusts to a new environment
senses.titleCN: 群体对新环境的整体调适
senses.definition: the process by which a community changes its customs and technology to suit a new environment
senses.definitionCN: 一个社群为适应新环境而改变习俗与技术的过程
senses.example: Cultural adaptation among the settlers included new roof shapes and new fuels.
senses.exampleCN: 定居者的文化适应包括新的屋顶形制与新的燃料。
senses.why: the phrase joins the Latin idea of cultivating a way of life to the Latin idea of fitting one thing to another, so it names a whole way of life being fitted to a place.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把拉丁「耕作、养成一种生活方式」与拉丁「使一物适配另一物」结合起来，指整套生活方式被调整以适配某地。

senses.title: One concrete adaptive custom
senses.definition: a particular practice or object adopted because it helps a group live in a new setting
senses.definitionCN: 某群体为在新环境中生活而采用的特定做法或物件
senses.example: The smoke-drying rack is a cultural adaptation to a short growing season.
senses.exampleCN: 熏鱼架是对短生长季的一项文化调适。
senses.why: once the process is familiar, each product of it can be counted and called an adaptation, so the phrase shifts from mass noun to count noun.
senses.whyCN: 过程一旦为人熟悉，它的每件产物都可以计数并称作一项 adaptation，短语便从不可数转为可数。

senses.title: A strategy in cross-cultural psychology
senses.titleCN: 跨文化心理学中的适应策略
senses.definition: the way individuals manage contact between their heritage culture and a host culture
senses.definitionCN: 个人在处理自身原有文化与所在文化接触时所采取的方式
senses.example: Integration is often the most successful cultural adaptation for migrants.
senses.exampleCN: 对移民而言，整合常是最成功的文化适应方式。
senses.why: psychology narrowed the group-level process to the individual, asking how a person holds two cultural frames at once.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把群体层面的过程收窄到个人，追问一个人如何同时持有两套文化框架。

senses.title: A change visible in material remains
senses.titleCN: 在物质遗存中可见的调适
senses.definition: in archaeology, a change in tools, houses or diet that answers a new environment
senses.definitionCN: 考古学中，工具、房屋或饮食为回应新环境而发生的变化
senses.example: Pottery with thicker walls records a cultural adaptation to colder winters.
senses.exampleCN: 器壁更厚的陶器记录了针对更冷冬季的一次文化调适。
senses.why: archaeologists cannot see a process, only its residue, so the phrase comes to name the trace of adjustment in objects.
senses.whyCN: 考古学家看不到过程，只看得到残留，于是这个短语用来指物件上留下的调适痕迹。

senses.title: Localising a policy or product
senses.titleCN: 政策或产品的本地化改编
senses.definition: the revision of a policy, service or product so that it fits a local culture
senses.definitionCN: 修改政策、服务或产品，使其契合当地文化
senses.example: The clinic's cultural adaptation of the consent form raised enrolment.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所对知情同意书所作的文化适配提高了入组率。
senses.why: organisations borrowed the anthropological phrase for a practical task: fitting a ready-made thing to the people who must use it.
senses.whyCN: 机构借用了人类学的说法来描述一项实务：把现成的东西调整给必须使用它的人。

senses.title: A work rewritten for another culture
senses.titleCN: 为另一文化改写过的作品
senses.definition: a book, film or play recast so that its setting and references suit another audience
senses.definitionCN: 经改写、使其背景与指涉适合另一受众的书、电影或戏剧
senses.example: The stage version is a cultural adaptation of a Nordic saga.
senses.exampleCN: 这个舞台版本是一部北欧萨迦的改编作品。
senses.why: the word adaptation already meant a rewritten work, so adding cultural specifies what is being adjusted rather than the medium.
senses.whyCN: adaptation 本已可指改写过的作品，加上 cultural 是说明被调整的是文化内容，而非媒介。

senses.title: Culture and biology adjusting together
senses.titleCN: 文化与生物性的协同调适
senses.definition: the mutual adjustment of a cultural practice and a biological trait over time
senses.definitionCN: 文化做法与生物性状在长时段中彼此调整
senses.example: Dairying and adult lactose tolerance are a case of cultural adaptation meeting genetics.
senses.exampleCN: 乳业与成年乳糖耐受，正是文化适应与遗传相遇的例证。
senses.why: once a practice changes what people eat, it also changes who survives, so culture and genes adapt to each other.
senses.whyCN: 一种做法一旦改变人们吃什么，也就改变了谁能存活，于是文化与基因彼此适应。

senses.title: Adjusting teaching to a culture
senses.titleCN: 教学对文化的适性调整
senses.definition: changes to curriculum, assessment or classroom practice that fit local cultural expectations
senses.definitionCN: 为使课程、评估或课堂做法契合当地文化期待而作的变化
senses.example: The school's cultural adaptation of the oral exam let students answer in pairs.
senses.exampleCN: 学校对口试所作的文化适性调整允许学生两人一组作答。
senses.why: education took the phrase from psychology and made it a design principle: methods that ignore local norms fail.
senses.whyCN: 教育学从心理学取来这个短语并当作设计原则：忽视本地规范的方法会失败。

intro.en: Cultural adaptation joins two Latin-shaped words: culture from colere 'to till', adaptation from aptare 'to fit'. The compound phrase itself is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cultural adaptation 由两个拉丁形态的词组合而成：culture 出自 colere「耕作」，adaptation 出自 aptare「使合适」。短语本身是近代产物。年代均为约数。

items.en: Colere meant 'to till, cultivate, inhabit, worship'. Its deeper origin is not settled; the range of senses already included caring for land and for gods.
items.cn: colere 意为「耕作、培育、居住、敬奉」。其更深来源未有定论；词义范围已同时包括照料土地与敬神。

items.en: Cultura named tilling and tending, and by extension the tending of the mind, from which the modern sense of culture grew.
items.cn: cultura 指耕作与照料，并引申为对心智的培育，现代「文化」义由此发展而来。

items.en: Aptus 'fit, suited' gave aptare 'to fit or adjust', the source of adapt and adaptation.
items.cn: aptus「合适的、相称的」给出 aptare「使合适、调整」，是 adapt 与 adaptation 的来源。

items.en: Culture entered English in the thirteenth century as husbandry and learning; adaptation entered in the sixteenth century for the act of fitting.
items.cn: culture 于 13 世纪以农事与学问义进入英语；adaptation 于 16 世纪以「使适配」的动作义进入英语。

items.en: Anthropology combined the two words to describe how a people adjusts its whole way of life to a habitat.
items.cn: 人类学把这两个词组合起来，描述一个民族如何把整套生活方式调整到某一生境。

items.en: Psychology, archaeology, education and marketing each took the phrase and narrowed it to their own kind of adjustment; the shared core is fitting a culture to a setting.
items.cn: 心理学、考古学、教育学与市场研究各自取用这个短语，并收窄为自己那一类调整；共同的核是让文化适配某种处境。

note.en: The first group is built on adapt and apt and is easily confused by spelling; the second holds neighbouring processes of cultural change.
note.cn: 第一组建于 adapt 与 apt，拼写极易混淆；第二组是邻近的文化变迁过程。

entries.definition: Any adjustment to a new condition, biological or practical; without cultural it need not involve a way of life.
entries.definitionCN: 对任何新条件的调整，生物性或实务性的皆可；不带 cultural 时不必涉及生活方式。

entries.definition: The act of taking something as one's own, such as a practice or a child; it names acceptance, not adjustment.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物据为己有，例如采用一种做法或收养孩子；指接受，而非调整。

entries.definition: An older spelling of adaptation that survives in some technical writing; it means the same thing and is now rare.
entries.definitionCN: adaptation 的旧拼法，仍见于部分技术文献；意思相同，如今罕见。

entries.definition: Describing a trait or practice that helps survival; the adjective describes, while the phrase names the process.
entries.definitionCN: 形容有助于生存的性状或做法；形容词是描述性的，短语则指过程本身。

entries.definition: Cultural change produced by sustained contact between two societies; the change comes from the meeting, not from a habitat.
entries.definitionCN: 两个社会长期接触所引起的文化改变；变化源于相遇，而非生境。

entries.definition: The process by which a minority group adopts the majority culture until the difference fades; it implies loss as well as fit.
entries.definitionCN: 少数群体采用多数文化直至差异消失的过程；既含适应，也含丧失。

entries.definition: The learning of one's native culture from childhood; it is acquisition, not adjustment to something new.
entries.definitionCN: 自幼习得本族文化；那是获得，而非对新事物的调整。

entries.definition: Any change made to fit circumstances; the plain term, with no claim that a whole culture is involved.
entries.definitionCN: 为适应情况而作的任何改变；最平实的说法，不表示涉及整套文化。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Latin verbs behind the phrase and the collocations researchers actually use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：短语背后两个拉丁动词，以及研究者实际使用的搭配。

normal.en: culture from colere 'to till' + adaptation from aptare 'to fit' = a way of life tilled to fit a place.
normal.cn: culture 出自 colere「耕作」+ adaptation 出自 aptare「使合适」= 被耕作到适配某地的生活方式。

normal.en: Adapt also gives adaptable, adaptive, adapter and maladaptive.
normal.cn: adapt 还给出 adaptable、adaptive、adapter、maladaptive。

normal.en: The usual frame is adaptation to something: to a climate, to a host society, to a market.
normal.cn: 常见搭配框架是「对某事物的适应」：对气候、对所在社会、对市场。

normal.en: In psychology the phrase contrasts with assimilation and separation as acculturation strategies.
normal.cn: 在心理学里，这个短语与 assimilation、separation 并列为涵化策略。

normal.en: Researchers often shorten it to cultural adaptation in titles and keep the full phrase in definitions.
normal.cn: 研究者常在标题里简写为 cultural adaptation，在定义里保留完整短语。

abstract.en: Picture a house whose roof is raised one beam at a time as the snow line drops.
abstract.cn: 想象一座房子，随着雪线下降，屋顶被一根梁一根梁地加高。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe card with old measurements crossed out and local ones pencilled in.
abstract.cn: 想象一张食谱卡，旧的计量被划掉，本地计量用铅笔补上。

abstract.en: Picture a song whose tune stays the same while the words learn a new landscape.
abstract.cn: 想象一首歌，曲调不变，歌词却学会了新的地貌。

examples.en: Cultural adaptation to the high plateau included heavier clothing and barley beer.
examples.cn: 对高原的文化适应包括更厚的衣物与青稞酒。

examples.en: The museum labels each object as a cultural adaptation rather than an invention.
examples.cn: 博物馆把每件物品标为一次文化调适，而非一项发明。

examples.en: Her research compares cultural adaptation among three groups of migrants.
examples.cn: 她的研究比较三组移民的文化适应情况。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「靠它适应」——culture 靠它、adapt 适应，合起来就是「靠文化去适应」。换地方先换活法，活法换了就是文化适应。

root: culture 出自拉丁 colere「耕作、培育」，经 cultura「耕作、培育」进入英语；adaptation 出自拉丁 aptus「合适的」所生的 aptare「使合适」。两者组合成短语是 19 世纪人类学的用法。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the whole group to single customs, then to individual psychology, material traces, policy, artworks, gene-culture coadjustment and finally the classroom.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从整个群体移到单项习俗，再到个体心理、物质痕迹、政策、作品、基因与文化的协同调整，最后落到课堂。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old house altered beam by beam until it suits a new climate.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座旧屋被一根根梁地改动，直到适配新的气候。

branches.en: PROCESS AND PRODUCT: the whole adjustment and one adjustable item are the same change seen at two scales.
branches.cn: 过程与产物：整体调整与单项可调之物，是同一变化在两个尺度上的样子。

branches.en: THE PERSON: psychology moves the unit from a community to an individual holding two cultural frames.
branches.cn: 个人：心理学把单位从社群移到同时持有两套文化框架的个人。

branches.en: THE TRACE: archaeology can only read the adjustment from what was left in the ground.
branches.cn: 痕迹：考古学只能从留在土里的东西读出这次调整。

branches.en: FITTING A READY-MADE THING: a policy or an artwork is reworked until the local audience can use it.
branches.cn: 适配现成之物：政策或作品被改写，直到本地受众能够使用。

branches.en: BODY AND CLASSROOM: practice and biology adjust to each other, and teaching adjusts to local norms.
branches.cn: 身体与课堂：做法与生物性彼此调整，教学也调整到本地规范。

intro.en: The phrase is transparent from its parts: a Latin noun of cultivation and a Latin noun of fitting, each with a living English family.
intro.cn: 这个短语从构件上一目了然：一个表示培育的拉丁名词与一个表示适配的拉丁名词，各自都有活跃的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin colere yields culture, cultivate, cult and colony; Latin aptare yields adapt, apt, aptitude and inept.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 colere 衍生 culture、cultivate、cult、colony；拉丁 aptare 衍生 adapt、apt、aptitude、inept。

items.example: The stem carries the idea of tending something over time.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干带着「长期照料某物」的意思。

items.example: The stem carries the idea of making one thing suit another.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干带着「使一物适合另一物」的意思。

items.example: The ending turns the verb adapt into the noun adaptation.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾把动词 adapt 变成名词 adaptation。

items.example: The two villages share a river culture.
items.exampleCN: 这两个村子共享一种河谷文化。

items.example: They cultivate rice on the lower terraces.
items.exampleCN: 他们在低处梯田种稻。

items.meaning: to fit oneself or something to a condition
items.example: The design adapts to both wet and dry years.
items.exampleCN: 这一设计能适应湿年与旱年。

items.example: An apt comparison makes the point at once.
items.exampleCN: 一个贴切的比较能立刻说明问题。

items.example: She showed an aptitude for languages.
items.exampleCN: 她显出语言天分。

items.example: Acculturation followed two generations of trade.
items.exampleCN: 两代人的贸易之后出现了文化涵化。

derivatives.meaning: adjusting in a way that harms survival

definition_zh: 发出信号；信号传递（过程）；（生物学）信号发送行为；（通信）信令
definition_en: the act or process of sending signals, especially as a system of communication
core_image: 夜里的池塘边，一只雄蛙鼓起鸣囊发声，邻近的雄蛙应声而答，声浪一圈圈向外推开
scene: 池塘边一只雄蛙鼓起鸣囊发声，邻近的雄蛙随即回应，声音在夜色中一层层传开。 At the pond edge one male inflates his vocal sac and calls, neighbours answer, and the sound spreads outward through the dark, a clear case of signaling.
sceneCN: 这里 signaling 指「发出信号并被接收的过程」（第 1 个义项：信号发送动作）；句意为雄蛙鸣叫、邻近雄蛙回应、声音层层传开，构成清楚的信号发送过程。可辨识物件：鼓起的鸣囊、池塘水面、夜色中的草丛、回应的另一只蛙。

pos.zh: 信号发送；信号传递（过程）
（生物学）信号行为；（通信）信令
发出信号的；信号传导的（作定语，如信号通路）

collocations.zh: 诚实信号（信号可靠地反映品质）

senses.title: The act of sending signals
senses.definition: the activity of producing a sign that another party is meant to receive
senses.definitionCN: 制造一个供他方接收的符号的活动
senses.example: Signaling began before any of the animals had moved.
senses.exampleCN: 在这些动物移动之前，信号发送就已经开始。
senses.why: The suffix -ing turns the verb into the name of an ongoing activity, so signaling is the sending seen as a process rather than as a single sign.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ing 把动词变成进行中活动的名称，因此 signaling 是被看作过程的发送，而非单个符号。

senses.title: Biological signal production
senses.titleCN: 生物学意义上的信号产生
senses.definition: the production of a cue by one organism that changes the behavior of another
senses.definitionCN: 一个生物产生线索，从而改变另一生物行为的过程
senses.example: Frog signaling peaks on warm nights after rain.
senses.exampleCN: 蛙类的信号发送在雨后温暖的夜里达到高峰。
senses.why: Biology separates the sender's act from the receiver's response, so signaling names only the first half of the exchange.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把发送者的动作与接收者的反应分开，因此 signaling 只命名这次交换的前一半。

senses.title: Telecommunications signaling
senses.definition: the exchange of control information that sets up and manages a connection
senses.definitionCN: 建立与管理连接时交换控制信息的过程
senses.example: The engineers traced the dropped calls to faulty signaling.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把掉话追查到信令故障。
senses.why: A telephone network must agree on how to start and stop a call, and that control conversation is the technical sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 电话网络必须就如何开始与结束通话达成一致，这场控制性的对话就是该词的技术义。

senses.title: Cell signaling in biology
senses.definition: the chain by which a cell receives a molecule and passes the message inward
senses.definitionCN: 细胞接收分子并把信息向内部传递的链条
senses.example: The drug blocks signaling at the receptor.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药在受体处阻断信号传导。
senses.why: The same idea of a message sent and received was scaled down to molecules, and the pathway became the standard compound.
senses.whyCN: 「消息被发送与接收」这一想法被缩小到分子层面，通路遂成为标准搭配。

senses.title: Gestural or traffic signaling
senses.definition: the use of visible movements, lights or flags to direct others
senses.definitionCN: 用可见的动作、灯光或旗子指挥他人
senses.example: Night signaling with torches was forbidden on the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 山脊上禁止用火把做夜间示意。
senses.why: Before wires, the act of sending a visible sign was literal, and that older picture survives in traffic and maritime uses.
senses.whyCN: 在有电线之前，发送可见符号是字面动作，那幅更早的图景仍存于交通与航海用法中。

senses.title: A gesture of intent in business or politics
senses.titleCN: 商业或政治中的示意姿态
senses.definition: an action whose main purpose is to show intention rather than to produce an effect
senses.definitionCN: 主要目的在于表明意图、而非产生实效的动作
senses.example: The small tax cut was signaling, not policy.
senses.exampleCN: 那点减税只是示意，并非政策。
senses.why: When an act is meant to be read rather than used, the act itself becomes a signal, and the activity is called signaling.
senses.whyCN: 当一个动作是为了被解读、而非被使用，动作本身就成了信号，这种活动就叫 signaling。

senses.title: Marking in linguistics
senses.definition: the use of a grammatical or lexical marker to show a category such as politeness or number
senses.definitionCN: 用语法或词汇标记来表明礼貌、数等范畴
senses.example: Polite signaling in that language is carried by verb endings.
senses.exampleCN: 那种语言的礼貌标记由动词词尾承担。
senses.why: A formal feature can carry meaning without being a message, and linguistics borrowed the word for exactly that role.
senses.whyCN: 一个形式特征可以不构成消息却承载意义，语言学正是为这一作用借用该词。

senses.title: Abstract: any display meant to be read
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何供他人解读的展示
senses.definition: any visible or detectable display whose point is to be interpreted by an observer
senses.definitionCN: 任何目的在于被观察者解读的可见或可察觉的展示
senses.example: The empty chair at the table was signaling in its own quiet way.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上那把空椅子以一种安静的方式传递着信号。
senses.why: At its widest, signaling needs no sender with a mind: anything arranged to be read counts.
senses.whyCN: 在最宽泛的用法里，signaling 不需要有心的发送者：凡被安排以供解读之物都算。

intro.en: Signaling is signal plus the English gerund suffix -ing. Signal goes back through Old French and Medieval Latin to Latin signum 'mark, sign'. The single l in signaling is American; British writing keeps signalling.
intro.cn: signaling 是 signal 加英语动名词后缀 -ing。signal 经古法语与中世纪拉丁语追溯到拉丁 signum「记号、标志」。signaling 的单 l 拼写属美式，英式写作 signalling。

items.en: Signum meant 'identifying mark, token, military standard, omen'. Its own origin is disputed: one reconstruction connects it with a root meaning 'to follow', another with a root meaning 'to cut', and the matter is not settled.
items.cn: signum 意为「识别记号、凭信、军旗、征兆」。其自身来源有争议：一种重构把它联系到意为「跟随」的词根，另一种联系到意为「切割」的词根，至今未定。

items.en: Late Latin signalis 'used as a sign' supplied Medieval Latin signale 'a signal', the immediate source of the French and English words.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 signalis「用作记号的」给出中世纪拉丁 signale「信号」，后者是法语与英语词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French signal 'seal, imprint, sign, mark' entered English in the late fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 signal「印记、标志、记号」在 14 世纪晚期进入英语。

items.en: The noun is recorded from the late fourteenth century; the restricted sense 'an agreed sign to act' is from the 1590s.
items.cn: 该名词自 14 世纪晚期有记录；「约定俗成、据以行动的信号」这一收窄义自 16 世纪 90 年代出现。

items.en: The suffix -ing comes from Old English -ung and names an action or its result, as in building and warning.
items.cn: 后缀 -ing 来自古英语 -ung，命名动作或其结果，如 building 与 warning。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): signum's pre-Latin history has competing reconstructions, and the earliest use of signaling as a standalone noun is not fixed, so the date should be treated as approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：signum 在拉丁语之前的历史存在彼此竞争的重构；signaling 作为独立名词的最早用法也无定论，因此年代应视为约数。

note.en: Group one separates the base word, the British spelling and inflected forms that differ only in grammar; group two holds nouns that name other parts of the same exchange.
note.cn: 第一组区分词基、英式拼写与仅语法不同的屈折形式；第二组是命名同一次交换中其他部分的名词。

entries.definition: The British form with double l; identical in meaning, different only in orthography.
entries.definitionCN: 双 l 的英式形式；意义相同，仅在正字法上不同。

entries.definition: The noun and verb from which signaling is formed; it names a sign or the act of sending one.
entries.definitionCN: 构成 signaling 的名词与动词；命名符号或发送符号的动作。

entries.definition: The past tense of the verb; it reports a completed act and cannot stand as the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 动词过去式；报告已完成的动作，不能充当名词。

entries.definition: From signum via Old French: a small seal, an object that makes a mark rather than an act of sending.
entries.definitionCN: 经古法语来自 signum：小印章，是留下记号的物件，而非发送动作。

entries.definition: The whole two-way process of sharing meaning; signaling is only the sender's side.
entries.definitionCN: 共享意义的整个双向过程；signaling 只是发送者一侧。

entries.definition: Giving a prompt that triggers a response; it stresses the trigger rather than the message.
entries.definitionCN: 给出触发反应的提示；强调触发，而非消息。

entries.definition: The carrying of a signal through a medium; it says nothing about a receiver interpreting it.
entries.definitionCN: 信号通过介质传输；不涉及接收者是否解读。

entries.definition: Making visible bodily movements to convey something; one channel of signaling.
entries.definitionCN: 做出可见的身体动作来传达；是 signaling 的一个渠道。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: signal + -ing: the act of sending a sign.
normal.cn: signal + -ing：发送符号的动作。

normal.en: The family runs signal, signaling, signaler, signalize, signalling.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 signal、signaling、signaler、signalize、signalling。

normal.en: Fixed compounds: signaling pathway, cell signaling, signaling system, honest signaling.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：信号传导通路、细胞信号传导、信令系统、诚实信号。

normal.en: British writing doubles the l: signalling.
normal.cn: 英式拼写双写 l：signalling。

normal.en: The root signum also gives sign, signal, signature and signet.
normal.cn: 词根 signum 还给出 sign、signal、signature 与 signet。

abstract.en: Picture a frog's call travelling outward as rings on dark water.
abstract.cn: 想象蛙鸣像黑水面上的同心圆向外扩散。

abstract.en: Picture an empty chair arranged carefully so that everyone reads it.
abstract.cn: 想象一把被刻意摆好的空椅子，让所有人都读出意思。

abstract.en: Picture a cell answering a molecule the way a room answers a knock.
abstract.cn: 想象细胞回应一个分子，就像房间回应一次敲门。

examples.en: Chemical signaling between roots and soil microbes is under intense study.
examples.cn: 根系与土壤微生物之间的化学信号传递正被密集研究。

examples.en: Faulty signaling, not the cable, caused the outage.
examples.cn: 造成中断的是信令故障，而非电缆。

examples.en: The peacock's display is signaling aimed at a single watching female.
examples.cn: 孔雀的展示是针对唯一一位观看的雌性的信号发送。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「signal（信号）+ ing（正在进行）」——正在把信号发出去的过程 → 信号发送、信令

root: signal（拉丁 signum「记号」经中世纪拉丁 signale、古法语 signal）+ -ing（古英语 -ung，表动作）；美式单 l，英式双 l；signum 更深来源有两种竞争性重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act outward: a sign is made, then made by an animal, then by a network, then by a cell, then by a hand, then by an institution, then by a grammar, and finally by anything arranged to be read.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个向外发出的动作：先造出符号，再由动物、网络、细胞、手势、机构、语法，最后由任何被安排以供解读之物造出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sign leaving a sender and travelling until someone reads it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个符号离开发送者，一路行进，直到有人读出它。

branches.en: SENDER'S SIDE: the general act, then the biological half that excludes the receiver's response.
branches.cn: 发送者一侧：一般动作，以及排除接收者反应的生物学那一半。

branches.en: SCALED SYSTEMS: telephone control signals and molecular pathways use the same shape.
branches.cn: 不同尺度的系统：电话控制信号与分子通路共享同一形状。

branches.en: VISIBLE ORDER: lights and flags direct bodies in space.
branches.cn: 可见的秩序：灯光与旗子在空间中指挥身体。

branches.en: MADE TO BE INTERPRETED: political gestures and grammatical markers both ask to be read.
branches.cn: 为被解读而造：政治姿态与语法标记都要求被读出。

branches.en: WIDEST SCOPE: any display arranged for an observer.
branches.cn: 最宽的范围：任何为观察者安排好的展示。

intro.en: Signaling is a Latin-derived noun plus a native English suffix, a common hybrid pattern in technical vocabulary.
intro.cn: signaling 是拉丁来源名词加本族英语后缀，是术语中常见的混合模式。

latinIntro.en: Latin signum 'mark' gives sign, signal, signature and signet; the suffix -ing is native English, from Old English -ung.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 signum「记号」给出 sign、signal、signature 与 signet；后缀 -ing 属本族英语，来自古英语 -ung。

items.example: The root underlies sign and signal.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根是 sign 与 signal 的基础。

items.example: The lighthouse sends a signal every twelve seconds.
items.exampleCN: 灯塔每十二秒发出一次信号。

items.example: Building, warning and signaling all name activities.
items.exampleCN: building、warning 与 signaling 都命名活动。

items.example: Signaling precedes any response.
items.exampleCN: 信号发送先于任何回应。

items.example: British manuals print signalling.
items.exampleCN: 英国手册写作 signalling。

items.example: The signaler stood where the ships could see.
items.exampleCN: 发信号的人站在船只能看见的地方。

items.example: The victory was signalized by a bell.
items.exampleCN: 这场胜利以钟声表明。

items.example: A sign can stand without being sent.
items.exampleCN: 符号可以不经过发送而存在。

items.example: The signature is a sign made by hand.
items.exampleCN: 签名是用手做出的符号。

definition_zh: 沉积的；沉积岩的；由沉积物形成的
definition_en: relating to sediment, or made of material deposited in layers by water, wind or ice
core_image: 河谷崖壁上层层平行的岩板，像被压平的沙层一页页叠着
scene: 野外课上，学生用锤子敲开一层层平整的岩石，看到沙粒被压成了薄薄的板。 The cliff is built of sedimentary layers laid down under an ancient sea.
sceneCN: 这里 sedimentary 指「由沉积物逐层堆积形成的」（第 1 个义项：沉积成因的，尤指沉积岩）；句意为这处崖壁由古老海底逐层堆积的沉积岩构成。可辨识物件：崖壁、平行层理、地质锤、砂质岩板。

pos.zh: 沉积的；沉积成的；沉积岩的

senses.title: Relating to sediment
senses.definition: of or concerning sediment as a material
senses.definitionCN: 指与作为物质的沉积物有关的
senses.example: The sedimentary particles range from clay to coarse sand.
senses.exampleCN: 这些沉积颗粒从黏土一直到粗砂。
senses.why: The suffix -ary means 'connected with', so the adjective simply attaches the noun to whatever it describes.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ary 意为「与……相关的」，因此这个形容词只是把名词连接到它所描述的对象。

senses.title: Formed by layer-by-layer deposition
senses.definition: formed by the accumulation and consolidation of deposited material
senses.definitionCN: 指由沉积物累积并固结而成
senses.example: The cliff is built of sedimentary layers laid down under an ancient sea.
senses.exampleCN: 这处崖壁由古老海底逐层堆积的沉积岩构成。
senses.why: 'Formed by layers' is the defining trait that separates this rock class from cooled melt and from pressed schist.
senses.whyCN: 「逐层形成」是这一岩类区别于冷却熔体与受压片岩的关键特征。

senses.title: Of the rock class so formed
senses.titleCN: 属于沉积岩这一岩类的
senses.definition: of rock: belonging to the class produced by deposition, as opposed to igneous or metamorphic
senses.definitionCN: 指岩石属于沉积成因的一类，与火成岩、变质岩相对
senses.example: Sandstone and limestone are sedimentary rocks.
senses.exampleCN: 砂岩与石灰岩是沉积岩。
senses.why: Classification needs one word for the whole family, and this adjective supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 分类需要用一个词指称整个岩族，这个形容词正好承担这一职能。

senses.title: Filling a depositional basin
senses.definition: of a basin: filled with deposited material over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 指盆地长期充填沉积物质
senses.example: The sedimentary basin holds kilometres of fill.
senses.exampleCN: 这个沉积盆地充填了数千米厚的物质。
senses.why: A basin is defined by what fills it, so the adjective marks the container by its contents.
senses.whyCN: 盆地由充填它的东西来定义，因此这个形容词用内容物来标记容器。

senses.title: Showing bedding or stratification
senses.definition: of a structure: showing the layering produced by deposition
senses.definitionCN: 指构造显示出沉积造成的成层性
senses.example: Cross-bedding is a sedimentary structure.
senses.exampleCN: 交错层理是一种沉积构造。
senses.why: Visible bedding is the physical proof of deposition, hence the fixed phrase sedimentary structure.
senses.whyCN: 可见层理是沉积的物理证据，因此有 sedimentary structure（沉积构造）这一固定说法。

senses.title: Belonging to a depositional cycle
senses.definition: of a cycle: beginning with deposition and ending with exposure or uplift
senses.definitionCN: 指以沉积开始、以暴露或抬升结束的旋回
senses.example: Each sedimentary cycle ends with a gap in the record.
senses.exampleCN: 每个沉积旋回都以记录中的一次间断结束。
senses.why: A cycle is deposition followed by exposure, and the adjective marks the depositional half.
senses.whyCN: 一个旋回是先沉积后暴露，这个形容词标记的是沉积的那一半。

senses.title: Formed by chemical or biological deposition
senses.titleCN: 由化学或生物作用沉积形成的
senses.definition: of deposits: produced by precipitation or by living organisms rather than clastic settling
senses.definitionCN: 指由沉淀作用或生物作用形成，而非碎屑沉降
senses.example: The sedimentary iron ore formed by precipitation.
senses.exampleCN: 这座沉积铁矿由沉淀作用形成。
senses.why: Not all sediment is broken fragments; chemical and biological precipitation also deposit, and the adjective covers both.
senses.whyCN: 并非所有沉积物都是碎屑；化学与生物沉淀同样在沉积，这个形容词两者都涵盖。

senses.title: Of the geological record these rocks keep
senses.titleCN: 指这些岩石保存的地质记录
senses.definition: of the record: the history preserved in deposited sequences
senses.definitionCN: 指保存在沉积序列中的历史
senses.example: The sedimentary record shows three marine invasions.
senses.exampleCN: 沉积记录显示出三次海侵。
senses.why: The record is the sum of all the layers, so the adjective extends from single beds to the whole archive.
senses.whyCN: 记录是全部岩层的总和，因此这个形容词从单层扩展到整部档案。

intro.en: Sedimentary is an English adjective formed on the noun sediment, which itself goes back to Latin sedere 'to sit'.
intro.cn: sedimentary 是在名词 sediment 上构成的英语形容词，而 sediment 本身可上溯到拉丁 sedere「坐」。

items.en: Sedere 'to sit, settle' supplies the root of the whole family, and its past participle sessum underlies words such as session.
items.cn: sedere「坐、安定」提供整个词族的词根，其过去分词 sessum 支撑 session 这类词。

items.en: Sedimentum named the result of settling, and English borrowed it through French as sediment in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: sedimentum 命名沉降的结果，英语在十六世纪经法语把它借入为 sediment。

items.en: The Latin adjectival suffix -arius, through French -aire and English -ary, means 'connected with', giving sedimentary 'connected with sediment'.
items.cn: 拉丁形容词后缀 -arius 经法语 -aire 与英语 -ary，意为「与……相关的」，由此得到 sedimentary「与沉积物相关的」。

items.en: The adjective became a standard rock-class term in nineteenth-century geology, pairing with igneous and metamorphic.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十九世纪地质学中成为标准的岩类术语，与 igneous（火成的）、metamorphic（变质的）并列。

items.en: Later phrases such as sedimentary basin, sedimentary structure and sedimentary cycle extended the adjective across the whole discipline.
items.cn: 后来 sedimentary basin（沉积盆地）、sedimentary structure（沉积构造）与 sedimentary cycle（沉积旋回）等说法把这个形容词扩展到整个学科。

items.en: Not uncertain: the derivation is established. Only the precise date of the first geological use is uncertain, and the older Indo-European root *sed- is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 并非存疑：派生关系是确定的。仅首次用于地质学义的准确年代不确定，更早的印欧词根 *sed- 属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes with other roots; group two holds adjectives describing how rock is made.
note.cn: 第一组是词根不同的形近词；第二组是描写岩石成因的形容词。

entries.definition: Means given to sitting, from sedere plus -ary; it shares root and suffix with sedimentary but describes a way of life, not a rock.
entries.definitionCN: 意为久坐的，来自 sedere 加 -ary；它与 sedimentary 共享词根与后缀，却描写生活方式而非岩石。

entries.definition: Means basic or introductory, from elementum 'first principle'; the ending is the same, the root is not.
entries.definitionCN: 意为基本的、初级的，来自 elementum「基本要素」；词尾相同，词根不同。

entries.definition: Means governed by tender feeling, from sentire 'to feel'; it looks close but has no connection with settling.
entries.definitionCN: 意为受柔情支配的，来自 sentire「感觉」；外形接近，但与沉降无关。

entries.definition: Means lasting only a moment, from moment plus -ary; it shares the long ending but comes from a different noun.
entries.definitionCN: 意为只持续一瞬的，由 moment 加 -ary 构成；共享长词尾，但名词词根不同。

entries.definition: Means relating to deposition as an action; sedimentary describes the material or rock that results.
entries.definitionCN: 指与沉积这一动作相关的；sedimentary 描写由此产生的材料或岩石。

entries.definition: Means arranged in layers, from stratum 'spread-out thing'; it names the visible layering that sedimentary rock usually shows.
entries.definitionCN: 意为成层的，来自 stratum「铺开之物」；它命名沉积岩通常显示的可见层理。

entries.definition: A technical adjective for rock made of broken pieces, from Greek klastos 'broken'; it is one kind of sedimentary rock, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 指由碎屑构成的岩石，来自希腊 klastos「破碎的」；它只是沉积岩的一类，不是同义词。

entries.definition: Means deposited by flowing water, from Latin alluvio 'a washing against'; it narrows sedimentary to river action.
entries.definitionCN: 指由流水沉积的，来自拉丁 alluvio「冲积」；它把 sedimentary 收窄到河流作用。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real root, the real suffix and the real rock-class triple.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的词根、真实的后缀与真实的三大岩类。

normal.en: Sediment plus -ary: 'connected with sediment', exactly as the suffix says.
normal.cn: sediment 加 -ary：正如后缀所示，「与沉积物相关的」。

normal.en: The rock triple is igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic.
normal.cn: 三大岩类是火成岩、沉积岩、变质岩。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: sedimentary rock, sedimentary layer, sedimentary basin, sedimentary structure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：沉积岩、沉积层、沉积盆地、沉积构造。

normal.en: The family climbs sediment, sedimentary, sedimentation, sedimentology.
normal.cn: 词族按 sediment、sedimentary、sedimentation、sedimentology 逐级展开。

normal.en: Layering is the giveaway: sedimentary rock comes in sheets, not in one cooled mass.
normal.cn: 成层是它的标志：沉积岩成片状，而不是一整块冷却的熔体。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of newspapers pressed into one hard board.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠报纸被压成一块硬板。

abstract.en: Picture a beach writing its own autobiography grain by grain.
abstract.cn: 想象一片海滩一粒一粒地写自传。

abstract.en: Picture time stored as thickness instead of as numbers.
abstract.cn: 想象时间以厚度而不是数字来储存。

examples.en: The sedimentary sequence records a shallow sea that lasted a million years.
examples.cn: 这套沉积序列记录了一片存在百万年的浅海。

examples.en: Sedimentary basins along the margin trap oil and gas.
examples.cn: 边缘的沉积盆地圈闭了石油与天然气。

examples.en: A sedimentary deposit of gypsum formed as the lake dried.
examples.cn: 湖泊干涸时形成了石膏沉积矿床。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞底（sedi）门（ment）特瑞（ary）」——塞在底下一层层压成的 → 沉积的

root: 拉丁 sedere「坐、安定」+ -mentum（结果）→ sedimentum，再加 -arius「与……相关的」→ sedimentary；词根与沉积作用同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective around one process: material settles, hardens, shows layers, fills basins and finally becomes a readable record of time.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一个形容词围绕同一个过程展开：物质沉降、固结、显出层理、充填盆地，最后成为可解读的时间记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: flat sheets of hardened sand stacked like pages in a book.
core.cn: 核心意象：压硬的砂层像书页一样平叠着。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND PROCESS: the adjective first names the stuff and then the way it was laid down.
branches.cn: 材料与过程：这个形容词先命名物质，再命名堆积方式。

branches.en: THE ROCK CLASS: one of the three great families, defined by deposition rather than by heat or pressure.
branches.cn: 岩类：三大岩族之一，以沉积而非热或压力来定义。

branches.en: SPACE AND TIME: a basin fills through cycles, each closing with a gap.
branches.cn: 空间与时间：盆地经由旋回充填，每个旋回以一次间断收尾。

branches.en: STRUCTURES AND CHEMISTRY: bedding shows the process, and precipitation adds a non-clastic route.
branches.cn: 构造与化学：层理显示过程，沉淀作用补充了非碎屑的途径。

branches.en: THE RECORD: what was deposited becomes the archive that geologists read.
branches.cn: 记录：沉积下来的东西成为地质学家解读的档案。

intro.en: Sedimentary combines the noun sediment with the Latin-derived suffix -ary, and the whole family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: sedimentary 把名词 sediment 与拉丁来源的后缀 -ary 组合起来，整个词族都可按语素读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin sedere 'to sit' and -mentum 'result' give sediment; -arius 'connected with' gives the adjective, as in elementary and military.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sedere「坐」与 -mentum「结果」构成 sediment；-arius「与……相关的」构成该形容词，如 elementary 与 military。

items.example: The root carries the idea of coming to rest.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带有归于静止的意思。

items.example: Sediment is what has settled.
items.exampleCN: 沉积物就是已经沉下来的东西。

items.example: Fine sediment filled the jar.
items.exampleCN: 细沉积物灌满了瓶子。

items.example: Military means connected with soldiers.
items.exampleCN: military 意为与士兵相关的。

items.example: The cliff is sedimentary.
items.exampleCN: 这处崖壁是沉积成因的。

items.example: Sedimentation buried the reef.
items.exampleCN: 沉积作用埋住了礁体。

items.example: Sedimentology reads ancient currents.
items.exampleCN: 沉积学解读古水流。

items.example: The sedimentologist sampled the bed.
items.exampleCN: 沉积学家在河床上取样。

definition_zh: 可到达的；可联系上的；可实现的；可够到的
definition_en: possible to arrive at, contact or achieve
core_image: 地图上标着一条短路径，尽头就在手心够得到的地方
scene: 向导说山顶的营地在两小时脚程之内，天黑前一定到得了。 The guide said the camp on the ridge was reachable in two hours before dark.
sceneCN: 这里 reachable 指可到达的（第 1 个义项：能够走到）；句意为向导说山顶的营地在两小时脚程之内，天黑前一定到得了。

pos.zh: 可到达的；可联系上的；可实现的

senses.title: Able to be arrived at
senses.definition: possible to arrive at, especially after a known distance or route
senses.definitionCN: 可以抵达的，尤指经过一段已知的距离或路线之后
senses.example: The guide said the camp on the ridge was reachable in two hours before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 向导说山顶的营地在两小时脚程之内，天黑前一定到得了。
senses.why: This is the map sense: reachable places are measured in roads and hours.
senses.whyCN: 这是地图上的一层：可达的地方用道路和小时来量。

senses.title: Able to be contacted
senses.definition: possible to get in touch with, by phone, message or another channel
senses.definitionCN: 可以通过电话、讯息或其他渠道联系到的
senses.example: The number was reachable only during office hours.
senses.exampleCN: 那个号码只在办公时间能打通。
senses.why: Contact replaces geography here: a signal can make a person reachable in an instant.
senses.whyCN: 这一层里联系取代了地理：一个信号就能让人瞬间可达。

senses.title: Able to be achieved
senses.definition: possible to achieve with the means and the time actually available
senses.definitionCN: 用实际可用的手段与时间能够做到的
senses.example: The first version of the product had to be reachable in three months.
senses.exampleCN: 产品的第一个版本必须在三个月内做出来。
senses.why: The word moves from distance to effort and asks what a given team can really finish.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从距离移到力气与时间，问的是一支具体的团队究竟能做完什么。

intro.en: Reachable joins reach, from Old English reccan, 'to stretch out', with -able.
intro.cn: reachable 把 reach（古英语 reccan，伸手）与 -able 组合在一起。

items.en: Reccan meant to stretch out a hand.
items.cn: reccan 意为伸出手。

items.en: Reach grew to mean arrive at or attain.
items.cn: reach 长成「抵达」或「达到」。

items.en: The ending marks what can be done.
items.cn: 词尾标记「能够被做到」。

items.en: Steam travel popularised reachable places.
items.cn: 蒸汽交通让「可达的地方」流行起来。

items.en: Today it also describes goals and budgets.
items.cn: 今天它也描述目标与预算。

note.en: The look-alike group is the reach- family; the near-meaning group separates accessible, attainable, available and approachable.
note.cn: 形近组是 reach 词族；近义组把「可进入的」「可达到的」「可获得的」「易接近的」分开。

entries.definition: to arrive at or stretch to.
entries.definitionCN: 抵达或伸手够到。

entries.definition: impossible to arrive at.
entries.definitionCN: 无法到达的。

entries.definition: in a reachable way.
entries.definitionCN: 以可达的方式。

entries.definition: applying to past events.
entries.definitionCN: 适用于过去事件的。

entries.definition: able to be entered or used.
entries.definitionCN: 可以进入或使用的。

entries.definition: able to be achieved.
entries.definitionCN: 可以达到的。

entries.definition: ready to be used or obtained.
entries.definitionCN: 可以使用或获得的。

entries.definition: easy to speak to.
entries.definitionCN: 容易交谈的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a short path ending inside the hand's range.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一条短路径，尽头就在手能够到的范围」的画面。

normal.en: Reachable is reach plus able: a hand can get there.
normal.cn: reachable 是 reach 加 able：一只手能到那里。

normal.en: Picture a map with a dotted line short enough to walk.
normal.cn: 想象地图上一条短到可以走完的虚线。

normal.en: Say REE-chuh-bl; it sounds like a door that opens.
normal.cn: 读 REE-chuh-bl，听起来像一扇会开的门。

normal.en: The word covers roads, signals, goals and budgets.
normal.cn: 这个词覆盖道路、信号、目标和预算。

normal.en: Ask reachable for whom: a fit walker, a caller, a team, a grant?
normal.cn: 问对谁可达：健步的人、打电话的人、团队，还是一笔拨款？

abstract.en: Reachable is a map word that became a planning word.
abstract.cn: reachable 是一个地图词，后来成了计划词。

abstract.en: It measures the gap between desire and means without naming either.
abstract.cn: 它量的是欲望与手段之间的缝隙，却不点名任何一方。

abstract.en: What is reachable is not always what is worth reaching.
abstract.cn: 可达的，并不总是值得抵达的。

examples.en: The number was reachable only during office hours.
examples.cn: 那个号码只在办公时间能打通。

examples.en: The first version of the product had to be reachable in three months.
examples.cn: 产品的第一个版本必须在三个月内做出来。

examples.en: The chair proposed a smaller package that was actually reachable.
examples.cn: 主席提出了一个更小、实际可达成的方案。

dict_mnemonic.text: reach（伸手够到）+ able（能）→ 能够到的。

root: 古英语 reccan（伸出手）+ -able

sensesIntro.en: Reachable has three senses: a place you can arrive at, a person you can contact, and a result you can actually achieve.
sensesIntro.cn: reachable 有三层：能抵达的地方、能联系上的人、真正能做到的结果。

core.en: A PATH ENDING IN THE HAND
core.cn: 止于手心的路径

branches.en: A route and a measured number of hours.
branches.cn: 一条路线与量过的若干小时。

branches.en: A signal that finds a person.
branches.cn: 找到某人的一个信号。

branches.en: A target within the means at hand.
branches.cn: 手头手段之内的目标。

branches.en: Distance turned into effort and time.
branches.cn: 距离变成力气与时间。

branches.en: Reachable by phone, reachable on budget.
branches.cn: 电话可及，预算可及。

intro.en: The reach- family is about extending: reach, reachable, unreachable and reachably all describe how far an arm or a plan can go.
intro.cn: reach 词族讲的是伸展：reach、reachable、unreachable、reachably 都描述手臂或计划能走多远。

latinIntro.en: Old English reccan gives the verb; the -able ending came through French from Latin -abilis, meaning fit to be.
latinIntro.cn: 古英语 reccan 提供动词；-able 词尾经法语来自拉丁语 -abilis，意为「可以被……的」。

items.example: A reachable goal.
items.exampleCN: 一个可达成的目标。

items.example: Reachably close.
items.exampleCN: 近得够得到。

items.example: Its reachableness helped.
items.exampleCN: 它的可达性帮了忙。

items.example: Reach the shore.
items.exampleCN: 到达岸边。

items.example: They reached the camp.
items.exampleCN: 他们到达了营地。

items.example: A reaching arm.
items.exampleCN: 一只伸出的手臂。

items.example: An unreachable island.
items.exampleCN: 一座无法到达的岛。

items.example: He overreached.
items.exampleCN: 他做得过头了。

latinEntries.meaning: to stretch out in Old English

definition_zh: 原住民族；世代生活在某地、先于外来定居者的族群；国际法意义上拥有独特制度与土地联系的人群
definition_en: peoples who have lived in a territory since before later settlers arrived and who keep distinct institutions and ties to the land
core_image: 海岸边的岩画上刻着潮水的刻度，讲解的人说这些刻度比任何航海图都早
scene: 海岸的岩壁上刻着潮水涨落的刻度，带队的人说这些刻度比任何航海图都早。 The indigenous people of the coast have mapped the tides for centuries.
sceneCN: 这里 indigenous people 指世代生活在某地、先于外来定居者的族群（第 1 个义项：先于定居者的人群）；句意为海岸的原住民族已经为潮水作图数百年。

pos.zh: 原住民族；土著居民（复数，指某一地区的原住人群）
（国际法）原住民族（作为一个拥有集体权利的类别）

forms.label: 单数（指一个民族或一个人）

derivatives.zh: 原产的；土著的（由拉丁 indigena「本地出生」进入，核心是「生于其地」，是本词组的基础形容词）
原住民个体（由基础形容词的词干加表人的词尾而来，由性质转指人）
原住民性（由基础名词加表抽象属性的名词后缀而来，由人转指抽象属性）
人群；民族（经古法语来自拉丁 populus「人民」，由「一群人」转指「一个民族」）
诸民族（由「人群」一词的复数形式而来，用于区分多个有名称的人群）

senses.title: Peoples before settlers
senses.definition: communities living in a territory before later arrivals settled there
senses.definitionCN: 在后来者定居之前就生活在某片土地上的共同体
senses.example: The indigenous people of the valley were there long before the road.
senses.exampleCN: 山谷里的原住民族早在公路出现之前就在那里。
senses.why: Indigenous means born in the place; the phrase names priority in time, not a stage of development.
senses.whyCN: 前一个词意为生于其地；这个词组命名时间上的在先，而非发展阶段。

senses.title: A category in international law
senses.definition: peoples recognised as holding collective rights to land, culture and self-government
senses.definitionCN: 被承认对土地、文化与自治拥有集体权利的人群
senses.example: The declaration on the rights of indigenous people was adopted in 2007.
senses.exampleCN: 《原住民族权利宣言》于二零零七年获得通过。
senses.why: Law needs a defined subject; this sense turns a historical description into a holder of rights.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要一个被界定的主体；这个义项把历史描述变成权利持有人。

senses.title: Distinct institutions
senses.definition: a people keeping its own language, law, medicine and forms of decision
senses.definitionCN: 保有自身语言、法律、医药与决策方式的人群
senses.example: The indigenous people settled disputes through their own councils.
senses.exampleCN: 这个原住民族通过自己的议事会解决纠纷。
senses.why: The category rests on difference that is institutional, not merely decorative: language and law must be maintained.
senses.whyCN: 这一类别建立在制度性的差异之上，而非装饰性差异：语言与法律必须被维持。

senses.title: First peoples of a region
senses.definition: the earliest known inhabitants of a particular land, often named by their own word for themselves
senses.definitionCN: 某一土地上已知最早的居民，常以其自称来命名
senses.example: The museum now names the indigenous people in their own language.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆现在用他们自己的语言称呼这支原住民族。
senses.why: Being first is local; the phrase can name one specific people in one specific landscape.
senses.whyCN: 「在先」是地方性的；这个词组可以命名某一片具体土地上的某一具体人群。

senses.title: Ties to land
senses.definition: a relationship to territory expressed through practice, story and seasonal use rather than a deed
senses.definitionCN: 通过实践、故事与季节性生活表达的土地关系，而非靠一纸地契
senses.example: For the indigenous people, the river is a relative, not a resource.
senses.exampleCN: 对这个原住民族来说，河流是亲属，不是资源。
senses.why: Land is not only property; this sense names a relation that law often struggles to translate.
senses.whyCN: 土地不只是财产；这个义项命名一种法律常难以转译的关系。

senses.title: Survivors of colonisation
senses.definition: peoples whose institutions and populations survived invasion, mission and resettlement
senses.definitionCN: 其制度与人口在入侵、传教与重新安置之后仍然存活的人群
senses.example: The indigenous people lost most of the island but kept the language.
senses.exampleCN: 这个原住民族失去了大部分岛屿，却保住了语言。
senses.why: The modern category is formed by loss; colonisation is the shared historical experience that gave it meaning.
senses.whyCN: 现代类别由失去所塑造；殖民是赋予它意义的共同历史经验。

senses.title: A collective in statistics and activism
senses.definition: an aggregate used by agencies and movements to speak of many distinct peoples at once
senses.definitionCN: 机构与运动用来同时指称许多不同民族的集合
senses.example: The census counted indigenous people in eight hundred villages.
senses.exampleCN: 普查清点了八百个村庄里的原住民族。
senses.why: Politics needs a large number; the phrase gathers very different peoples under one heading for counting and campaigning.
senses.whyCN: 政治需要一个大的数字；这个词组把非常不同的民族收进一个名目下，以便清点与动员。

senses.title: Self-naming versus outside label
senses.definition: the tension between a people's own name and the generic label applied from outside
senses.definitionCN: 一个民族自己的名称与外部施加的概括标签之间的张力
senses.example: The indigenous people prefer their own name to the official term.
senses.exampleCN: 这个原住民族更喜欢自己的名称，而非官方术语。
senses.why: Naming is power; the phrase can be correct in law and still be rejected by the people it describes.
senses.whyCN: 命名就是权力；这个词组在法律上可以正确，却仍可能被它所描述的人拒绝。

intro.en: Indigenous comes from Latin indigena 'native, born in the land', from indu 'in' plus gignere 'to beget'. People comes through Old French from Latin populus 'people', a word of uncertain origin. The English phrase is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: indigenous 来自拉丁 indigena「本地的、生于此地的」，由 indu「在内」加 gignere「生育」构成。people 经古法语来自拉丁 populus「人民」，其来源不确定。这个英语词组是现代的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Indigena meant 'a native, one born in a place', formed with indu, an old form of in, and the root gen- 'be born'. The adjective indigenus is parallel.
items.cn: indigena 意为「本地人、生于此地者」，由 indu（in 的旧形式）与表示「出生」的词根 gen- 构成。形容词 indigenus 与之并行。

items.en: Gignere 'to beget, bring forth' belongs to the gen- family that also gives genus, generate and native.
items.cn: gignere「生育、产生」属于 gen- 词族，该词族还给出 genus、generate 与 native。

items.en: Populus 'people' is the source of English people through Old French. Its own origin is uncertain; a link with Etruscan has been suggested but not proved.
items.cn: populus「人民」经古法语成为英语 people 的来源。它自身的来源不确定；有人提出与伊特鲁里亚语有关，但未获证明。

items.en: English indigenous appears in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries meaning 'native to a place', first of plants and animals as well as people.
items.cn: 英语 indigenous 在十六、十七世纪出现，意为「原产于某地」，最初既用于人，也用于动植物。

items.en: Indigenous people became a standard term of law and advocacy in the late twentieth century, especially with the 2007 UN declaration.
items.cn: indigenous people 在二十世纪后期成为法律与倡议的标准术语，尤其是在二零零七年联合国宣言之后。

items.en: Source uncertain: the origin of populus is unresolved; the deeper history of the gen- root is reconstructed; and the plural form peoples is used in law to mark distinct nations rather than one mass.
items.cn: 来源不确定：populus 的来源未有定论；gen- 词根更早的历史属重构形式；法律文本用复数 peoples 来标记不同民族，而非一整团人。

note.en: Group one separates words that look or sound close; group two holds alternative labels for original inhabitants.
note.cn: 第一组区分形近或音近的词；第二组是「原住居民」的其他称呼。

entries.definition: Poor, needy. It looks almost identical but comes from a different Latin word meaning 'lacking'.
entries.definitionCN: 贫穷的、匮乏的。拼写几乎相同，却来自另一个意为「缺少」的拉丁词。

entries.definition: A deep blue dye. It shares the opening letters but has nothing to do with birth or land.
entries.definitionCN: 一种深蓝色染料。开头字母相同，却与出生或土地无关。

entries.definition: Native to a place; alone it can describe a plant, a language or a species, not only people.
entries.definitionCN: 原产于某地的；单用时可形容植物、语言或物种，不只指人。

entries.definition: Born in a place; it is broader and can describe anyone born locally, not only original peoples.
entries.definitionCN: 生于某地的；范围更宽，可以指任何本地出生的人，而不只是原住民族。

entries.definition: A term used especially in Canada and Australia; it stresses priority in time without the Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 尤其在加拿大与澳大利亚使用的说法；强调时间上的在先，而不带拉丁词根。

entries.definition: Original inhabitants of a land, from Latin ab origine 'from the beginning'; in some countries it is the official term.
entries.definitionCN: 某地的原住居民，来自拉丁「从起初」；在有些国家它是官方术语。

entries.definition: The locally born residents of an area; it can include settlers' descendants and is not a legal category.
entries.definitionCN: 某地本地出生的居民；可以包括定居者的后代，且不是法律类别。

entries.definition: Peoples organised in tribes; it describes a social form rather than a historical or legal status.
entries.definitionCN: 以部落组织的人群；它描述社会形式，而非历史或法律地位。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin parts, real legal terms and real alternative labels.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁构件、真实的法律术语与真实的替代称呼。

normal.en: Indigenous means born inside the land: the old preposition for 'in' plus the root for birth.
normal.cn: indigenous 意为生在这片土地之内：表示「在内」的旧介词加「出生」词根。

normal.en: The same birth root gives native and nation, so indigenous, native and nation are cousins.
normal.cn: 同一个「出生」词根给出 native 与 nation，所以 indigenous、native、nation 是表亲。

normal.en: Keep indigent apart: it means needy, not native.
normal.cn: 把 indigent 分开：它意为贫穷，而不是原产。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the legal field: indigenous people's rights, indigenous people and local communities.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出法律领域：原住民族权利、原住民族与当地社区。

normal.en: In law, peoples is plural to mark distinct nations rather than one undifferentiated mass.
normal.cn: 在法律文本中，peoples 用复数来标记不同民族，而非一整团没有区分的人。

abstract.en: Picture a rock covered in tide marks older than any chart.
abstract.cn: 想象一块岩石，上面刻着比任何航海图都古老的潮位记号。

abstract.en: Picture a deed that cannot describe a river, because the river is a relative.
abstract.cn: 想象一纸地契无法描述一条河，因为那条河是亲属。

abstract.en: Picture a name chosen by the people and a label chosen by the office.
abstract.cn: 想象一个由人群自己选定的名字，和一个由机关选定的标签。

examples.en: The indigenous people manage the forest with fire, not with fences.
examples.cn: 这个原住民族用火管理森林，而不是用围栏。

examples.en: Treaties with indigenous people were signed and then ignored.
examples.cn: 与原住民族签订的条约被签下，随后被无视。

examples.en: The school invites indigenous people to teach the local language.
examples.cn: 学校邀请原住民族来教授当地语言。

dict_mnemonic.text: indigena（生在此地）+ people（人群）＝ 生在这片土地上的人；记「先来的人，后来的路」。

root: indigenous 源自拉丁 indigena「本地出生者」，由 indu「在内」加 gignere「生育」构成，词根 gen- 的更早形式属重构；people 经古法语来自拉丁 populus「人民」，populus 的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from priority in time to legal category, distinct institutions, local first peoples, land ties, colonial survival, statistical aggregation and the politics of naming.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从时间上的在先，移到法律类别、独特制度、地方先住民、土地联系、殖民后的存续、统计集合与命名政治。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: tide marks cut into rock long before the first chart was drawn.
core.cn: 核心意象：在最早的航海图出现之前，潮位记号就已刻进岩石。

branches.en: PRIORITY IN PLACE: a people already there, and one specific people in one landscape.
branches.cn: 地方上的在先：一群早已在那里的人，以及某片土地上的某一具体人群。

branches.en: LOSS BECOMES LAW: colonial survival produces the legal subject that claims rights.
branches.cn: 失去变成法律：殖民后的存续产生出主张权利的法律主体。

branches.en: KEPT INSTITUTIONS: language, law and councils carry the difference.
branches.cn: 被保住的制度：语言、法律与议事会承载着差异。

branches.en: THE RIVER AS RELATIVE: land is a relation, not only a deed.
branches.cn: 河流即亲属：土地是一种关系，不只是地契。

branches.en: COUNTED AND NAMED: agencies gather many peoples into one figure, while the peoples choose their own names.
branches.cn: 被计数与被命名：机构把许多民族汇成一个数字，而各民族选择自己的名称。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin adjective of local birth to a Latin noun for a people; both halves are learned borrowings.
intro.cn: 这个词组把表示「本地出生」的拉丁形容词与表示「人民」的拉丁名词结合起来，两半都是学术借词。

latinIntro.en: Indigena and gignere supply the first element; populus, through Old French, supplies the second. Populus has no proven Latin derivation.
latinIntro.cn: indigena 与 gignere 提供前一成分；populus 经古法语提供后一成分。populus 没有已证实的拉丁派生来源。

items.example: The palm is indigenous to the island.
items.exampleCN: 这种棕榈原产于该岛。

items.example: The law uses indigene in its French text.
items.exampleCN: 该法律的法语文本使用 indigene 一词。

items.example: Indigeneity is recognised by institutions as well as by descent.
items.exampleCN: 原住民性既由制度承认，也由世系确认。

items.example: She is a native speaker of the language.
items.exampleCN: 她是这门语言的母语者。

items.example: The nation includes many peoples.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家包含许多民族。

items.structure: populus (Latin n.) via Old French people
items.meaning: a body of persons; a nation
items.example: The people of the coast keep the old calendar.
items.exampleCN: 海岸的人们保留着旧历法。

items.meaningCN: 诸民族；多个有名称的人群
items.example: The charter speaks of peoples, not populations.
items.exampleCN: 该宪章说的是诸民族，而不是人口。

items.meaning: the people counted in a place
items.meaningCN: 人口；某地被清点的人群
items.example: The population includes both groups.
items.exampleCN: 人口中包括这两个群体。

items.example: The song became popular far from home.
items.exampleCN: 这首歌在远方变得流行。

latinEntries.structure: indu (Latin preposition, old form of in)

definition_zh: 多叶的；由叶组成的；叶菜类的；（街区）绿树成荫的
definition_en: having many leaves, made of leaves, or consisting mainly of edible leaves
core_image: 一根枝条叶片密到看不见茎，整条街被这层绿盖住
scene: 老城南边那条街两侧的梧桐把阳光筛成碎斑，中介带人看房时总要先提这一点。 A leafy street like that sells houses faster than a bare one.
sceneCN: 这里 leafy 是「（街区）树木成荫的」（第 5 个义项：用多叶来形容一个地方绿荫浓密）；句意：那样绿树成荫的街道，房子卖得比光秃秃的街道快。

pos.zh: 多叶的；枝叶茂密的
由叶子组成的；叶制的
叶菜类的；以叶片为食用部分的
绿树成荫的（街道、郊区）

senses.title: Full of leaves
senses.definition: having many leaves; covered with leaves
senses.definitionCN: 多叶的；枝叶茂密的
senses.example: A leafy branch hung over the path.
senses.exampleCN: 一根多叶的枝条悬在小路上。
senses.why: The suffix -y in English adjectives means 'having the quality of', so leafy is simply leaf plus abundance.
senses.whyCN: 英语形容词后缀 -y 表示「具有……的性质」，leafy 就是叶加上「多」这一层。

senses.title: Made of leaves
senses.definition: made of leaves or built from leaf material
senses.definitionCN: 由叶子制成的
senses.example: The nest is a leafy ball above the water.
senses.exampleCN: 巢是水面上方一个用叶子团成的球。
senses.why: Once a leaf stops being a living organ and becomes a material, the same adjective names the substance.
senses.whyCN: 一旦叶片不再是活器官而变成材料，同一个形容词就用来指这种材料。

senses.title: Leaf vegetables
senses.titleCN: 叶菜的：以叶片为食用部分
senses.definition: consisting mainly of edible leaves, as a class of vegetables
senses.definitionCN: 叶菜类的；以叶为食的
senses.example: Leafy greens lose vitamins if boiled too long.
senses.exampleCN: 叶菜煮得太久会损失维生素。
senses.why: Shops sort vegetables by the part that gets eaten; leafy names the group whose edible part is the leaf.
senses.whyCN: 商店按食用部位给蔬菜分堆；leafy 指可食部分为叶片的那一堆。

senses.title: Canopy layer
senses.definition: of or forming a dense layer of leaves in a canopy
senses.definitionCN: 叶层厚密的；构成林冠叶层的
senses.example: The leafy canopy kept the ground cool.
senses.exampleCN: 茂密的树冠让地面保持凉爽。
senses.why: In ecology the leaves of a stand act as one layer, and leafy describes how thick that layer is.
senses.whyCN: 在生态学里，一片林木的叶子被当作一个层，leafy 描述这个层有多厚。

senses.title: Leafy neighbourhood
senses.titleCN: 绿荫的：街道两侧树木成行
senses.definition: having many trees and much greenery, used of streets and suburbs
senses.definitionCN: 绿树成荫的（街道、郊区）
senses.example: They bought a house in a leafy suburb.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在绿树成荫的郊区买了房子。
senses.why: Estate agents borrow the plant word to sell shade, quiet and clean air in a single adjective.
senses.whyCN: 房产中介借这个植物词，用一个形容词同时卖绿荫、安静与干净的空气。

senses.title: Vegetative shoot
senses.titleCN: 营养枝的：只长叶不开花
senses.definition: producing leaves rather than flowers or fruit
senses.definitionCN: 营养生长的；长叶而不开花的
senses.example: A leafy shoot grew from the cut stem.
senses.exampleCN: 一根营养枝从剪口处长了出来。
senses.why: Botany divides a shoot into leafy and flowering kinds; here leafy marks the phase, not the quantity.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把枝条分成营养枝与花枝；这里的 leafy 标的是阶段，不是数量。

senses.title: Whole-leaf tea
senses.definition: made of whole, unbroken leaves, used of tea
senses.definitionCN: 全叶的（茶叶未切碎）
senses.example: The tin holds a leafy tea from the high hills.
senses.exampleCN: 罐里装的是高山产的全叶茶。
senses.why: Tea grading counts how much leaf stays whole, so leafy turns into a quality label.
senses.whyCN: 茶叶分级看叶片保留得多完整，leafy 于是成了品质标签。

senses.title: Leaf-green
