senses.titleCN: 叶绿的：像叶子那样的颜色
senses.definition: of a colour like that of leaves
senses.definitionCN: 叶绿色的
senses.example: She painted the wall a leafy green.
senses.exampleCN: 她把墙刷成了叶绿色。
senses.why: Colour words often come from the object: leafy names the shade a leaf shows.
senses.whyCN: 颜色词常取自物体：leafy 指叶子呈现的那种色调。

senses.title: Leaf ornament
senses.titleCN: 叶饰的：建筑上刻成叶形
senses.definition: decorated with leaf-shaped forms, used of architecture
senses.definitionCN: 叶饰的（建筑装饰）
senses.example: The capital carries a leafy pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 柱头上有叶形花纹。
senses.why: Carvers copied leaves, and the adjective moved from the plant to the stone copy.
senses.whyCN: 雕刻匠照着叶子刻，形容词就从植物移到了石头的复制品上。

intro.en: Leafy is simply the native noun leaf plus the adjective suffix -y. The root is Germanic; the earliest date for the adjective is only approximate.
intro.cn: leafy 就是本族名词 leaf 加形容词后缀 -y。词根属日耳曼语；这个形容词的首见年代只是约数。

items.en: Old English leaf meant 'leaf' and also 'sheet of paper'; the noun has been in the language since the earliest records.
items.cn: 古英语 leaf 既指「叶」也指「纸页」，这个名词从最早的文献起就在英语里。

items.en: The Germanic form laub is attested in German Laub 'foliage' and in other Germanic languages, so the root itself is not in doubt.
items.cn: 日耳曼形式 laub 有德语 Laub「叶丛」等书证，词根本身并无疑问。

items.en: The adjective suffix -y, from Old English -ig, means 'having the quality of' and is the same suffix as in sandy, salty and rainy.
items.cn: 形容词后缀 -y 来自古英语 -ig，意为「具有……性质」，与 sandy、salty、rainy 里的后缀相同。

items.en: The adjective leafy appears in Middle English; the exact first written example is uncertain, since the form was common in dialect.
items.cn: 形容词 leafy 在中古英语时期已经出现；确切的首次书面用例不确定，因为该形式在方言中很常见。

items.en: Victorian gardening and later estate advertising extended leafy from plants to whole streets, and tea grading extended it to whole-leaf produce.
items.cn: 维多利亚时代的园艺以及后来的房产广告，把 leafy 从植物扩展到整条街道；茶叶分级又把它扩展到全叶产品。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the root is securely Germanic, but any Indo-European ancestor offered for it is a reconstruction, and the link to Latin folium is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：词根确属日耳曼语，但凡为它给出的印欧祖形都是重构形式，与拉丁 folium 的联系只是假说。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes that share no root from the base word itself; group two holds words for thick green growth.
note.cn: 第一组区分词根无关的外形相近词与基础词本身；第二组列出表示浓密绿意的词。

entries.definition: The noun behind the adjective; both have a long vowel, but leafy adds a final syllable.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词背后的名词；两者元音都长，但 leafy 多一个音节。

entries.definition: From leak, probably a Germanic word for 'drip'; nothing to do with plants.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 leak，大概是日耳曼语中表示「滴漏」的词，与植物无关。

entries.definition: From Old English lif 'existence'; the vowel is /aɪ/ and the spelling has no a.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古英语 lif「生命」；元音是 /aɪ/，拼写里没有 a。

entries.definition: Leaf plus the privative -less: without leaves, the exact opposite of leafy.
entries.definitionCN: leaf 加否定后缀 -less：无叶的，正好与 leafy 相反。

entries.definition: Having thick, healthy growth, often of grass; leafy counts leaves, lush judges moisture.
entries.definitionCN: 指草木厚密、长势好，多用于草；leafy 数叶子，lush 判断水分是否充足。

entries.definition: Covered with green vegetation; a bookish word for the same look.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖着绿色植被；是形容同一种景象的书面词。

entries.definition: Having many branches close together; leafy is about leaves, bushy about the branching.
entries.definitionCN: 指枝条多而密；leafy 讲叶子，bushy 讲分枝。

entries.definition: The leaves of a plant taken as one mass; leafy says that mass is thick.
entries.definitionCN: 把一株植物的叶子当作一团；leafy 说这一团很厚。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix and the real family, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实的后缀与真实的词族，不编顺口溜。

normal.en: leaf + -y, the same suffix as in sandy and salty: full of what the noun names.
normal.cn: leaf 加 -y，与 sandy、salty 同一种后缀：充满名词所指的东西。

normal.en: The family: leaf, leaflet, leafless, leafage, leafed.
normal.cn: 同族：leaf、leaflet、leafless、leafage、leafed。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: leafy green, leafy suburb, leafy canopy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：绿叶菜、绿荫郊区、茂密树冠。

normal.en: Foliage is the mass; leafy says the mass is thick.
normal.cn: foliage 是那一团叶子；leafy 说这一团很厚。

normal.en: A supermarket shelf says leafy greens; an estate agent's window says leafy street.
normal.cn: 超市货架写的是叶菜，房产中介的橱窗写的是绿荫街道。

abstract.en: Picture a wall so covered in ivy that no brick shows.
abstract.cn: 想象一面被常春藤盖满、看不见砖的墙。

abstract.en: Picture a street where the trees meet overhead and the pavement is in shadow at noon.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街，树冠在头顶合拢，正午路面仍在阴影里。

abstract.en: Picture one word that turns a plant part into a description of a whole neighbourhood.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词，把一个植物器官变成对整个街区的描述。

examples.en: A leafy branch hung over the path.
examples.cn: 一根多叶的枝条悬在小路上。

examples.en: They bought a house in a leafy suburb.
examples.cn: 他们在绿树成荫的郊区买了房子。

examples.en: Leafy greens lose vitamins if boiled too long.
examples.cn: 叶菜煮得太久会损失维生素。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「叶（leaf）加衣（y）」——给街道披上一层叶衣，就成了绿树成荫

root: 古英语 leaf「叶、纸页」＋形容词后缀 -y「充满……的」；日耳曼语 laub 有德语 Laub 等同族书证。更早的印欧形式属重构；与拉丁 folium 的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses spread outward from one idea: many leaves, then leaves as material, as food, as a layer, as shade, as a stage, as a grade, as a colour and as an ornament.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从一个意思向外铺开：叶子多，然后叶子成了材料、成了食物、成了一层覆盖、成了绿荫、成了生长阶段、成了等级、成了颜色、成了装饰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surface so covered in leaves that the stem disappears.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个被叶子盖住、连茎都看不见的表面。

branches.en: ABUNDANCE: the suffix first says that leaves are present in quantity, then that they are the substance.
branches.cn: 多：后缀先说叶子数量多，再说叶子就是材料本身。

branches.en: FOOD: what is eaten is sorted by the plant part, and grades follow the same part.
branches.cn: 食物：可食部分决定分类，等级也按同一部位划分。

branches.en: LAYER: leaves of a stand or a shoot form one working layer in ecology and in botany.
branches.cn: 层：一片林木或一根枝条的叶子，在生态学与植物学里都构成一个工作层。

branches.en: PLACE: the layer becomes the character of a street, and the word sells shade.
branches.cn: 地点：这一层变成街道的性格，这个词开始卖绿荫。

branches.en: FORM: once leaves are a shape rather than a thing, they become a colour and a carved pattern.
branches.cn: 形状：当叶子不再是一样东西而是一个形状，它就变成一种颜色和一种雕花。

intro.en: Leafy is a native Germanic word with native suffixes; it has no Latin affixes and no reliable Latin cognate.
intro.cn: leafy 是日耳曼本族词，配本族后缀；它没有拉丁词缀，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

latinIntro.en: Old English leaf and Germanic laub supply the root; -y, -let, -less and -age are suffixes attached to it, and no Latin cognate is established.
latinIntro.cn: 古英语 leaf 与日耳曼 laub 提供词根；-y、-let、-less、-age 是加在其上的后缀，拉丁同族词未获证实。

items.example: The word is native, not borrowed.
items.exampleCN: 这个词是本族词，不是借词。

items.example: German Laub preserves the old form.
items.exampleCN: 德语 Laub 保留了古老形式。

items.example: It makes leafy from leaf.
items.exampleCN: 它把 leaf 变成 leafy。

items.example: A leafy hedge screened the door.
items.exampleCN: 多叶的树篱挡住了门。

items.example: It makes leaflet, a small leaf.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 leaflet，即小叶。

items.meaning: a small leaf; a printed sheet
items.example: The leaflet folded twice.
items.exampleCN: 这张传单折了两下。

items.example: It makes leafless, bare of leaves.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 leafless，即无叶的。

items.example: The leafless branches stood out.
items.exampleCN: 无叶的枝条格外显眼。

items.example: It makes leafage, a mass of leaves.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 leafage，即叶丛。

items.example: Leafage is rarer than foliage.
items.exampleCN: leafage 比 foliage 少见。

definition_zh: 财务损失；金钱上的损失
definition_en: money lost through an event, a transaction or a period of operation
core_image: 一只账本摊在桌上，某一页的数字被红笔划掉，旁边写下一个更小的数
scene: 账本摊在桌上，某一页的数字被红笔划掉，旁边改写成更小的数。 The flood caused a financial loss that the family could not absorb alone.
sceneCN: 账页上的数字被红笔划掉并改小，形成一笔亏空；句中的 financial loss 指「以金钱计量的损失」（第 1 个义项：因事件而失去的钱）。图中可辨识物件：账本、红笔、改写后的数字、计算器、保险单。

pos.zh: 财务损失；金钱上的损失

senses.title: Money lost in an event
senses.definition: money that is lost as the result of an accident, disaster or other event
senses.definitionCN: 因事故、灾害或其他事件而失去的钱
senses.example: The flood caused a financial loss that the family could not absorb alone.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水造成的财务损失，这家人无法独自承受。
senses.why: The phrase joins a measure to a misfortune: loss counted in money rather than in anything else.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把度量单位接到不幸上：损失以金钱而非其他东西来计量。

senses.title: An accounting loss
senses.definition: a negative result recorded in the accounts when costs exceed income
senses.definitionCN: 成本超过收入时记入账目的负数结果
senses.example: The audit revealed a financial loss hidden in the accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 审计发现账目中隐藏着一笔财务亏损。
senses.why: Once loss is booked, it becomes a line in a statement, and the qualifier distinguishes it from other kinds of shortfall.
senses.whyCN: 一旦损失被入账，它就成了报表中的一行，而限定词把它与其他类型的缺口区分开。

senses.title: A capital loss on an investment
senses.definition: the amount by which an asset's value falls below what was paid for it
senses.definitionCN: 资产价值低于买入价的那部分金额
senses.example: They accepted a financial loss rather than hold the shares longer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们宁愿接受一笔财务损失，也不愿继续持有这些股票。
senses.why: Investing separates the price paid from the price realised, and the gap between them is counted as a loss.
senses.whyCN: 投资把买入价与实现价分开，两者之间的差距就被计为损失。

senses.title: An operating loss
senses.definition: a loss made by ordinary business activity before other gains or charges are counted
senses.definitionCN: 在计入其他收益或费用之前，由日常经营活动造成的亏损
senses.example: The retail division posted an operating financial loss.
senses.exampleCN: 零售部门录得经营亏损。
senses.why: Accounting separates trading from financing, so a loss from trading gets its own label.
senses.whyCN: 会计把经营与融资分开，因此来自经营的亏损得到自己的标签。

senses.title: A loss covered by insurance
senses.definition: a loss that an insurer agrees to pay for under the terms of a policy
senses.definitionCN: 承保人依保单条款同意赔付的损失
senses.example: The policy covers financial loss from business interruption.
senses.exampleCN: 该保单承保营业中断造成的财务损失。
senses.why: Insurance needs to name the kind of harm it covers, and money lost is one standard category.
senses.whyCN: 保险需要指明承保的是哪类损害，而金钱损失是其中一个标准类别。

senses.title: A loss to the wider economy
senses.definition: the value destroyed in an economy by a shock, measured in money
senses.definitionCN: 冲击给一个经济体造成的、以金钱计量的价值毁损
senses.example: Economists put the financial loss from the port closure in the billions.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家估计港口关闭造成的财务损失达数十亿。
senses.why: At the scale of a country, many private losses are added into one public figure.
senses.whyCN: 到了国家尺度，许多私人损失被加总成一个公共数字。

senses.title: A reported loss in statements
senses.titleCN: 财务报表中报告的亏损
senses.definition: the loss figure that a company discloses in its published statements
senses.definitionCN: 公司在公开报表中披露的亏损数字
senses.example: The annual report disclosed a financial loss for the second year.
senses.exampleCN: 年报披露了第二年的财务亏损。
senses.why: Disclosure has its own vocabulary, and the phrase marks a figure that has passed audit and been made public.
senses.whyCN: 披露有其自身词汇，这个短语标记一个经过审计并向公众公布的数字。

senses.title: Any loss measured in money
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何以金钱计量的损失
senses.definition: any deprivation whose size is expressed in money, including lost opportunity or reputation
senses.definitionCN: 规模以金钱表示的任何损失，包括机会或声誉的损失
senses.example: The reputational damage was counted as a financial loss.
senses.exampleCN: 声誉损害被折算成一笔财务损失。
senses.why: The phrase can price what is not itself money, so long as a money value can be put on it.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语可以给本身并非金钱的东西定价，只要能为它估出一个金钱价值。

intro.en: The phrase joins financial, from Latin finis 'end, boundary' through French finance, with loss, an Old English noun of Germanic origin. The compound belongs to modern accounting and insurance. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语由 financial 与 loss 组成：前者经法语 finance 来自拉丁语 finis「终点、边界」；后者是日耳曼语源的古英语名词。复合短语属于近代会计与保险。年代为约数。

items.en: Finis meant 'end, boundary, limit'. A debt was settled when it reached its end, and that idea produced the money sense of the French word.
items.cn: finis 意为「终点、边界、限度」。债务到达终点即为结清，这一观念产生了法语词的金钱义。

items.en: Old French finance meant 'payment, debt, settlement', from the verb finer 'to settle, pay'.
items.cn: 古法语 finance 意为「付款、债务、结清」，来自动词 finer「结清、支付」。

items.en: English borrowed finance in the fifteenth century; its modern sense of money management and public revenue took shape in the eighteenth.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 finance；其「资金管理、公共收入」的现代义在十八世纪成形。

items.en: Loss goes back to Old English los 'loss, destruction', from a Germanic stem; it has no connection with the Latin word for an end.
items.cn: loss 可追溯到古英语 los「丧失、毁灭」，出自日耳曼语词干；它与拉丁语中表示「终点」的词毫无关联。

items.en: Financial loss appears in nineteenth- and twentieth-century insurance, accounting and economics, wherever a misfortune must be given a money value.
items.cn: financial loss 出现在十九、二十世纪的保险、会计与经济学中，凡需为不幸估出金钱价值之处都用它。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first use of the exact phrase is not recorded precisely, and the deeper root of the Germanic noun behind loss is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个确切短语的首见记录无法精确定位，loss 背后那个日耳曼名词的更早词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the two halves and their forms, which are easy to confuse; group two holds other ways of naming a money shortfall.
note.cn: 第一组是短语的两半及其形式，容易混淆；第二组是其他指金钱缺口的说法。

entries.definition: Means 'of money or finance'; it needs a noun such as loss, year or adviser to complete it.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「金钱或金融的」；必须搭配一个名词（如损失、年度、顾问）才完整。

entries.definition: Either the management of money or the act of providing funds; it is not the shortfall itself.
entries.definitionCN: 或指资金管理，或指提供资金的行为；它不是缺口本身。

entries.definition: Modifies a verb or adjective, as in financially dependent; it cannot stand where a noun is required.
entries.definitionCN: 修饰动词或形容词，如「经济上依赖」；不能占据名词的位置。

entries.definition: The loss on its own may be emotional or physical; the qualifier limits it to money.
entries.definitionCN: 单独使用时，损失可能是情感或身体上的；限定词把它限定为金钱。

entries.definition: A loss on the sale or valuation of an asset; it is one species of financial loss.
entries.definitionCN: 资产出售或估值上的损失；是财务损失的一个种类。

entries.definition: Loss measured in economic value, including lost output and welfare, not only cash.
entries.definitionCN: 以经济价值计量的损失，包括产出与福利的损失，不限于现金。

entries.definition: The gap between what is available and what is required, common in public budgets.
entries.definitionCN: 可用量与所需量之间的缺口，常见于公共预算。

entries.definition: Physical harm to property or reputation; it may or may not be given a money value.
entries.definitionCN: 对财产或声誉的实际损害；未必被折算成金钱。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real two halves, the real money vocabulary and the real insurance phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的两半、真实的金钱词汇与真实的保险搭配。

normal.en: Finance once meant settling a debt at its end; loss means the amount that never came back.
normal.cn: 金融一词曾指在终点结清债务；损失则是那笔始终没回来的钱。

normal.en: The family runs finance, financial, financially, financier, loss, lose.
normal.cn: 词族包括 finance、financial、financially、financier、loss、lose。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the context: suffer a financial loss, cover a financial loss, financial loss insurance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出语境：遭受财务损失、弥补财务损失、财务损失保险。

normal.en: The adjective does not change the noun: financial loss is loss priced in money.
normal.cn: 形容词并不改变名词：财务损失就是以金钱定价的损失。

normal.en: Insurance turns a misfortune into a figure, which is exactly what this phrase names.
normal.cn: 保险把不幸变成一个数字，而这正是这个短语所指。

abstract.en: Picture a number crossed out and replaced by a smaller one in red ink.
abstract.cn: 想象一个数字被划掉，旁边用红笔写上一个更小的数。

abstract.en: Picture a wallet that is lighter at the end of the month than at the start.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钱包，月底比月初轻。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger with one column that will never balance.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账簿，其中一栏永远无法平衡。

examples.en: The port strike caused a financial loss for exporters.
examples.cn: 港口罢工给出口商造成财务损失。

examples.en: Small firms often cannot survive a large financial loss.
examples.cn: 小公司往往经不起一次重大财务损失。

examples.en: The insurer disputed the size of the financial loss.
examples.cn: 承保人对财务损失的规模提出异议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「financial（钱的）＋loss（丢了）」——钱包里丢掉的那部分，就是财务损失

root: financial 经法语 finance 来自拉丁语 finis（终点、边界），原指债务结清；loss 为古英语 los（丧失），属日耳曼语源。二者组合指以金钱计量的损失。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one figure: a misfortune is converted into money, and that figure is then read as an event's cost, a booked loss, a fall in asset value, a trading result, an insured item, a national total, a disclosed number and finally any deprivation with a price tag.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个数字展开：不幸被换算成钱；这个数字再被读成事件的代价、入账的亏损、资产价值下跌、经营结果、承保项目、全国总额、披露的数字，最后指任何带价签的损失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure crossed out and replaced by a smaller one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个数字被划掉，换成一个更小的数。

branches.en: EVENT AND BOOK: a misfortune becomes money, then a line in the accounts.
branches.cn: 事件与账簿：不幸先变成钱，再变成账目中的一行。

branches.en: INVESTMENT AND TRADING: a fall in asset value and a trading shortfall are two ways the same gap appears.
branches.cn: 投资与经营：资产价值下跌与经营缺口，是同一个缺口出现的两种方式。

branches.en: INSURANCE: the covered loss is the misfortune given a contractual price.
branches.cn: 保险：被承保的损失，就是被合同定价的不幸。

branches.en: SCALE AND DISCLOSURE: private losses add into a national total, and audited figures are published.
branches.cn: 规模与披露：私人损失加总成全国数字，经审计的数字则被公布。

branches.en: PRICE TAG: even reputation and opportunity can be converted into this figure.
branches.cn: 价签：连声誉与机会都可以被换算成这个数字。

intro.en: The phrase pairs a Latin-derived adjective of money with a Germanic noun of loss, so its two halves come from different language stocks.
intro.cn: 这个短语把源自拉丁语、表示金钱的形容词，与日耳曼语源的「丧失」名词配在一起，两半来自不同的语源。

latinIntro.en: Latin finis supplies the finance half; the loss half has no Latin ancestor and comes from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 finis 提供「金融」那一半；「损失」那一半没有拉丁语祖先，来自古英语。

items.example: A debt ends when it is settled.
items.exampleCN: 债务在结清时到达终点。

items.meaning: to end a debt by paying
items.example: Settlement gave the word its money sense.
items.exampleCN: 结清这一动作赋予该词金钱义。

items.example: Finance became a field of its own.
items.exampleCN: 金融成为独立领域。

items.example: Financial records must be kept.
items.exampleCN: 财务记录必须保存。

items.example: The project is financially sound.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目在财务上是稳健的。

items.example: The financier backed the railway.
items.exampleCN: 这位金融家资助了铁路。

items.example: The Germanic noun carried the sense of loss.
items.exampleCN: 这个日耳曼名词承载了「丧失」之义。

items.meaning: the state of no longer having
items.example: The loss was recorded at once.
items.exampleCN: 损失被立即记录。

items.example: The firm reported a financial loss.
items.exampleCN: 该公司报告了财务损失。

definition_zh: 资本化；资本总额；市值；大写（首字母大写）；利用
definition_en: the act of turning something into capital, the total capital of a company, or the use of capital letters
core_image: 把某物抬到“头”的位置：字母抬到词首，金钱抬成资本
scene: 编辑部里，编辑把每一段的第一个字母改成大写，并在页边写下三条规则。 In the editorial office, the editor changes the first letter of every paragraph and writes three capitalization rules in the margin.
sceneCN: 这里指第 1 个义项。这里 capitalization 是「大写、首字母大写」（第 1、8 个义项：正字法与字母用法）；句意：编辑把每段第一个字母改为大写，并在页边写下三条大写规则。图中可辨识物件：稿件、红笔、页边批注、字母表。

pos.zh: 资本化；资本总额；大写

forms.label: 复数（多种资本化／大写方式）

derivatives.zh: 资本化；用大写字母书写；利用

senses.title: Writing a letter as a capital
senses.definition: the use of capital letters at the beginning of a word or sentence
senses.definitionCN: 在词首或句首使用大写字母
senses.example: Check the capitalization of every proper noun in the essay.
senses.exampleCN: 检查文章中每个专有名词的大写。
senses.why: A capital letter was once the letter 'of the head', standing at the head of a sentence. Capitalization names the act of putting that head-letter in place.
senses.whyCN: 大写字母原本是“头部的字母”，站在句子的开头。capitalization 命名的是把这个“头字母”放到位的行为。

senses.title: Writing a whole word in capitals
senses.definition: the practice of setting an entire word or phrase in capital letters, as in headlines
senses.definitionCN: 把整个词或短语排成大写字母的做法，如标题中
senses.example: The headline uses full capitalization for emphasis.
senses.exampleCN: 标题用全大写来强调。
senses.why: Once the head-letter idea is established, the same device can spread to the whole word. Emphasis, not grammar, now drives the choice.
senses.whyCN: 一旦“头字母”的观念建立起来，同一种手段就能扩展到整个词。此时驱动选择的是强调，而不是语法。

senses.title: The total capital of a company
senses.definition: the total amount of money and other capital invested in a business
senses.definitionCN: 投入一家企业的资金与其他资本的总量
senses.example: The firm has a total capitalization of about two billion dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司的资本总额约为二十亿美元。
senses.why: Capital is the 'principal sum', the chief amount at the head of an account. Capitalization turns that sum into a measured total.
senses.whyCN: capital 是“本金”，账目顶端的那个主要数额。capitalization 把这个数额变成一个被计量的总量。

senses.title: Market value of a listed company
senses.definition: the total value of a company's shares on the stock market
senses.definitionCN: 一家公司股票在证券市场上的总价值
senses.example: Its market capitalization fell by a third in one week.
senses.exampleCN: 它的市值一周内跌去三分之一。
senses.why: The market, not the accountant, now decides the size of the principal. Capitalization becomes a price times a number of shares, a public measure of value.
senses.whyCN: 现在由市场而非会计决定本金的大小。资本化变成价格乘以股数，是一种公开的价值度量。

senses.title: Turning a cost into an asset
senses.definition: in accounting, the treatment of a cost as a long-term asset rather than an immediate expense
senses.definitionCN: 会计中把某项支出作为长期资产而非当期费用处理
senses.example: The capitalization of the new equipment spread its cost over ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 新设备的资本化把成本分摊到十年。
senses.why: To capitalize a cost is to place it at the head of the balance sheet instead of writing it off at once. The accounting sense is a spatial promotion.
senses.whyCN: 把成本资本化，就是把它放到资产负债表的前端，而不是一次核销。这个会计义是一种空间上的“提拔”。

senses.title: Supplying a business with capital
senses.definition: the act of providing a company with money or capital to start or expand
senses.definitionCN: 为公司提供资金或资本以启动或扩张
senses.example: The bank required a detailed plan before capitalization.
senses.exampleCN: 银行在注资前要求一份详细计划。
senses.why: Here the word names the act that creates the principal. Money is not merely counted as capital; it is made into capital by being put in.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词命名的是创造本金的行为。钱不只是被算作资本，它是因为被投入才成为资本。

senses.title: Converting income into value
senses.titleCN: 把收益折算为价值（估值）
senses.definition: in valuation, the conversion of a stream of future income into a present capital value
senses.definitionCN: 估值中把未来收入流折算为当前资本价值
senses.example: The appraiser used income capitalization to value the building.
senses.exampleCN: 评估师用收益资本化法给这栋楼估值。
senses.why: Future rent is imagined as a flow that can be gathered into one principal sum. Capitalization is the formula that gathers it.
senses.whyCN: 未来租金被想象成一条可以聚成一个本金总额的流。资本化就是把这条流聚起来的公式。

senses.title: Turning a chance into an advantage
senses.definition: the act of taking advantage of a situation, from the verb phrase capitalize on
senses.definitionCN: 利用某种局面，来自动词短语 capitalize on
senses.example: The capitalization of the crisis by rivals was swift.
senses.exampleCN: 对手对这场危机的利用十分迅速。
senses.why: Capitalize on means to turn an event into capital. The noun extends the financial metaphor to any situation that can be made profitable.
senses.whyCN: capitalize on 意为把某件事变成资本。这个名词把金融比喻扩展到任何可以被“变现”的局面。

senses.title: The rate used in income valuation
senses.definition: the multiplier or rate used to convert expected income into capital value
senses.definitionCN: 把预期收益换算成资本价值所用的比率或乘数
senses.example: A lower capitalization rate raises the estimated value.
senses.exampleCN: 较低的资本化率会抬高估算价值。
senses.why: Once income is gathered into capital, the gathering needs a rate. Capitalization then names the number that governs the conversion, not the conversion itself.
senses.whyCN: 一旦收益被聚成资本，这个聚拢就需要一个比率。于是 capitalization 命名的是支配换算的那个数字，而不是换算本身。

intro.en: Capitalization is a two-storey derivative: capital plus the verb suffix -ize, then plus the noun suffix -ation. Capital itself goes back to Latin caput, 'head', and the whole family turns on the idea of something chief being placed at the top.
intro.cn: capitalization 是两层派生：capital 先加动词后缀 -ize，再加名词后缀 -ation。capital 本身上溯拉丁语 caput“头”，整个词族都围绕“把主要的东西放到顶端”这一想法转动。

items.en: The root *kaput- meant 'head'. It gave Latin caput and English head is a different formation, but the Latin branch supplies capital, captain, chapter and cattle.
items.cn: 词根 *kaput- 意为“头”。它给出拉丁语 caput；英语 head 是另一支，但拉丁这一支提供了 capital、captain、chapter、cattle。

items.en: Caput was the head of a person or an object. Capitalis, formed with -alis, meant 'of the head' and then 'chief, principal', because what is at the head leads the rest.
items.cn: caput 是人或物的头。capitalis 由 -alis 构成，先指“属于头的”，后指“首要的、主要的”，因为位于头部的部分引领其余部分。

items.en: The diminutive capitulum meant 'little head' and came to name a division of a book, a chapter. English chapter descends from it, showing how 'head' became a unit of text.
items.cn: 指小词 capitulum 意为“小头”，后来用来命名书中的一个部分，即一章。英语 chapter 由此而来，展示“头”如何变成一个文本单位。

items.en: Old French and Italian capitale named the principal sum of a loan and the chief city of a region. Both senses grew from 'chief thing', not from 'money' as such.
items.cn: 古法语与意大利语 capitale 指贷款的本金以及一个地区的主要城市。两者都从“首要之物”生长出来，而不是直接来自“钱”。

items.en: English capital is established in the 17th century for the principal sum of money. The phrase capital letter, a letter at the head of a sentence, gives the later orthographic branch.
items.cn: 英语 capital 在 17 世纪确立为“本金”。短语 capital letter 指句子开头的字母，给出后来正字法这一支。

items.en: Capitalize appears in the 18th century with both the money sense and the letter sense; capitalization follows in the 19th. The suffixes are Greek -izein through Latin -izare, and Latin -atio.
items.cn: capitalize 出现于 18 世纪，兼具金钱义与字母义；capitalization 随后在 19 世纪出现。后缀是希腊语 -izein 经拉丁语 -izare，以及拉丁语 -atio。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the verb, the base noun and the British spelling. The meaning group compares words from finance and writing that sit close by.
note.cn: 形近组区分动词、基础名词与英式拼写；词义组比较金融与书写领域中相邻的词。

entries.definition: the same word spelled with -s- instead of -z-, standard in British English.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词，用 -s- 代替 -z-，是英式英语的标准拼写。

entries.definition: the verb behind the noun: to write in capitals, to convert into capital, or to exploit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词：用大写书写、转为资本，或利用。

entries.definition: money, a chief city, or a capital letter. It is the base from which capitalization is built.
entries.definitionCN: 资本、首都或大写字母。它是构成 capitalization 的基础词。

entries.definition: money provided for a project or organization. It names the money itself, while capitalization names the act or the total.
entries.definitionCN: 为项目或组织提供的钱。它指钱本身，而 capitalization 指行为或总额。

entries.definition: an estimate of how much something is worth. Market capitalization is one kind of valuation.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物价值的估算。市值是估值的一种。

entries.definition: the value of a company's shares, or ownership in it. It is a component of capitalization, not the whole measure.
entries.definitionCN: 公司股份的价值，或其中的所有权。它是资本化的组成部分，而不是全部度量。

entries.definition: the conventions of writing a language, including capitals. Capitalization is one small part of orthography.
entries.definitionCN: 一种语言的书写惯例，包括大写。大写只是正字法的一小部分。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the word from capital and its two suffixes, then attach the two large meaning fields: money and letters.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩从 capital 与两个后缀搭起这个词，再挂上两大义场：金钱与字母。

normal.en: See the layers: capital + -ize + -ation. The noun is the action of the verb.
normal.cn: 看见层级：capital 加 -ize 再加 -ation。名词就是动词的动作。

normal.en: Link capital to caput, head: capital is the head-sum of an account.
normal.cn: 把 capital 连到 caput“头”：资本是账目的“头款”。

normal.en: For writing, remember that a capital letter stands at the head of a sentence.
normal.cn: 在书写方面，记住大写字母站在句子的头部。

normal.en: Pair market capitalization with share price: price times shares gives the total.
normal.cn: 把市值与股价配对：价格乘以股数得到总额。

normal.en: Keep capitalize on in mind: to capitalize is to turn an event into capital.
normal.cn: 记住 capitalize on：capitalize 就是把一件事变成资本。

abstract.en: Hold one vertical image: something is lifted to the head. Letters, costs and money are all lifted.
abstract.cn: 抓住一个垂直意象：某物被抬到头部。字母、成本、金钱都被抬起。

abstract.en: Sort the senses into two towers: the money tower and the letter tower, joined by the same 'head' idea.
abstract.cn: 把义项分成两座塔：金钱塔与字母塔，由同一个“头”的观念连接。

abstract.en: Remember the suffix chain: -ize makes the verb, -ation makes the process noun.
abstract.cn: 记住后缀链：-ize 造动词，-ation 造过程名词。

examples.en: Please follow the house style for capitalization in headings.
examples.cn: 标题中的大写请遵循本刊体例。

examples.en: The company's market capitalization passed one trillion dollars.
examples.cn: 这家公司的市值突破了一万亿美元。

examples.en: The capitalization of research costs changed the reported profit.
examples.cn: 研发成本的资本化改变了报告的利润。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“资本头来则神”：把“资本”抬到“头”上，字母也抬到词首——capitalization 就是资本化与大写。

root: 拉丁语 caput“头”及其形容词 capitalis“头部的、首要的”，经古法语与意大利语 capitale“本金、首城”进入英语作 capital；再加希腊—拉丁动词后缀 -ize 与拉丁名词后缀 -ation，构成 capitalization。

sensesIntro.en: Capitalization keeps one gesture across two very different fields: lifting something to the head. In writing, a letter is lifted to the head of a sentence; in finance, a sum is lifted to the head of an account and becomes capital. The nine senses are variations on that promotion, plus the modern extension in which any opportunity can be turned into capital.
sensesIntro.cn: capitalization 在两个很不同的领域保持同一个动作：把某物抬到头部。在书写中，字母被抬到句首；在金融中，一笔钱被抬到账目前端，成为资本。九个义项都是这种“提拔”的变体，再加上现代延伸——任何机会都能被转化为资本。

core.en: Lifting something to the head: making a letter, a cost or a sum into 'capital'.
core.cn: 把某物抬到头部：使字母、成本或款项成为“资本”。

branches.en: LETTERS: single capitals and whole words set in capitals.
branches.cn: 字母：单个大写字母与整词大写。

branches.en: CAPITAL STOCK: total capital, market value, and the act of supplying it.
branches.cn: 资本存量：资本总额、市值，以及注资行为。

branches.en: ACCOUNTING: a cost promoted to an asset.
branches.cn: 会计：成本被提升为资产。

branches.en: VALUATION: income gathered into capital, and the rate that governs it.
branches.cn: 估值：收益被聚成资本，以及支配它的比率。

branches.en: METAPHOR: any situation turned into an advantage.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何局面被转为优势。

intro.en: Capitalization shows two suffixes stacked on one base: -ize turns capital into a verb, and -ation turns that verb into a process noun. The family below also shows -ism and -ist on the same base.
intro.cn: capitalization 展示同一个词基上叠了两层后缀：-ize 把 capital 变成动词，-ation 再把动词变成过程名词。下列词族也展示同一词基上的 -ism 与 -ist。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries go back to the head itself and to the adjective of 'chief'. They explain why the financial and typographic senses share one word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目回到“头”本身以及“首要的”形容词。它们解释了为什么金融义与排版义共用同一个词。

items.meaning: the act of capitalizing; total capital; use of capitals
items.example: Capitalization rules vary between languages.
items.exampleCN: 大写规则因语言而异。

items.meaning: to write in capitals, convert into capital, or exploit
items.meaningCN: 用大写书写；转为资本；利用
items.example: You should capitalize the first word.
items.exampleCN: 你应该把第一个词大写。

items.example: They raised capital for the factory.
items.exampleCN: 他们为工厂筹集了资本。

items.example: Caput is the root behind capital.
items.exampleCN: caput 是 capital 背后的词根。

items.example: The Latin adjective capitalis meant chief.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁形容词 capitalis 意为首要的。

items.example: Capitulum became English chapter.
items.exampleCN: capitulum 演变为英语 chapter。

items.meaning: an economic system based on private capital
items.example: Industrial capitalism changed the city.
items.exampleCN: 工业资本主义改变了这座城市。

items.meaning: a person who owns or invests capital
items.example: The factory was built by a local capitalist.
items.exampleCN: 这座工厂由一位本地资本家兴建。

items.meaning: a letter at the head of a word or sentence
items.example: Names begin with a capital letter.
items.exampleCN: 姓名以大写字母开头。

items.meaning: to use an event or chance to gain an advantage
items.example: They capitalized on the confusion.
items.exampleCN: 他们利用了那场混乱。

definition_zh: 完整；正直；诚信；操守；完整性
definition_en: the state of being whole and unbroken; the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles; the soundness of data, structures, or records
core_image: 一只没有裂缝的瓷瓶：既没有缺口，也没有被偷偷换过的釉
scene: 这里指「完整」。 She refused the offer, and her integrity impressed even her opponents.
sceneCN: 这里 integrity 是「正直」（第 2 个义项：诚实且坚守道德原则的品质）；句意：她拒绝了那笔钱，她的正直甚至打动了对手。图中可辨识物件：拒签的手、信封、对方点头的神情。

pos.zh: 完整；正直；诚信；完整性

senses.title: Wholeness; the state of being complete
senses.definition: the state of being whole and undivided, with no part missing
senses.definitionCN: 完整且未被分割、没有缺失部分的状态
senses.example: The manuscript survived in its integrity despite the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管经历火灾，这份手稿仍完整保存。
senses.why: Latin integritas comes from integer 'untouched, whole', built from in- 'not' + tangere 'to touch'. What has not been touched remains whole.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 integritas 来自 integer「未被碰过的、完整的」，由 in-「不」+ tangere「触碰」构成。未被碰过的东西保持完整。

senses.title: Honesty and moral firmness
senses.definition: the quality of being honest and firm in one's moral principles
senses.definitionCN: 诚实且坚守道德原则的品质
senses.example: No one doubted the judge's personal integrity.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人怀疑这位法官的个人正直。
senses.why: A person of integrity is morally unbroken: no part has been chipped away by lies or bribes, so the whole self holds together.
senses.whyCN: 正直的人在道德上未被破坏：没有哪一部分被谎言或贿赂敲掉，因此整个自我保持完整。

senses.title: Professional probity
senses.definition: the quality of behaving honestly and ethically in a profession
senses.definitionCN: 在职业中诚实且合乎伦理地行事的品质
senses.example: The code demands integrity in handling client funds.
senses.exampleCN: 该准则要求在处理客户资金时保持职业操守。
senses.why: The metaphor moves from an unbroken object to an uncorrupted role: the professional's duty is kept whole.
senses.whyCN: 隐喻从未被破坏的物体转到未被腐蚀的角色：专业人士的职责被保持完整。

senses.title: Soundness of data or records
senses.definition: the condition in which data is accurate, complete, and unaltered
senses.definitionCN: 数据准确、完整且未被篡改的状态
senses.example: Checksums are used to verify the integrity of the file.
senses.exampleCN: 校验和用于核实文件的完整性。
senses.why: Digital data is whole when no bit has been silently changed; integrity names that untouched state.
senses.whyCN: 当没有任何一位被悄悄改动时，数字数据就是完整的；integrity 指这种未被触碰的状态。

senses.title: Structural soundness
senses.definition: the ability of a structure to hold together without weakening or collapse
senses.definitionCN: 结构保持整体、不弱化或不倒塌的能力
senses.example: Engineers inspected the dam for signs of lost integrity.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师检查大坝是否有失去完整性的迹象。
senses.why: A structure has integrity when all its parts still act as one body, with no crack allowed to divide it.
senses.whyCN: 当所有部分仍作为一个整体起作用、没有裂缝将其分开时，结构就具有完整性。

senses.title: Artistic wholeness
senses.definition: the quality of a work of art that remains true to its own vision and is not compromised
senses.definitionCN: 艺术作品忠于自身构想且未被妥协的品质
senses.example: The director fought to preserve the film's artistic integrity.
senses.exampleCN: 导演力争保全这部影片的艺术完整性。
senses.why: An artist's work is whole when nothing foreign is inserted for profit; the moral and structural senses meet.
senses.whyCN: 当没有为利益插入异物时，艺术家的作品就是完整的；道德义与结构义在此交汇。

senses.title: Territorial wholeness
senses.definition: the principle that a state's territory must not be divided or violated
senses.definitionCN: 国家领土不得被分割或侵犯的原则
senses.example: The charter protects the territorial integrity of member states.
senses.exampleCN: 该宪章保护成员国的领土完整。
senses.why: A country is pictured as a body whose borders must remain unbroken; any seizure is a wound to its integrity.
senses.whyCN: 国家被想象成一个边界必须保持完整的身体；任何夺取都是对其完整性的创伤。

senses.title: Coherence of the self
senses.definition: in psychology, the condition of a self whose parts are not split off from one another
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中，自我的各部分未彼此割裂的状态
senses.example: Sleep loss undermined his sense of integrity.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠不足损害了他的自我完整感。
senses.why: The psyche is treated as a whole that can fragment; integrity is the state in which its parts remain joined.
senses.whyCN: 心灵被当作一个可能碎裂的整体；integrity 是其各部分保持连接的状态。

senses.title: Freedom from corruption in public life
senses.definition: the quality of public conduct that is uncorrupted by private gain
senses.definitionCN: 公共行为不被私人利益腐蚀的品质
senses.example: Voters questioned the integrity of the procurement process.
senses.exampleCN: 选民质疑采购程序的公正性。
senses.why: Public trust depends on a process no one has quietly altered; integrity is the guarantee that it remains untouched.
senses.whyCN: 公共信任取决于一个无人悄悄改动的程序；integrity 是它未被触碰的保证。

intro.en: Integrity comes from Latin integritas, from integer 'untouched, whole'. It shares the root tangere 'touch' with integration, but names a state rather than a process, and has shifted from physical wholeness to moral soundness.
intro.cn: integrity 来自拉丁 integritas，源自 integer「未被碰过的、完整的」。它与 integration 共享 tangere「触碰」词根，但指状态而非过程，并从物理完整偏移到道德操守。

items.en: The reconstructed root *tag- 'to touch' is generally thought to underlie Latin tangere. The star marks a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 原始印欧语重构形式 *tag- 意为「接触」，一般认为它是拉丁 tangere 的来源。星号表示重构，并非有记录的实际词。

items.en: tangere 'to touch' also gives contact, tangent, and tactile; the family is about contact with a surface.
items.cn: tangere「触碰」还产生 contact、tangent、tactile；这个词族都与接触表面有关。

items.en: integer is in- 'not' + tangere 'touch': 'not touched, unharmed, whole'. The in- here is a real negative prefix.
items.cn: integer 是 in-「不」+ tangere「触碰」：「未被碰过的、未受损伤的、完整的」。这里的 in- 是真正的否定前缀。

items.en: integritas 'wholeness, soundness' added -itas to integer. It named the state of being untouched and complete.
items.cn: integritas「完整、健全」由 integer 加 -itas 构成，指未被触碰且完整的状态。

items.en: Latin -itas became French -ité and English -ity. English integrity kept both the physical sense of wholeness and the moral sense of soundness.
items.cn: 拉丁 -itas 变为法语 -ité 和英语 -ity。英语 integrity 同时保留物理完整义与道德健全义。

items.en: From the 16th century the word was increasingly applied to character: a person of integrity is one whose moral self has no cracks.
items.cn: 自 16 世纪起，该词越来越多用于品格：一个 integrity 的人，其道德自我没有裂缝。

note.en: The first group shares the integer root or a near shape but differs in formation and sense; the second contains words close in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组共享 integer 词根或外形相近，但构词与意义不同；第二组是意义相近的词。

entries.definition: the process of making whole; -ation names the act, while integrity names the state, and integration has no moral sense
entries.definitionCN: 使完整的过程；-ation 指动作，integrity 指状态，且 integration 没有道德义

entries.definition: necessary to the whole; as a noun, a mathematical integral; it does not mean honesty
entries.definitionCN: 对整体不可或缺的；作名词指积分；不含诚实义

entries.definition: the whole of something; from entire + -ty, naming a total, not a moral quality
entries.definitionCN: 某物的全部；由 entire + -ty 构成，指总体，不是道德品质

entries.definition: a whole number; the adjective integer 'whole' lies behind integrity but is not the noun itself
entries.definitionCN: 整数；形容词 integer「完整的」是 integrity 的来源，但并非该名词本身

entries.definition: the quality of being truthful; narrower than integrity, which also includes wholeness and firm principles
entries.definitionCN: 诚实的品质；比 integrity 窄，后者还包括完整与原则坚定

entries.definition: the state of being complete; close to sense 01 but without the moral extension
entries.definitionCN: 完整的状态；接近第 1 个义项，但没有道德延伸

entries.definition: the condition of being structurally healthy; close to senses 04 and 05
entries.definitionCN: 结构健全的状态；接近第 4、5 个义项

entries.definition: strict moral uprightness, especially in public life; close to sense 03 and more formal than integrity
entries.definitionCN: 严格的道义正直，尤指公共生活；接近第 3 个义项，比 integrity 更正式

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real word relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分和真实同族词。

normal.en: in- 'not' + tangere 'touch' gives integer 'untouched'; integritas is the state of being untouched and whole.
normal.cn: in-「不」+ tangere「触碰」构成 integer「未被碰过的」；integritas 是未被触碰且完整的状态。

normal.en: Integrity and integration share the same root, but -ity names a state while -ation names a process.
normal.cn: integrity 与 integration 同根，但 -ity 指状态，-ation 指过程。

normal.en: A person of integrity has no moral cracks: the same picture as an unbroken vase.
normal.cn: 有 integrity 的人没有道德裂缝：与一只完好的花瓶是同一画面。

normal.en: Data integrity means no bit has been silently changed; structural integrity means no crack has divided the whole.
normal.cn: 数据完整性指没有一位被悄悄改动；结构完整性指没有裂缝把整体分开。

normal.en: The moral sense grew from the physical one: untouched -> uncorrupted -> honest.
normal.cn: 道德义从物理义生长而来：未被碰过 → 未被腐蚀 → 诚实。

abstract.en: Think of a vase with no crack and no swapped glaze: integrity is both the shape and the fact that nothing was quietly replaced.
abstract.cn: 把 integrity 想象成一只没有裂缝、也没有被偷换釉面的花瓶：既是形状完整，也是没有东西被悄悄替换。

abstract.en: Think of a bridge whose every cable still pulls as one: that is structural integrity, and the same image explains moral integrity.
abstract.cn: 把 integrity 想象成一座每根缆索仍整体受力的桥：那是结构完整性，同一画面也解释道德正直。

abstract.en: Think of a public ledger with no erased line: integrity is the page that no one has quietly altered.
abstract.cn: 把 integrity 想象成一本没有擦改痕迹的公共账本：它是无人悄悄改动的那一页。

examples.en: The engineers certified the structural integrity of the tower.
examples.cn: 工程师认证了这座塔的结构完整性。

examples.en: She is widely respected for her personal and professional integrity.
examples.cn: 她因个人正直与职业操守广受尊敬。

examples.en: Encryption helps protect the integrity of transmitted records.
examples.cn: 加密有助于保护传输记录的完整性。

dict_mnemonic.note: 拆词联想 · 词源辅助
dict_mnemonic.text: in-（不）+ tegr（触碰）+ -ity（状态）：没有被碰坏的状态 → 完整 → 引申为「正直」

root: 拉丁 integritas「完整、无缺损」← integer「完整的、未被碰过的」（in-「不」+ tangere「触碰」，词根 tag-「接触」）+ -itas（英语 -ity）；与 integration、integral、integrate 同源：integral 与 integrate 强调「使合为一体」，integrity 强调未被破坏的整全，并引申出「正直」义。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses grow from 'untouched and whole': an intact manuscript, an honest character, sound data, a strong bridge, a country's borders, an unbroken self.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从「未被碰过且完整」生长而来：完好的手稿、诚实的品格、健全的数据、坚固的桥、国家的边界、未碎裂的自我。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole vessel with no crack and nothing quietly replaced.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只没有裂缝、也没有东西被悄悄替换的完整器皿。

branches.en: PHYSICAL WHOLENESS: nothing missing, nothing divided.
branches.cn: 物理完整：没有缺失，也没有被分割。

branches.en: MORAL WHOLENESS: personal honesty, professional probity, and uncorrupted public conduct.
branches.cn: 道德完整：个人诚实、职业操守与未被腐蚀的公共行为。

branches.en: TECHNICAL AND STRUCTURAL SOUNDNESS: data unchanged, structures holding together.
branches.cn: 技术与结构健全：数据未被改动，结构保持整体。

branches.en: ARTISTIC WHOLENESS: a work true to its own vision.
branches.cn: 艺术完整：作品忠于自身构想。

branches.en: BOUNDED WHOLENESS: a country's borders and a coherent self.
branches.cn: 有边界的完整：国家边界与连贯统一的自我。

intro.en: Integrity is integer plus -ity, from Latin -itas. The in- is a real negative prefix, and the root tangere 'touch' is fossilized inside the base.
intro.cn: integrity 是 integer 加 -ity（拉丁 -itas）。in- 是真正的否定前缀，词根 tangere「触碰」凝固在词基中。

latinIntro.en: Latin tangere 'to touch' also gives contact, tangent, tactile, and integer. The root appears as tang-, tact-, or teg-; *tag- is a reconstruction, not a recorded form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tangere「触碰」还产生 contact、tangent、tactile、integer。词根以 tang-、tact- 或 teg- 形式出现；*tag- 是重构形式，并非有记录的实际词。

items.meaningCN: 整数；字面为「未被碰过的、完整的」（in- 否定 + tangere）
items.example: Five is an integer.
items.exampleCN: 五是一个整数。

items.meaning: necessary to the whole; a mathematical integral
items.meaningCN: 不可或缺的；积分（-al 形容词后缀）
items.example: Trust is integral to the team.
items.exampleCN: 信任对团队不可或缺。

items.meaningCN: 使完整；整合（-ate 动词后缀）
items.example: The design integrates old and new.
items.exampleCN: 设计整合了新旧元素。

items.meaningCN: 整合；一体化（-ation 过程名词）
items.example: Integration followed the merger.
items.exampleCN: 合并之后进行了整合。

items.meaning: the state of being whole; moral soundness
items.meaningCN: 完整；正直（-ity 状态名词，由物理完整偏移到道德完整）
items.example: The seal guarantees the product's integrity.
items.exampleCN: 密封保证产品的完整性。

items.meaningCN: 整合的；综合的（-ed 分词形容词）
items.example: They use an integrated approach.
items.exampleCN: 他们采用综合方法。

items.example: The comet disintegrated in the atmosphere.
items.exampleCN: 彗星在大气中解体。

items.example: Avoid contact with the chemical.
items.exampleCN: 避免接触该化学品。

items.meaningCN: 完整的；全部的（经法语 entier 来自 integer）
items.example: The entire class attended.
items.exampleCN: 全班都出席了。

definition_zh: n. 芽，花蕾；v. 发芽；（喻）初现
definition_en: a small growth on a plant that becomes a leaf or flower; to produce buds; also to begin to develop
core_image: 三月窗台上的枝条，每个节上都冒出一个芽
scene: 三月里，窗台上那盆树每个节上都冒出了芽。 In March, a bud appeared at every joint of the plant on the windowsill.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bud 指植物的芽或花蕾；句意是三月里窗台那盆树每个节上都冒出芽。

pos.zh: 芽；花蕾
发芽；开始发育

senses.title: A small growth that becomes leaf or flower
senses.definition: a small round growth on a plant from which a leaf or flower develops
senses.definitionCN: 植物上会长成叶或花的小突起
senses.example: A green bud showed at the tip of the branch.
senses.exampleCN: 枝端露出一个绿色的芽。
senses.why: A bud is the plant folded into its smallest form.
senses.whyCN: 芽是折叠成最小形态的植物。

senses.title: To produce buds
senses.definition: to begin to grow buds
senses.definitionCN: 开始长出芽
senses.example: The roses budded early this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年玫瑰早早打苞。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb of beginning.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词变成了表示「开始」的动词。

senses.title: The first stage of something
senses.definition: the very beginning of a feeling, idea or process
senses.definitionCN: 情感、想法或过程的最初阶段
senses.example: The idea was still only a bud.
senses.exampleCN: 这个想法还只是个萌芽。
senses.why: Plants and plans both start small and enclosed.
senses.whyCN: 植物与计划都从微小封闭处开始。

intro.en: Bud comes from Middle English budde, a sprout.
intro.cn: bud 来自中古英语 budde，意为嫩芽。

items.en: Budde means a sprout or a seed case.
items.cn: budde 意为嫩芽或种荚。

items.en: Bud names the growth that becomes a leaf.
items.cn: bud 指会长成叶的突起。

items.en: The word covers flower buds as well.
items.cn: 该词也涵盖花蕾。

items.en: Nip in the bud means stop it early.
items.cn: nip in the bud 意为及早制止。

items.en: Grafting uses buds as growing points.
items.cn: 嫁接以芽作为生长点。

items.en: Budding means beginning to succeed.
items.cn: budding 意为崭露头角。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bud- shape; the near-meaning group ranks plant beginnings from seed to flower.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bud- 形状；近义组把植物的开端从种子排到花。

entries.definition: A close friend.
entries.definitionCN: 好友。

entries.definition: To move slightly.

entries.definition: Furniture for sleeping.

entries.definition: Not good.

entries.definition: A new stem growing from a plant.
entries.definitionCN: 植物长出的新茎。

entries.definition: A very young shoot.
entries.definitionCN: 刚冒出的幼芽。

entries.definition: The first living point of a seed.
entries.definitionCN: 种子的最初生长点。

entries.definition: The flower of a tree or bush.
entries.definitionCN: 树或灌木的花。

normalIntro.en: A bud is a whole plant folded up small enough to wait.
normalIntro.cn: bud 是一整棵植物折小到可以等待的样子。

normal.en: Bud rhymes with mud.
normal.cn: bud 与 mud 押韵。

normal.en: It is a leaf or flower still folded.
normal.cn: 它是尚未展开的叶或花。

normal.en: To bud is to start producing them.
normal.cn: to bud 意为开始长出芽。

normal.en: Nip in the bud means stop it early.
normal.cn: nip in the bud 意为及早制止。

normal.en: Budding means just beginning to shine.
normal.cn: budding 意为刚崭露头角。

abstract.en: A fist that will open into a leaf.
abstract.cn: 将要张成叶子的一个拳头。

abstract.en: Something waiting at the tip of a branch.
abstract.cn: 在枝头等待的某种东西。

abstract.en: A plan small enough to hide.
abstract.cn: 小到能藏起来的计划。

examples.en: The first buds appeared after the rain.
examples.cn: 雨后第一批芽冒了出来。

examples.en: Prune the branch just above a bud.
examples.cn: 在芽的上方修剪枝条。

examples.en: They nipped the rumour in the bud.
examples.cn: 他们把谣言消弭于萌芽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「巴得」——芽巴在枝头上，得等一等才展开。

root: 中古英语 budde（嫩芽）

sensesIntro.en: A bud is potential held in the smallest possible package: a tree, a flower, or an idea, all still shut.
sensesIntro.cn: 芽是把潜力装进最小的包裹：一棵树、一朵花或一个念头，都还闭合着。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one green bud at every joint of a windowsill plant
core.cn: 核心意象：窗台植物每个节上的一个绿芽

branches.en: A green tip at the end of a branch.
branches.cn: 枝端的一个绿尖。

branches.en: Roses budding earlier than usual.
branches.cn: 比往年早打苞的玫瑰。

branches.en: An idea still folded shut.
branches.cn: 仍合着的想法。

branches.en: A rumour stopped at once.
branches.cn: 被立刻制止的谣言。

branches.en: A beginning small enough to protect.
branches.cn: 小到能保护起来的开端。

definition_zh: 花岗岩；由石英、长石与云母等矿物结晶而成的粗粒酸性侵入岩
definition_en: a coarse-grained intrusive igneous rock made mainly of quartz, feldspar, and mica
core_image: 海边灰白色崖壁上散布着黑色与白色矿物颗粒
scene: 海边悬崖被浪切成陡壁，灰白色岩石里闪着黑色与白色的颗粒： The sea cliff is solid granite speckled with dark and pale crystals.
sceneCN: 这里 granite 指「粗粒的酸性侵入岩」（第 1 个义项：由石英、长石与云母结晶成的深成岩）；句意为海边崖壁是坚实的花岗岩，上面布满深浅色晶体颗粒。

pos.zh: 花岗岩（物质名词；指多种花岗岩时复数为 granites）

senses.title: Coarse-grained intrusive igneous rock
senses.definition: an igneous rock that cooled slowly deep underground, allowing large crystals of quartz, feldspar, and mica to grow
senses.definitionCN: 在地下深处缓慢冷却、因而长出大颗石英、长石与云母晶体的火成岩
senses.example: The sea cliff is solid granite speckled with dark and pale crystals.
senses.exampleCN: 海边崖壁是坚实的 granite，布满深浅色晶体颗粒。
senses.why: Slow cooling gives crystals time to grow, and the visible speckle is the signature of that slow history.
senses.whyCN: 缓慢冷却给晶体生长的时间，肉眼可见的斑点正是这段缓慢历史的标志。

senses.title: The stone as a building material
senses.definition: the rock cut and polished for countertops, paving, walls, and monuments
senses.definitionCN: 被切割抛光用于台面、铺地、墙体与纪念碑的该种岩石
senses.example: The kitchen counter is polished granite.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房台面是抛光花岗岩。
senses.why: Hard, acid-resistant, and polishable, granite moved from cliffs into kitchens and bank lobbies.
senses.whyCN: 坚硬、耐酸且可抛光，使花岗岩从崖壁走进厨房与银行大厅。

senses.title: A large intrusive body
senses.definition: a batholith or stock of granite covering many square kilometres underground
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖地下许多平方公里的大型岩基或岩株
senses.example: The mountain range sits on a granite batholith.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山脉坐落在一处花岗岩岩基上。
senses.why: At depth, many granite intrusions merge into one enormous body that only erosion later reveals.
senses.whyCN: 在地下深处，许多花岗岩侵入体合并成一个巨大岩体，只有侵蚀才后来将其揭示。

senses.title: A tor or weathered upland
senses.definition: granite that weathering has shaped into tors, rounded boulders, and bare uplands
senses.definitionCN: 被风化塑造成岩丘、浑圆巨砾与裸露高地的花岗岩
senses.example: Granite tors crown the moor.
senses.exampleCN: 花岗岩岩丘耸立在荒原上。
senses.why: Granite fractures along joints and decays into rounded blocks, leaving towers where the rock was jointed least.
senses.whyCN: 花岗岩沿节理裂开并风化成浑圆石块，在节理最少处留下塔状岩丘。

senses.title: Monument and memorial stone
senses.definition: granite valued for monuments because it resists weather and takes a sharp edge
senses.definitionCN: 因耐风化且能磨出锋利边缘而用于纪念碑的花岗岩
senses.example: Names were cut deep into the granite obelisk.
senses.exampleCN: 名字被深深刻入花岗岩方尖碑。
senses.why: A memorial must outlast the memory it serves, and granite is chosen for exactly that durability.
senses.whyCN: 纪念碑必须比它所承载的记忆更长久，花岗岩正因这种耐久性被选中。

senses.title: Continental crust material
senses.definition: the granitic rock that makes up much of the continental crust, lighter than oceanic basalt
senses.definitionCN: 构成大陆地壳大部分的花岗质岩石，比大洋玄武岩轻
senses.example: Granite floats the continents higher than the ocean floor.
senses.exampleCN: 花岗岩使大陆浮得比洋底更高。
senses.why: Because it is less dense than basalt, continental crust rises and stands above the oceans.
senses.whyCN: 由于密度低于玄武岩，大陆地壳抬升并高出海面。

senses.title: A dimension stone trade name
senses.definition: any hard speckled stone sold under the commercial label granite, even when it is not true granite
senses.definitionCN: 商业上以花岗岩为标签销售的硬质斑点石材，即使并非真正花岗岩
senses.example: The showroom sells black granite that is really gabbro.
senses.exampleCN: 展厅卖的黑色花岗岩其实是辉长岩。
senses.why: Trade names follow appearance and durability rather than petrology, so the market's granite is wider than the geologist's.
senses.whyCN: 商品名依据外观与耐久性而非岩石学，因此市场上的花岗岩比地质学家的定义更宽。

senses.title: Abstract: unyielding hardness
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：坚硬不屈的性质
senses.definition: a quality of stubborn strength and resistance to change
senses.definitionCN: 固执坚强、抗拒改变的性质
senses.example: She met the criticism with granite calm.
senses.exampleCN: 她以花岗岩般的镇定面对批评。
senses.why: The metaphor takes the rock's most obvious property, hardness, and applies it to character.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻取岩石最明显的属性——坚硬，并将其用于性格。

intro.en: Granite is an Italian coinage from the Latin word for grain, named for its visible crystals. The origin of the base word is well attested. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: granite 是意大利语造词，来自拉丁语「谷粒」，因肉眼可见的晶体而得名。词根书证充分。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin granum meant 'grain, seed', from Proto-Indo-European gerh2- 'grain'. The root is widely attested in grain, granary, and granular.
items.cn: 拉丁语 granum 意为「谷粒、种子」，来自原始印欧语 gerh2-「谷粒」。该词根广见于 grain、granary 与 granular。

items.en: Italian stonecutters called the speckled rock granito, literally 'grained stone', from granire 'to produce grains'.
items.cn: 意大利石匠把这种带斑点的岩石称作 granito，字面是「有颗粒的石头」，来自 granire「使成粒」。

items.en: English adopted granite in the eighteenth century as the geological classification of rocks developed.
items.cn: 随着岩石地质分类的发展，英语在 18 世纪借入 granite。

items.en: Later petrology narrowed granite to a specific plutonic rock of quartz, alkali feldspar, and mica, excluding similar-looking stones.
items.cn: 后来的岩石学把 granite 收窄为一种由石英、碱性长石与云母组成的具体深成岩，排除外观相似的石材。

items.en: The building trade kept the older, looser sense, so commercial granite includes rocks that petrology would call something else. The exact date of this split is uncertain.
items.cn: 建筑行业保留了更早、更宽松的含义，因此商业花岗岩包括岩石学会另作定名的石材。这一分野的确切年代不确定。

note.en: Group one holds igneous rock names that are easily confused with granite; group two holds stones that look similar in use.
note.cn: 第一组是易与花岗岩混淆的火成岩名称；第二组是用途上外观相近的石材。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of granite'; it describes the rock rather than naming it.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「花岗岩的」的形容词；它描述该岩石，而不是命名它。

entries.definition: To make into grains; it shares the Latin grain root but has nothing to do with igneous rock.
entries.definitionCN: 使成颗粒；与花岗岩共享拉丁语「谷粒」词根，但与火成岩无关。

entries.definition: A coarse-grained intrusive rock rich in dark minerals; commercial 'black granite' is often gabbro.
entries.definitionCN: 富含暗色矿物的粗粒侵入岩；商业上的「黑色花岗岩」常是辉长岩。

entries.definition: An intrusive rock between granite and gabbro in composition, with little quartz.
entries.definitionCN: 成分介于花岗岩与辉长岩之间的侵入岩，石英很少。

entries.definition: Recrystallized limestone used for carving and polish; it is softer and reacts with acid.
entries.definitionCN: 重结晶的石灰岩，用于雕刻与抛光；它更软且遇酸反应。

entries.definition: Metamorphosed sandstone, hard and granular but without feldspar's cleavage faces.
entries.definitionCN: 变质的砂岩，坚硬且具颗粒感，但没有长石的解理面。

entries.definition: A fine-grained volcanic rock, denser and darker than granite, forming the ocean floor.
entries.definitionCN: 细粒火山岩，比花岗岩更致密更深色，构成洋底。

entries.definition: A high-grade metamorphic rock with light and dark bands, often derived from granite.
entries.definitionCN: 具深浅条带的高级变质岩，常由花岗岩变质而来。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin roots, real rock names and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实拉丁词根、真实岩石名称与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Granite is named for its grains: granum is Latin for grain.
normal.cn: 花岗岩因颗粒得名：granum 是拉丁语「谷粒」。

normal.en: Visible crystals mean slow cooling deep underground.
normal.cn: 可见晶体意味着在地下深处缓慢冷却。

normal.en: Its family runs granite, granitic, granular, granulate, grain.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 granite、granitic、granular、granulate 与 grain。

normal.en: Granite is continental; basalt is oceanic. Density explains the difference.
normal.cn: 花岗岩属大陆，玄武岩属大洋；密度解释了这一差别。

normal.en: Commercial granite is broader than geological granite.
normal.cn: 商业花岗岩比地质学定义的花岗岩更宽泛。

abstract.en: Picture a stone made of many tiny mirrors, each catching light at a different angle.
abstract.cn: 想象一块由许多小镜子组成的石头，每面镜子以不同角度反光。

abstract.en: Picture a cliff that refuses to soften even after a thousand winters.
abstract.cn: 想象一面崖壁，历经千个冬天仍不肯变软。

abstract.en: Picture a person whose calm looks carved rather than practised.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人的镇定像是被凿出来的，而不是练出来的。

examples.en: The sea cliff is solid granite speckled with dark and pale crystals.
examples.cn: 海边崖壁是坚实的花岗岩岩体，布满深浅色晶体颗粒。

examples.en: The counter is polished granite, cold even in summer.
examples.cn: 台面是抛光花岗岩，夏天摸着也是凉的。

examples.en: Weathering splits granite into rounded blocks that pile up as tors.
examples.cn: 风化把花岗岩裂成浑圆石块，堆成岩丘。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「格拉尼特」——布满彩色颗粒的硬石头 → 花岗岩

root: 意大利语 granito「有颗粒的石头」，源自 granire「使成粒」与 grano「谷粒」，再上溯拉丁语 granum「谷粒」，原始印欧语词根 gerh2-「谷粒」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the rock's cooling history to its uses, its landforms, its crustal role, its trade name, and finally to hardness as a human image.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从冷却历史走到用途、地貌、地壳角色、商品名，最后落到作为人性意象的坚硬。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey cliff surface speckled with black and white crystals, each large enough to see.
core.cn: 核心意象：布满黑白晶体的灰色崖面，每颗晶体都大到肉眼可见。

branches.en: CRYSTALS AND BODY: visible grains are the small signature of a very large slow-cooled mass.
branches.cn: 晶体与岩体：可见颗粒是巨大慢冷岩体的小小标志。

branches.en: DURABLE USE: hardness and polish make it a kitchen surface and a memorial stone.
branches.cn: 耐久用途：硬度与可抛光使它成为台面与纪念碑。

branches.en: LANDSCAPE: jointing and weathering turn the mass into tors and rounded boulders.
branches.cn: 地貌：节理与风化把岩体变成岩丘与浑圆巨砾。

branches.en: CRUST: low density keeps the continents standing above the ocean floor.
branches.cn: 地壳：低密度让大陆高出洋底。

branches.en: NAME AND METAPHOR: the market stretches the word, and the language borrows its hardness.
branches.cn: 名称与比喻：市场扩大了词义，语言则借用了它的坚硬。

intro.en: Granite's family is built on the Latin grain root, which is unusually productive in English.
intro.cn: 花岗岩的词族建立在拉丁语「谷粒」词根上，这一词根在英语中格外多产。

latinIntro.en: Latin granum and the Italian derivative granito stand behind granite; granum also gives grain, granary, and granular.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 granum 与意大利语派生词 granito 支撑 granite；granum 还给出 grain、granary 与 granular。

items.example: Granum is the source of several English grain words.
items.exampleCN: granum 是若干英语「颗粒」词的来源。

items.example: Italian masons named the rock granito.
items.exampleCN: 意大利石匠把这种岩石称作 granito。

items.example: Granite cools slowly and grows large crystals.
items.exampleCN: 花岗岩缓慢冷却，长出大晶体。

items.example: The granitic intrusion extends for many kilometres.
items.exampleCN: 这处花岗质侵入体延伸许多公里。

items.example: Granular texture is typical of slow cooling.
items.exampleCN: 颗粒状结构是缓慢冷却的典型特征。

items.example: The machine granulates the slag.
items.exampleCN: 机器把矿渣造粒。

items.example: The rock's grain size is easy to see.
items.exampleCN: 这块岩石的粒径很容易看清。

items.example: Granary and granite share the same Latin root.
items.exampleCN: granary 与 granite 共享同一拉丁词根。

items.structure: German Gneis, probably from a mining term
items.example: Gneiss often forms from granite under pressure.
items.exampleCN: 片麻岩常由花岗岩在压力下形成。

definition_zh: 火山的；火山造成的；火山岩的；火山土的；（脾气或局势）一触即发的
definition_en: relating to or produced by a volcano, or, of a mood or situation, ready to explode like one
core_image: 一座锥形山体顶端喷出灰柱，黑色熔岩顺坡流下，冷却成坚硬的石
scene: 海边的小村旁，黑色砂粒在浪里翻滚，孩子弯腰捧起一把，掌心留下细小的黑色颗粒。 The black sand under our feet is volcanic, worn from old lava by the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 volcanic 是形容词「由火山物质形成的」（第 2 个义项：火山岩、火山灰等喷出物构成的）；句意为脚下的黑沙是火山物质，由古老熔岩被海水磨碎而成。

pos.zh: 火山的；火山造成的；火山岩的；火山土的；（比喻）一触即发的

forms.label: 名词化用法（前加定冠词，指火山岩类）

derivatives.zh: 由火山作用地；火山性地

senses.title: Relating to a volcano
senses.definition: relating to a volcano or to the fire, ash and rock it produces
senses.definitionCN: 与火山或与其产生的火、灰、岩石有关的
senses.example: The island's volcanic peaks rise straight from the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛上的火山峰从海面直直升起。
senses.why: the adjective simply marks belonging: volcanic scenery, volcanic origin, volcanic island all attach the noun to the fire mountain.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只标记归属：火山地貌、火山成因、火山岛，都是把名词挂到那座火之山上。

senses.title: Rock and ash from a volcano
senses.definition: made of or consisting of material thrown out by a volcano, such as lava, ash or pumice
senses.definitionCN: 由火山喷出的物质（如熔岩、火山灰或浮石）构成或组成的
senses.example: Layers of volcanic ash lie between the coal seams.
senses.exampleCN: 煤层之间夹着层层火山灰。
senses.why: geology uses the adjective for the material itself, so a rock can be called volcanic without naming a particular mountain.
senses.whyCN: 地质学用这个形容词指材料本身，因此一块岩石可以被称为火山的，而不必指明某座具体的山。

senses.title: Volcanic activity or eruption
senses.definition: caused by or showing the action of a volcano, including eruptions, tremors and gas release
senses.definitionCN: 由火山作用引起或表现出的，包括喷发、颤动与气体释放
senses.example: Volcanic activity increased sharply before the evacuation.
senses.exampleCN: 撤离之前，火山活动急剧增加。
senses.why: the adjective shifts from the place to the process, naming an event rather than a mountain or a stone.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从「地点」转到「过程」，指事件而非山体或石头。

senses.title: Fertile volcanic soil
senses.definition: describing soil formed from weathered volcanic material, which is often rich in minerals and very productive
senses.definitionCN: 描述由风化火山物质形成的土壤，常富含矿物质且十分肥沃
senses.example: Farmers prize the deep volcanic soil for its minerals.
senses.exampleCN: 农民看重深厚的火山土，因为它富含矿物质。
senses.why: the destructive mountain leaves a gift behind, and the adjective carries that unlikely pairing of fire and fertility.
senses.whyCN: 毁灭性的山体留下了一份礼物，这个形容词就承载着「火与肥沃」这种出人意料的组合。

senses.title: Volcanic glass
senses.definition: a natural glass formed when lava cools too quickly to crystallize, as in obsidian
senses.definitionCN: 熔岩冷却过快、来不及结晶时形成的天然玻璃，如黑曜岩
senses.example: Volcanic glass forms when lava cools too fast to crystallize.
senses.exampleCN: 熔岩冷却得太快、来不及结晶时就形成火山玻璃。
senses.why: the adjective names the origin of the material, while glass names its structure, so the phrase combines a source and a texture.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词指明材料的来源，玻璃指明其结构，因此这个短语把来源与质地组合在一起。

senses.title: Volcanic winter
senses.definition: a period of global cooling caused by ash and sulfur aerosols from a very large eruption blocking sunlight
senses.definitionCN: 极大规模喷发产生的灰与硫气溶胶遮挡阳光、造成全球降温的一段时期
senses.example: A large eruption can cause a volcanic winter that cools the whole planet.
senses.exampleCN: 一次大喷发可能引发火山冬天，使整个行星降温。
senses.why: climate science extended the adjective from the mountain to the planet, because the effects of an eruption travel far beyond the cone.
senses.whyCN: 气候科学把这个形容词从山体扩展到行星，因为喷发的影响会远远超出火山锥。

senses.title: Volcanic arc
senses.definition: a curved chain of volcanoes formed above a descending tectonic plate at a subduction zone
senses.definitionCN: 在俯冲带、位于下沉板块之上形成的一列弧形火山链
senses.example: The islands form a volcanic arc above the subducting plate.
senses.exampleCN: 这些岛屿在俯冲板块之上构成一条火山弧。
senses.why: plate tectonics needed a term for a whole line of volcanoes, and the adjective turned a single mountain into a geographic pattern.
senses.whyCN: 板块构造学需要一个指整条火山链的术语，这个形容词把单座山变成了地理格局。

senses.title: Ready to explode, of temper or tension
senses.titleCN: 比喻：脾气或局势一触即发
senses.definition: extremely explosive, violent or unstable, used of a person's temper or of a tense situation
senses.definitionCN: 极其易爆、猛烈或不稳定的，用于人的脾气或紧张的局势
senses.example: His volcanic temper emptied the meeting room in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 他那火山般的脾气几秒钟内就让会议室空了。
senses.why: the metaphor is almost too easy: a volcano gives warning, then erupts, and so does a temper that has been held down too long.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻几乎太顺理成章：火山先有预兆再喷发，被压抑太久的脾气也是如此。

intro.en: Volcanic is volcano plus the adjective suffix -ic. Volcano reached English through Italian from Latin Volcanus, also spelled Vulcanus, the Roman god of fire and metalworking. The suffix -ic came from Greek -ikos by way of Latin -icus.
intro.cn: volcanic 是在表示火山的那个英语名词上加形容词后缀 -ic 构成。那个名词经意大利语来自拉丁 Volcanus（亦作 Vulcanus），即罗马的火与冶金之神。后缀 -ic 由希腊 -ikos 经拉丁 -icus 进入英语。

items.en: Volcanus was the Roman god of fire and the forge. His name was also given to burning ground and to the fire itself, which is why a mountain that burns bears it.
items.cn: Volcanus 是罗马的火与锻造之神。他的名字也被用于燃烧的地面与火本身，因此一座会燃烧的山沿用此名。

items.en: Italian vulcano named a burning mountain, and English borrowed the word as volcano, generally in the seventeenth century, through Italian or French.
items.cn: 意大利语中的火山之名本指「燃烧的山」，英语一般在十七世纪经意大利语或法语借入这个词，成为表示火山的名称。

items.en: The suffix -ic entered English from Latin -icus, itself from Greek -ikos, meaning belonging to or connected with; it turns a noun into an adjective of relation.
items.cn: 后缀 -ic 由拉丁 -icus 进入英语，而 -icus 又出自希腊 -ikos，意为「属于……的、与……有关的」；它把名词变成表示关系的形容词。

items.en: Volcanic was formed on volcano in the late eighteenth century, first describing rocks and terrain produced by fire, then widening to the whole subject.
items.cn: volcanic 于十八世纪后期在火山这一名词上构成，最初描述火造成的岩石与地貌，随后扩展到整个主题。

items.en: Geology added volcanic arc, volcanic glass and volcaniclastic; climatology added volcanic winter. All keep the original image of a mountain that burns.
items.cn: 地质学增添了火山弧、火山玻璃与火山碎屑等说法；气候学增添了火山冬天。它们都保留着「会燃烧的山」这一原初意象。

items.en: Two tiers of doubt: the origin of the god's name is uncertain, with an Etruscan source often suggested but never proved, a root question; the first date of the rock sense is only approximate, a dating question.
items.cn: 来源不确定，分两档：火神之名的来源不确定，常有人提出源自伊特鲁里亚语，但从未得到证实，属词根存疑；岩石义的首见年代只是约数，属年代存疑。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the volcano family; group two holds near neighbours that describe fire, rock and eruption.
note.cn: 第一组是建于火山这一词族之上的词；第二组是描述火、岩石与喷发的近义词。

entries.definition: The mountain itself, from which volcanic is formed by adding -ic; the direction is noun to adjective, never the reverse.
entries.definitionCN: 指山体本身；volcanic 是在它之上加 -ic 构成的形容词，方向是名词到形容词，绝非反向。

entries.definition: The whole set of processes by which magma reaches the surface; it names the activity, not a single mountain.
entries.definitionCN: 岩浆到达地表的整套过程；它指活动，而非单座山。

entries.definition: The scientific study of volcanoes and volcanic phenomena, built with the study suffix -logy.
entries.definitionCN: 研究火山与火山现象的科学，由表示「学科」的后缀构成。

entries.definition: In a volcanic manner or by volcanic action, as in a volcanically active region.
entries.definitionCN: 以火山的方式或由火山作用地，如「火山活动活跃的地区」。

entries.definition: Relating to rock solidified from magma or lava; broader than volcanic, because it also covers rock that cooled deep underground.
entries.definitionCN: 指由岩浆或熔岩固结而成的岩石；比 volcanic 更广，因为它也包括地下深处冷却的岩石。

entries.definition: Relating to an eruption or tending to burst out suddenly, used of volcanoes, skin rashes and tempers alike.
entries.definitionCN: 与喷发有关的，或倾向于突然爆发的，火山、皮疹与脾气都可用。

entries.definition: Made of fragments of hot rock and ash thrown out by an eruption, a narrower technical term than volcanic.
entries.definitionCN: 由喷发抛出的炽热岩石碎片与灰构成的，是比 volcanic 更窄的术语。

entries.definition: Burning or glowing like fire, or intensely passionate; it shares the heat image but not the geological meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 像火一样燃烧或发光的，或极其炽烈的；它共享「热」的意象，但没有地质含义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin name, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁名称、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Volcan- is the fire god's name, so the root already contains a mountain that burns.
normal.cn: volcan- 就是火神的名字，因此词根本身已经含着一座会燃烧的山。

normal.en: The suffix -ic makes an adjective of belonging: relating to the fire mountain.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ic 造出表示归属的形容词：与那座火之山有关的。

normal.en: Volcanic describes origin and material; the noun names the mountain. Keep the direction straight.
normal.cn: volcanic 描述来源与材料，名词则指山本身；要把构词方向记牢。

normal.en: Each science borrows the adjective for its own object: winter, glass, arc, soil.
normal.cn: 每门学科都借这个形容词指自己的对象：冬天、玻璃、弧、土。

normal.en: The figurative use keeps the eruption: a volcanic temper erupts, it does not simmer.
normal.cn: 比喻用法保留喷发的意象：火山般的脾气是爆发，而不是慢炖。

abstract.en: Picture a pressure cooker whose lid lifts before anyone expects it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只压力锅，锅盖在谁都没预料到的时候被顶起。

abstract.en: Picture a classroom silent because one person's anger fills it.
abstract.cn: 想象一间教室鸦雀无声，只因一个人的怒气充满了整个空间。

abstract.en: Picture a hillside green with vines growing on old ash.
abstract.cn: 想象一片山坡绿意盎然，藤蔓长在陈年的火山灰上。

examples.en: Volcanic ash grounded flights across the region.
examples.cn: 火山灰使整个地区的航班停飞。

examples.en: The vineyard thrives on volcanic soil.
examples.cn: 这片葡萄园在火山土上长势旺盛。

examples.en: He has a volcanic temper that shows up without warning.
examples.cn: 他有一种毫无预兆就爆发的火暴脾气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「volcan（火神）+ ic」——火神的山一喷就炸 → 火山的、火山岩的、一触即发的

root: 拉丁 Volcanus（罗马火神，亦作 Vulcanus）经意大利语进入英语，成为表示火山的那个名词；本词是在该名词上加希腊来源、经拉丁而来的形容词后缀 -ic 构成，方向是名词加后缀，而非反向派生。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one source: a mountain that opens and pours out fire, ash and stone. The adjective first marks the mountain, then its material, its activity, its gifts to soil, glass and climate, its geography, and finally an explosive human mood.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个源头展开：一座裂开并喷出火、灰与石的山。这个形容词先标记山体，再依次标记其材料、活动、对土壤与玻璃与气候的馈赠、其地理格局，最后落到人的爆发性情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mountain that opens and pours fire, ash and black glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座裂开、喷出火、灰与黑色玻璃的山。

branches.en: THE MOUNTAIN ITSELF: the plain adjective of belonging, with no special object yet.
branches.cn: 山体本身：最朴素的归属形容词，尚未挂上特定对象。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND PROCESS: what comes out of the mountain, and the act of it coming out.
branches.cn: 材料与过程：山喷出的东西，以及它喷出的那个动作。

branches.en: PRODUCTS ON LAND: the same material becomes fertile soil or natural glass.
branches.cn: 陆地上的产物：同一种材料变成肥沃的土或天然的玻璃。

branches.en: PLANETARY SCALE: one eruption reaches the climate, many eruptions make an arc.
branches.cn: 行星尺度：一次喷发触及气候，许多次喷发连成一道弧。

branches.en: FIGURATIVE FIRE: a person or a situation that holds pressure until it blows.
branches.cn: 比喻之火：一个人或一种局势积压着压力，直到炸开。

intro.en: Volcanic is a noun of place turned into an adjective by one suffix, and that same root supports a whole vocabulary of fire, rock and study.
intro.cn: volcanic 是由地名名词经一个后缀变成的形容词，而同一词根支撑起整套关于火、岩石与研究的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin Volcanus, the fire god, and the Greek-origin suffix -icus give volcanic and its relatives volcano, volcanism and volcanology.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 Volcanus（火神）与希腊来源的后缀 -icus 构成本词及其同族词，包括表示火山的那个名词、火山作用与火山学。

items.example: The stem volcan- names the fire god and his mountain.
items.exampleCN: 词干 volcan- 指火神与他的山。

items.example: The volcano rises from the sea.
items.exampleCN: 那座火山从海面升起。

items.example: The suffix -ic turns a noun of place into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 把指地点的名词变成形容词。

items.example: The island has a volcanic origin.
items.exampleCN: 这座岛有火山成因。

items.example: The ridge was volcanically active for ages.
items.exampleCN: 这条山脊长期处于火山活动之中。

items.example: Volcanism shaped the whole plateau.
items.exampleCN: 火山作用塑造了整个高原。

items.example: Volcanology combines geology and chemistry.
items.exampleCN: 火山学结合了地质学与化学。

items.example: The volcanologist measured the swelling of the cone.
items.exampleCN: 火山学家测量了锥体的膨胀。

items.example: The sediment is volcanogenic, not river-borne.
items.exampleCN: 这种沉积物是火山成因的，而非河流搬运的。

items.example: The cliff is built of volcaniclastic layers.
items.exampleCN: 这处崖壁由火山碎屑层构成。

latinEntries.meaning: the same god, the spelling behind the Italian name for a burning mountain
latinEntries.meaningCN: 同一位火神的另一种拼写，也是意大利语火山之名的来源拼写

definition_zh: 重新评估；重新考虑；重新掂量
definition_en: to judge the value, risk or worth of something again, usually because circumstances have changed
core_image: 一叠旧报表被推到桌边，一只手拿起了新的那一页
scene: 项目做到一半，账上的数字对不上了，团队只好把整个计划重新掂量一遍。 Halfway through the project the figures no longer matched, and the team had to reassess the whole plan.
sceneCN: 这里 reassess 指重新评估（第 1 个义项：重新评估计划）；句意为项目做到一半，账上的数字对不上了，团队只好把整个计划重新掂量一遍。

pos.zh: 重新评估；重新考虑；重新掂量

collocations.zh: 在结果出来之后重新评估

senses.title: To reassess a plan
senses.definition: to judge a plan again after its assumptions have shifted
senses.definitionCN: 在假设发生变化之后重新判断一个计划
senses.example: The team had to reassess the plan after the second delay.
senses.exampleCN: 第二次延误之后，团队不得不重新评估这个计划。
senses.why: The first sense is the practical one: the ground moved.
senses.whyCN: 第一个义项是最实际的：地基移动了。

senses.title: To reassess the risk
senses.definition: to recalculate how dangerous something is with new evidence
senses.definitionCN: 用新证据重新衡量某事的危险程度
senses.example: The bank reassessed the risk of the loan after the audit.
senses.exampleCN: 审计之后，银行重新评估了这笔贷款的风险。
senses.why: Risk is the word's most common object in finance.
senses.whyCN: 在金融里，risk 是这个词最常见的宾语。

senses.title: To reassess a decision
senses.definition: to reopen a choice that had been treated as settled
senses.definitionCN: 重新打开一个已被当作定案的选择
senses.example: The board reassessed its decision when the costs doubled.
senses.exampleCN: 成本翻倍之后，董事会重新考虑了它的决定。
senses.why: The sense admits that a judgement can be wrong.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项承认判断可能是错的。

senses.title: To reassess priorities
senses.definition: to change the order in which things matter
senses.definitionCN: 改变事物重要性的先后次序
senses.example: After the illness he reassessed his priorities in a single afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 病后他在一个下午之内重新排定了自己的轻重缓急。
senses.why: The word can describe a private turning point.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能描述私人的转折点。

senses.title: To reassess the situation
senses.definition: to form a fresh reading of events as they develop
senses.definitionCN: 随着事态发展形成新的判断
senses.example: Officials reassessed the situation hourly during the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水期间，官员每小时重新评估一次局势。
senses.why: The sense is the language of briefings and command.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是指挥与简报的语言。

senses.title: To reassess after the results
senses.definition: to test an earlier judgement against what actually happened
senses.definitionCN: 用实际发生的事情检验先前的判断
senses.example: The theory was reassessed after the second experiment failed.
senses.exampleCN: 第二次实验失败之后，这个理论被重新评估。
senses.why: The sense links review to evidence rather than to mood.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项把复查连到证据，而不是情绪。

senses.title: To reassess a person's worth
senses.titleCN: 重新掂量一个人的价值
senses.definition: to revise what someone is owed in respect or payment
senses.definitionCN: 修改某人在尊重或报酬上应得的部分
senses.example: The company reassessed her worth after she saved the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 她救下那份合同之后，公司重新掂量了她的价值。
senses.why: The word can carry a cold accounting of people.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能带着对人的冷账。

senses.title: Versus reevaluate
senses.definition: to judge anew in practical terms, as opposed to weighing values
senses.definitionCN: 以实际尺度重新判断，与权衡价值相对
senses.example: Managers reassess a budget; philosophers reevaluate a principle.
senses.exampleCN: 经理重新评估预算，哲学家重新衡量原则。
senses.why: The pair separates the ledger from the value.
senses.whyCN: 这一对词把账本与价值分开。

intro.en: Reassess is re-, 'again', plus assess, from Latin assidere, 'to sit beside', the image of a judge sitting by the accused.
intro.cn: reassess 是 re-（再次）加 assess，assess 来自拉丁语 assidere（坐在旁边），原指法官坐在被告身旁。

items.en: Assidere meant to sit beside, especially as an assistant judge.
items.cn: assidere 意为坐在旁边，尤指作为陪审法官。

items.en: Assess became to fix a value or a tax.
items.cn: assess 变成确定价值或税额。

items.en: The prefix adds a second sitting of the same court.
items.cn: 前缀加上同一法庭的第二次开庭。

items.en: Business made reassessment a routine step.
items.cn: 商业把重新评估变成例行步骤。

items.en: Today it covers risk, priorities and personal worth.
items.cn: 今天它覆盖风险、轻重缓急与个人价值。

note.en: The look-alike group is the assess- family; the near-meaning group separates reevaluate, reconsider, review and reappraise.
note.cn: 形近组是 assess 词族；近义组把「重新评价」「重新考虑」「复查」「重新估价」分开。

entries.definition: to fix the value of something.
entries.definitionCN: 确定某物的价值。

entries.definition: a judgement of value or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 对价值或质量的判断。

entries.definition: a second judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 第二次判断。

entries.definition: something of value that is owned.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有的有价值之物。

entries.definition: to weigh values again.
entries.definitionCN: 重新权衡价值。

entries.definition: to think a decision over again.
entries.definitionCN: 重新考虑一个决定。

entries.definition: to examine something again.
entries.definitionCN: 再次检查某事。

entries.definition: to set a new price or value.
entries.definitionCN: 重新定价或估值。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a judge sitting down a second time beside a case already heard.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「法官在一桩已审过的案子旁边第二次坐下」的画面。

normal.en: Reassess is re plus assess: the court sits again.
normal.cn: reassess 是 re 加 assess：法庭再开一次庭。

normal.en: Picture old papers pushed aside and a fresh page lifted.
normal.cn: 想象旧报表被推到一边，新的一页被拿起。

normal.en: Say ree-uh-SESS; the stress sits on SESS.
normal.cn: 读 ree-uh-SESS，重音在 SESS。

normal.en: The word is not doubt for its own sake; it follows new evidence.
normal.cn: 这个词不是为怀疑而怀疑；它跟着新证据来。

normal.en: Ask what changed since the first judgement.
normal.cn: 问一句：第一次判断之后，什么变了？

abstract.en: To reassess is to admit that a judgement has a date on it.
abstract.cn: 重新评估就是承认判断上都印着日期。

abstract.en: The word keeps the courtroom image: value is decided by someone sitting in authority.
abstract.cn: 这个词保留法庭意象：价值由某个坐在权威位置上的人决定。

abstract.en: Reassessment is cheapest before the cost of being wrong arrives.
abstract.cn: 在错误的代价到来之前，重新评估最便宜。

examples.en: The bank reassessed the risk of the loan after the audit.
examples.cn: 审计之后，银行重新评估了这笔贷款的风险。

examples.en: The board reassessed its decision when the costs doubled.
examples.cn: 成本翻倍之后，董事会重新考虑了它的决定。

examples.en: After the illness he reassessed his priorities in a single afternoon.
examples.cn: 病后他在一个下午之内重新排定了自己的轻重缓急。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（再）+ assess（坐在旁边定价）→ 再坐一次，重新定值。

root: 拉丁语 assidere（坐在旁边）→ assess + re-（再次）

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses re-open a judgement: a plan, a risk, a decision, priorities, a situation, results, a person's worth and the line to reevaluate.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在重开一次判断：计划、风险、决定、轻重缓急、局势、结果、一个人的价值，以及与 reevaluate 的界线。

core.en: A SECOND SITTING BY THE SAME CASE
core.cn: 在同一案子旁第二次坐下

branches.en: A plan and a private order of importance.
branches.cn: 计划与私人的重要性次序。

branches.en: Risk in money and risk in events.
branches.cn: 金钱上的风险与事态中的风险。

branches.en: A settled choice reopened by evidence.
branches.cn: 被证据重新打开的定案。

branches.en: The cold accounting of a person.
branches.cn: 对人的一笔冷账。

branches.en: Practical judgement against value judgement.
branches.cn: 实际判断与价值判断相对。

intro.en: The assess- family is a courtroom vocabulary turned commercial: assess, assessment, reassess and reassessment all fix a value.
intro.cn: assess 词族是从法庭词汇变成商业词汇：assess、assessment、reassess、reassessment 都在确定价值。

latinIntro.en: Latin assidere gives assess; the re- prefix simply asks the same judges to sit again.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 assidere 给出 assess；re- 前缀只是请同一批法官再坐一次。

items.exampleCN: 一个正在重新评估的委员会。

items.exampleCN: 一次全面的重新评估。

items.example: Assess the damage.
items.exampleCN: 评估损失。
