definition_zh: 牧人；畜群看管者；牧场雇工；宗教比喻中的牧养者
definition_en: a person who watches over and drives a herd of animals, either for a family or for an employer
core_image: 一个裹着旧毯子的人坐在羊栏边的石头上，手里的牧杖横在膝上，眼睛跟着每一只走动的羊。
scene: 夜里风大，羊栏边的石头上坐着一个人，牧杖横放膝头，眼睛跟着每一只羊。 An old herdsman watched the flock while the others slept.
sceneCN: 这里 herdsman 指「看管并驱赶畜群的牧人」（第 1 个义项：以照看一群牲畜为职责的人）；句意为一位老牧人在其他人睡着时看守羊群。可辨识物件：羊栏、石头、牧杖、旧毯子、羊群。

pos.zh: 牧人；畜群看管者；（比喻）牧养者

derivatives.zh: 古英语 heord（畜群）→ 由「一群牲畜」转为「把牲畜聚成一群」
herd + -er（施事后缀）→ 牧人，语义偏重日常照看者
herdsman 的 man 换为 woman → 女牧人，语义仅改性别
herdsman + -ship（技艺或身份后缀）→ 牧放的本领与职责，语义由人转为能力
herd + -ing（动作名词后缀）→ 放牧这项劳动，语义由人转为活动

senses.title: A person who watches a herd
senses.definition: a person whose job is to keep a group of animals together and safe while they feed
senses.definitionCN: 职责是在牲畜吃草时把它们聚在一起并保其安全的人
senses.example: An old herdsman watched the flock while the others slept.
senses.exampleCN: 一位老牧人在其他人睡着时看守羊群。
senses.why: herd plus man simply names the person attached to the herd, so the basic sense is the keeper himself.
senses.whyCN: herd 加 man 直接指与畜群相连的人，因此最基本的义项就是看管者本人。

senses.title: Hired labour on a ranch
senses.definition: a paid worker who tends stock on land owned by someone else
senses.definitionCN: 在他人所有的土地上照看牲畜、领取报酬的工人
senses.example: The ranch hired two herdsmen for the lambing season.
senses.exampleCN: 牧场在产羔季雇了两名牧工。
senses.why: once herding became wage work, the title split off from the owner and named the employee.
senses.whyCN: 一旦放牧变成雇佣劳动，这个称呼就与所有者分开，用来指受雇者。

senses.title: A keeper of one kind of animal
senses.definition: a specialist who tends a single species, such as cattle, goats or camels
senses.definitionCN: 只照看一种牲畜的专门人员，如牛、山羊或骆驼
senses.example: The cattle herdsman knew which cow would calve first.
senses.exampleCN: 牛倌知道哪头母牛会先产犊。
senses.why: where a village keeps several species, the work divides, and the title takes the animal's name in front.
senses.whyCN: 当村庄饲养数种牲畜时，工作会分门，称呼就在前面加上牲畜之名。

senses.title: Owner or manager of stock
senses.titleCN: 牲畜的所有者或管理者
senses.definition: in older usage, the person who owns or directs the herd rather than only tending it
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，指拥有或支配畜群的人，而不只是照看者
senses.example: The herdsman whose brand marked the cattle also decided where they grazed.
senses.exampleCN: 给牛打上烙印的畜主也决定它们去哪里吃草。
senses.why: before specialised labour, the keeper and the owner were often the same man, and the word covered both.
senses.whyCN: 在分工之前，看管者与所有者常是同一个人，这个词因而兼指两者。

senses.title: A religious figure who tends souls
senses.definition: a minister pictured as a shepherd guiding and protecting a congregation
senses.definitionCN: 被比作牧羊人、引导并保护会众的宗教人员
senses.example: The sermon called every pastor a herdsman of people, not of sheep.
senses.exampleCN: 布道把每位牧师称为人的牧人，而不是羊的牧人。
senses.why: the Bible uses shepherd imagery for leaders, and English sermons carried that imagery into herdsman language.
senses.whyCN: 《圣经》用牧羊人的形象指领导者，英语布道把这一形象带进了 herdsman 的说法。

senses.title: An archetype in myth and literature
senses.titleCN: 神话与文学中的牧人原型
senses.definition: the stock figure of the lonely keeper, often a guide, a singer or a witness in stories
senses.definitionCN: 故事中孤独看管者的定型形象，常充当引路人、歌者或见证者
senses.example: In the legend the herdsman is the only one who sees the stranger arrive.
senses.exampleCN: 传说中，牧人是唯一看见陌生人到来的人。
senses.why: a keeper who sits through the night sees what sleeping villages miss, so stories place him at the edge of events.
senses.whyCN: 守夜的人看见睡着的村庄看不见的事，因此故事把他放在事件的边缘。

senses.title: One who guides a crowd
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：带领并照看一群人的人
senses.definition: a leader described as keeping a group together and moving it safely, with a hint of care
senses.definitionCN: 被描述为把一群人聚住并安全带走的人，含照料意味
senses.example: The strike leader acted as a herdsman for two hundred frightened workers.
senses.exampleCN: 罢工领袖像牧人一样带着两百名惊恐的工人。
senses.why: guiding people and guiding animals share the same gestures, so the farm title transfers with its protective tone.
senses.whyCN: 带人和带牲畜的手势相同，因此这个农场称呼连同其保护口吻一起转移过来。

senses.title: Any keeper of a dependent group
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何照料并引导一群对象的人
senses.definition: anyone responsible for keeping a dependent collection together, whether animals, people or data
senses.definitionCN: 负责把一群依赖性的对象聚住并照看的任何人，无论对象是牲畜、人还是数据
senses.example: The archive's herdsman kept ten thousand files from drifting apart.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆的看管人让一万份文件不致散失。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps only the role: something scattered needs one person who holds it together.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只保留角色本身：散开的东西需要一个把它们聚住的人。

intro.en: Herdsman is an English compound of herd and man, with a genitive -s between them. Both parts are Old English and Germanic; no Latin element is involved.
intro.cn: herdsman 是 herd 与 man 的英语复合词，中间有属格 -s。两部分都属古英语与日耳曼语，不含拉丁成分。

items.en: Heord 'group of animals' is the first element; its Germanic shape is reconstructed, and the exact wider Indo-European link is disputed.
items.cn: heord「一群牲畜」是第一部分；其日耳曼语形式属重构，更广的印欧联系有争议。

items.en: Man meant 'human being, person' and still did when the compound formed; the modern restriction to an adult male came later.
items.cn: man 意为「人、人类」，复合词形成时仍是此义；后来才收窄为成年男性。

items.en: The -s is the old genitive ending, so herdsman originally meant 'the herd's man', the man belonging to the herd.
items.cn: 这个 -s 是古属格词尾，因此 herdsman 原意是「畜群的人」，即属于这群牲畜的人。

items.en: Middle English herdesman kept the compound for a professional keeper, alongside the shorter herd and herder.
items.cn: 中古英语 herdesman 保留了这个复合词，指职业看管者，同时还有更短的 herd 与 herder。

items.en: From the sixteenth century English sermons applied shepherd and herdsman imagery to clergy, adding the figurative sense.
items.cn: 从 16 世纪起，英语布道把牧羊人与牧人的形象用于神职人员，增添了比喻义。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the precise first written appearance of the compound is not fixed, and the pre-Germanic origin of heord remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个复合词确切的首次书面出现并无定说，heord 在日耳曼语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds titles from the same herding stock that differ only in formality or gender; group two holds words for people who look after animals or people.
note.cn: 第一组是同出放牧词源、只在正式程度或性别上不同的称呼；第二组是照看动物或照看人的邻近词。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a keeper of animals, formed with -er; herdsman is the older, more formal title.
entries.definitionCN: 指牲畜看管者的日常词，由 -er 构成；herdsman 是更古老、更正式的称呼。

entries.definition: The animals themselves, or the verb for driving them; it never names the keeper.
entries.definitionCN: 指牲畜本身，或指驱赶它们的动词，从不指看管者。

entries.definition: The same job with woman in place of man; the plural is herdswomen.
entries.definitionCN: 同一职业，把 man 换成 woman；复数为 herdswomen。

entries.definition: From sheep plus hierde 'herder', so it is a compound of a different animal and an older agent noun, not a variant of herdsman.
entries.definitionCN: 由 sheep 加 hierde「牧人」构成，是另一种牲畜与更古老施事名词的复合，并非 herdsman 的变体。

entries.definition: A rider who works cattle on open range; the word stresses horses and driving rather than daily watching.
entries.definitionCN: 在开阔牧场上骑马管牛的人；这个词强调马与驱赶，而非日常看管。

entries.definition: A farm worker who handles livestock; it is an agricultural job title rather than a cultural one.
entries.definitionCN: 料理牲畜的农场工人；它是农业职称，而非文化称呼。

entries.definition: A minister; its literal shepherd sense is historical, while herdsman keeps the animal sense alive.
entries.definitionCN: 牧师；其字面的牧人义已属历史，而 herdsman 仍保留牲畜义。

entries.definition: The owner or manager of a ranch; herdsman names the person who does the daily watching.
entries.definitionCN: 牧场所有者或经营者；herdsman 指做日常看管的人。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real genitive compound, real relatives and real occupational phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的属格复合、真实同族词与真实职业搭配。

normal.en: herd + genitive -s + man: literally 'the herd's man'.
normal.cn: herd + 属格 -s + man：字面就是「畜群的人」。

normal.en: The family runs herd, herder, herding, herdsman, herdswoman, herdsmanship.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 herd、herder、herding、herdsman、herdswoman、herdsmanship。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the job: a cattle herdsman, a nomadic herdsman, the herdsman's staff.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这一职业：牛倌、游牧牧人、牧人的杖。

normal.en: Shepherd is a parallel compound, sheep plus the older agent noun hierde.
normal.cn: shepherd 是平行复合词，由 sheep 加更古老的施事名词 hierde 构成。

normal.en: The irregular plural herdsmen keeps the old genitive sound.
normal.cn: 不规则复数 herdsmen 保留了古属格的读音。

abstract.en: Picture one man awake at night so that a hundred animals can sleep standing up.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人夜里不睡，好让一百头牲畜能站着睡。

abstract.en: Picture a staff laid across a lap, doubling as a seat and a counting tool.
abstract.cn: 想象一根杖横在膝上，既是坐处也是数数的工具。

abstract.en: Picture a leader who walks behind the crowd so that no one is left at the edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一位带头人走在人群后面，好让边上没人被落下。

examples.en: The herdsman could name every animal in the flock by its markings.
examples.cn: 牧人能凭毛色花纹叫出羊群里每一只的名字。

examples.en: Wages for a herdsman are low, but the work comes with milk and wool.
examples.cn: 牧人的工资不高，但这活附带奶和羊毛。

examples.en: Novels often give the herdsman a song and no other possession.
examples.cn: 小说常给牧人一首歌，别的财产一概不给。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「herds（畜群）+ man（人）」——属于畜群的那个人 → 牧人、看管者

root: 古英语 heord「一群牲畜」+ 属格 -s + man「人」，字面为「畜群的人」；两部分皆属日耳曼语系，无拉丁成分。英语 herdsman。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one role: a person attached to a herd. The role is then read as a hired worker, a species specialist, an owner, a pastor, a mythic figure, a guide of people and finally any keeper of a dependent group.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个角色展开：一个属于畜群的人。这个角色再依次被读作雇工、单一畜种的专人、畜主、牧养者、神话人物、人群的引导者，最后读作任何依赖群体的看管者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person awake at the edge of a sleeping flock.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人醒着，守在一群睡着的牲畜旁边。

branches.en: KEEPER AND OWNER: the same title covers the man who watches and the man whose brand the animals carry.
branches.cn: 看管者与所有者：同一个称呼既指看羊的人，也指牲畜身上打着他烙印的人。

branches.en: DIVIDED LABOUR: hired hands and single-species specialists appear once herds grow beyond one family.
branches.cn: 分工：当畜群超过一户人家能管的规模，雇工与单一畜种的专人就出现了。

branches.en: SOULS AND STORIES: the night watcher becomes a pastor in sermons and a witness in legends.
branches.cn: 灵魂与故事：守夜人在布道里成了牧养者，在传说里成了见证者。

branches.en: GUIDE OF PEOPLE: the protective gestures of herding transfer to a leader of a crowd.
branches.cn: 人的引导者：放牧中保护性的手势转移到带领人群的人身上。

branches.en: ANY DEPENDENT GROUP: keep only the role, and files or data can need a keeper too.
branches.cn: 任何依赖群体：只保留角色，文件或数据也可以需要一个看管者。

intro.en: Herdsman is a two-part English compound with an old genitive ending; no Latin prefix or root takes part.
intro.cn: herdsman 是由两部分构成的英语复合词，中间带古属格词尾，不含拉丁前缀或词根。

latinIntro.en: This line has no Latin relative, so the Latin list is left empty; the parts are Old English and Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这一词线没有拉丁同族词，因此拉丁列表留空；各成分属古英语与日耳曼语。

items.example: The first element names the animals.
items.exampleCN: 第一部分指那群牲畜。

items.example: The older agent noun also survives inside shepherd.
items.exampleCN: 更古老的施事名词也残留在 shepherd 里。

items.example: The second element names the person, not the sex.
items.exampleCN: 第二部分指人，而不是指性别。

items.example: The ending makes herdsman literally 'the herd's man'.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾使 herdsman 字面成为「畜群的人」。

items.meaning: a group of animals; to drive them
items.example: The herd moved down the valley.
items.exampleCN: 畜群沿着山谷下行。

items.example: The herder carried no staff.
items.exampleCN: 这位牧人没有带杖。

items.example: Herdsman plus -ship yields herdsmanship.
items.exampleCN: herdsman 加 -ship 得出 herdsmanship。

items.meaning: the skill and duty of tending stock
items.example: Herdsmanship was judged by the winter survival rate.
items.exampleCN: 放牧本领以越冬存活率来评判。

items.example: The herdswoman kept the sick lambs indoors.
items.exampleCN: 女牧人把病羔留在室内。

definition_zh: 创业；创业精神；创办事业的活动与本领；创业学
definition_en: the activity, skill or spirit of starting and running new businesses
core_image: 一间空铺面里，几个学生把货架摆好，门上还挂着刚写的营业牌
scene: 这所职业学校把创业课直接开在街边的真实铺面里。 At this vocational school, the entrepreneurship course runs inside a real shop on the street.
sceneCN: 这所职业学校把创业课直接开在街边的真实铺面里；句中的 entrepreneurship 指「以创办与经营新事业为内容的教学领域」（第 4 个义项：创业学、创业课程）。图中可辨识物件：货架、营业牌、收银盒、学生笔记本。

pos.zh: 创业；创业精神；创业本领；创业学

senses.title: The activity of starting ventures
senses.definition: the activity of identifying an opportunity and building a new business around it
senses.definitionCN: 发现机会并围绕它建立新企业的活动
senses.example: The region's growth was driven by quiet entrepreneurship in small towns.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的增长由小城镇里低调的创业活动推动。
senses.why: The suffix turns the person into a practice: what the undertaker does, repeated across a society, becomes an activity.
senses.whyCN: 后缀把「人」变成「实践」：承担者所做的事，在一个社会里反复发生，就成了活动。

senses.title: The spirit of initiative and risk
senses.titleCN: 创业精神；敢闯敢试的态度
senses.definition: the attitude that welcomes initiative, experiment and the risk of failure
senses.definitionCN: 欢迎主动、试验并接受失败风险的态度
senses.example: The prize honours entrepreneurship as much as profit.
senses.exampleCN: 这个奖项看重创业精神，不亚于看重利润。
senses.why: A practice also becomes a disposition, so the word names the willingness to undertake things at all.
senses.whyCN: 实践也会成为一种性情，因此这个词也指「愿意承担事情」的意愿。

senses.title: The skill of building a business
senses.titleCN: 创业本领；经营新事业的能力
senses.definition: the practical ability to spot a market, raise resources and keep a new firm going
senses.definitionCN: 发现市场、筹集资源并让新企业存活的实际能力
senses.example: She learned entrepreneurship by running the stall for two summers.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠两个夏天守摊学会了创业本领。
senses.why: What begins as an activity is also something one can be good at, so the word shifts from doing to skill.
senses.whyCN: 开始时指活动，也可以指擅长的本事，因此这个词从「做」转向「能力」。

senses.title: The academic field that studies it
senses.titleCN: 创业学；创业课程与研究领域
senses.definition: the university subject that studies how ventures are created, financed and grown
senses.definitionCN: 研究事业如何被创造、筹资与成长的高校学科
senses.example: At this vocational school, the entrepreneurship course runs inside a real shop on the street.
senses.exampleCN: 这所职业学校把创业课直接开在街边的真实铺面里。
senses.why: Once a practice is studied and taught, its name attaches to the department and the course.
senses.whyCN: 一种实践被研究与教授之后，它的名称就挂到系所与课程上。

senses.title: The surrounding ecosystem
senses.titleCN: 创业生态；支撑创业的环境
senses.definition: the network of finance, mentors, rules and customers that lets ventures start and scale
senses.definitionCN: 让事业得以启动与扩张的资金、导师、规则与客户网络
senses.example: Cheap loans and open data built a lively entrepreneurship in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价贷款与开放数据在这座城市培育出活跃的创业生态。
senses.why: Individual ventures depend on shared conditions, so the practice is also named as a surrounding system.
senses.whyCN: 单个事业依赖共同条件，因此这种实践也被命名为一个环绕的系统。

senses.title: Venturing for a social goal
senses.titleCN: 社会创业；以社会目标为导向的创业
senses.definition: the practice of building enterprises whose main aim is social or environmental benefit
senses.definitionCN: 建立以社会或环境效益为主要目标的企业实践
senses.example: Social entrepreneurship has brought cheap spectacles to rural clinics.
senses.exampleCN: 社会创业让乡村诊所有了便宜的眼镜。
senses.why: The undertaking can serve a public purpose, so a modifier marks the goal rather than the method.
senses.whyCN: 承担之事可以服务公共目的，于是用修饰语标出目标而非方法。

senses.title: Venturing inside an existing firm
senses.titleCN: 机构内创业；企业内部创新
senses.definition: the practice of starting new projects with an owner's freedom inside an established organization
senses.definitionCN: 在既有组织内部以创办者的自由启动新项目的实践
senses.example: The group encourages intrapreneurship among its engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 该集团鼓励工程师进行机构内创业。
senses.why: The undertaking does not need a new company, so a variant word marks the same act performed inside one.
senses.whyCN: 承担事业并不需要新公司，因此一个变体词标记在同一家公司内部完成的同一动作。

senses.title: The measured rate of new ventures
senses.titleCN: 创业率；创业活动的总量指标
senses.definition: the statistical level of new business formation in an economy or region
senses.definitionCN: 一个经济体或地区新企业形成的统计水平
senses.example: Surveys now track entrepreneurship as a share of the workforce.
senses.exampleCN: 调查如今把创业率作为劳动人口的一个比重来追踪。
senses.why: Governments need to count what they wish to encourage, so the practice becomes a statistic.
senses.whyCN: 政府需要数清自己想要鼓励的东西，于是这种实践变成一个统计量。

intro.en: Entrepreneurship is entrepreneur plus the English suffix -ship, from Old English -scipe 'state, condition'. The word is a modern formation, spread by economics and business schools. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: entrepreneurship 是 entrepreneur 加英语后缀 -ship 构成，后者源自古英语 -scipe「状态、情形」。这个词是近代构词，由经济学与商学院推广开来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Entrepreneur, 'one who undertakes', came from entreprendre 'to take in hand', built on Latin prehendere 'to grasp'.
items.cn: entrepreneur「承担者」来自 entreprendre「着手、承担」，由拉丁 prehendere「抓住」构成。

items.en: The suffix -scipe named a state or condition and survives in friendship, hardship and leadership; it turns a person into a practice or role.
items.cn: 后缀 -scipe 表示状态或情形，保留在 friendship、hardship 与 leadership 中；它把「人」变成实践或身份。

items.en: English joined the two elements to name the activity of the entrepreneur, at first in economic writing about production and risk.
items.cn: 英语把两个成分合起来，命名企业家所从事的活动，最初见于关于生产与风险的经济论述。

items.en: Twentieth-century business schools made the word a subject with courses, journals and textbooks.
items.cn: 二十世纪的商学院使这个词成为一门有课程、期刊与教科书的学科。

items.en: Governments began to measure and promote entrepreneurship, and the word acquired a statistical sense.
items.cn: 各国政府开始测量并促进创业，这个词于是取得统计义。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same word; group two holds wider words for the activity of building something new.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词的各种形式；第二组是表示「开创新事物」这一活动的更宽泛的词。

entries.definition: The undertaker himself or herself; the practice noun adds the activity around that person.
entries.definitionCN: 指承担者本人；这个实践名词加上的是围绕那个人的活动。

entries.definition: An adjective for the outlook or style, not the field of study or the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指那种眼光或风格，不指学科领域或活动。

entries.definition: Simply more than one founder; it counts people rather than practice.
entries.definitionCN: 只是不止一位创办者；数的是人，不是实践。

entries.definition: The same practice carried out inside an existing organization, marked by a prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 同一实践在既有组织内部进行，由前缀标出场景。

entries.definition: A firm, a project or the general drive to undertake things; broader and less technical than entrepreneurship.
entries.definitionCN: 指企业、项目或承担事情的劲头；比 entrepreneurship 更宽、更不技术化。

entries.definition: A single commercial project with risk attached; entrepreneurship is the whole practice of making such projects.
entries.definitionCN: 指单独一个有风险的商业项目；entrepreneurship 是制造这类项目的整体实践。

entries.definition: The readiness to act first without being told; it is a personal quality, not a field of activity.
entries.definitionCN: 指无需吩咐就先行行动的意愿；是个人品质，不是活动领域。

entries.definition: The introduction of something new; it can happen inside a firm and need not involve founding one.
entries.definitionCN: 指引入新事物；可在企业内部发生，不必创办企业。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: Entrepreneur plus the state suffix: the condition of being one who undertakes.
normal.cn: entrepreneur 加状态后缀：身为承担者的状态。

normal.en: The family runs entrepreneur, entrepreneurial, entrepreneurship and intrapreneurship.
normal.cn: 同族词有 entrepreneur、entrepreneurial、entrepreneurship 与 intrapreneurship。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: a course in entrepreneurship, social entrepreneurship, a culture of entrepreneurship.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出各义项：创业课程、社会创业、创业文化。

normal.en: The suffix also builds friendship and leadership, all states or roles.
normal.cn: 同一后缀还构成 friendship 与 leadership，都表示状态或身份。

normal.en: Economics measures it as a rate, schools teach it as a subject.
normal.cn: 经济学把它当比率来测量，学校把它当学科来教授。

abstract.en: Picture an empty shop that fills with shelves before the sign is painted.
abstract.cn: 想象一间空铺面，招牌还没刷，货架已经摆满。

abstract.en: Picture a classroom whose desks are replaced by a counter and a cash box.
abstract.cn: 想象一间教室，课桌换成了柜台与钱箱。

abstract.en: Picture a small flame passed from one candle to the next along a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一簇火苗沿着桌面从一根蜡烛传到下一根。

examples.en: The foundation runs workshops on entrepreneurship for teenagers.
examples.cn: 该基金会为青少年举办创业工作坊。

examples.en: Social entrepreneurship attracts graduates who want measurable impact.
examples.cn: 社会创业吸引希望看到可衡量影响的毕业生。

examples.en: Low barriers to registration are linked to higher entrepreneurship.
examples.cn: 较低的注册门槛与更高的创业率相关。

dict_mnemonic.text: 空铺面先装货架，招牌后刷 → 创业

root: 英语构词：entrepreneur（法语「承担者」，出自拉丁 prehendere「抓住」）+ 古英语后缀 -ship（状态、身份）；指创办与经营新事业的活动、精神与学科。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one practice: the activity, the spirit, the skill, the academic field, the ecosystem, the social variant, the in-house variant, and the statistical rate.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一种实践：活动、精神、本领、学科、生态、社会版本、机构内版本，以及统计上的比率。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty shop being fitted with shelves before the sign is painted.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间空铺面正在装货架，招牌还没刷。

branches.en: DOING AND BEING ABLE: the activity and the skill are the same practice seen from outside and inside.
branches.cn: 做与能做：活动与本领，是同一实践从外部和内部看到的两种样子。

branches.en: DISPOSITION: the willingness to undertake becomes a character trait.
branches.cn: 性情：愿意承担事情的意愿成为一种性格。

branches.en: TAUGHT AND SUPPORTED: a subject in a classroom and an ecosystem of finance and mentors both surround the practice.
branches.cn: 被教授与被支撑：课堂里的学科与资金导师构成的生态，都环绕着这种实践。

branches.en: TWO DIRECTIONS: the same undertaking can aim at a public good or happen inside an existing firm.
branches.cn: 两个方向：同样的承担可以指向公共利益，也可以发生在既有企业内部。

branches.en: COUNTED: what is encouraged must be measured, so the practice becomes a rate.
branches.cn: 被计数：被鼓励的东西必须被测量，于是这种实践变成一个比率。

intro.en: Entrepreneurship joins a French agent noun to an Old English state suffix, so it mixes two language layers.
intro.cn: entrepreneurship 把法语施事名词与古英语状态后缀接在一起，因此混合了两个语言层。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is prehendere 'to grasp'; the suffix layer is Old English -scipe, seen in friendship and leadership.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 prehendere「抓住」；后缀层是古英语 -scipe，见于 friendship 与 leadership。

items.example: The root pictures a hand closing on a task.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根描绘一只手合拢抓住任务。

items.example: The verb means to take a task in hand.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词意为把任务接到手里。

items.example: The entrepreneur opened a laundry.
items.exampleCN: 这位创业者开了一家洗衣店。

items.example: The team had an entrepreneurial style.
items.exampleCN: 这个团队有创业风格。

items.example: The school teaches entrepreneurship.
items.exampleCN: 这所学校教授创业。

items.example: The suffix also builds leadership.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀还构成 leadership。

items.example: The lab supports intrapreneurship.
items.exampleCN: 该实验室支持机构内创业。

items.meaningCN: 以社会目标为导向的创业
items.example: Social entrepreneurship funded the clinic.
items.exampleCN: 社会创业为诊所提供了资金。

definition_zh: 畜牧的；牧羊的；田园的；牧歌式的；牧师的；田园诗
definition_en: relating to shepherds or country life, or to the care of a religious congregation
core_image: 一道石墙围着草坡，羊群散在墙内，墙外的城市只剩一条模糊的边
scene: 清晨的坡地上羊群散开， A pastoral valley keeps its shepherds and its dry stone walls.
sceneCN: 这里 pastoral 指「与牧羊、畜牧相关的」（第 1 个义项：畜牧的）；句意为这座牧歌式的山谷仍保留着牧人与干砌石墙。图中可辨识物件：干砌石墙、羊群、牧杖、远处城市的轮廓。

pos.zh: 畜牧的；田园的；牧歌式的；牧灵的
田园诗；牧歌

senses.title: Relating to sheep and cattle farming
senses.definition: concerned with the grazing of livestock rather than with crops
senses.definitionCN: 与放牧牲畜有关，而非与种植作物有关
senses.example: Pastoral land here is too dry for wheat and too steep for ploughs.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的牧地太干种不了麦，太陡使不了犁。
senses.why: pastor is Latin for shepherd, so the first sense is the working sense: everything to do with grazing animals.
senses.whyCN: pastor 是拉丁语「牧人」，因此第一个义项是干活的义：一切与放牧牲畜有关的事。

senses.title: An idealised countryside
senses.definition: describing a peaceful rural scene imagined as simple and harmonious
senses.definitionCN: 形容被想象为朴素和谐的宁静乡野景象
senses.example: The brochure sells a pastoral image of village life.
senses.exampleCN: 宣传册贩卖一种田园式的乡村生活形象。
senses.why: town writers looked at herding country and saw peace, so the working word acquired a glow it did not have for the herders.
senses.whyCN: 城里的写作者看着牧区，看到了安宁，于是这个干活用的词多了一层牧人自己感受不到的光晕。

senses.title: A literary and artistic mode
senses.titleCN: 文学与艺术中的牧歌体裁
senses.definition: belonging to poems, plays, music or paintings that treat shepherd life as a theme
senses.definitionCN: 属于以牧人生活为主题的诗歌、戏剧、音乐或绘画
senses.example: The pastoral tradition puts shepherds into a golden weather that never rains.
senses.exampleCN: 牧歌传统把牧人放进一个从不下雨的金色天气里。
senses.why: the idealised countryside became a genre with set conventions, and the adjective names the genre.
senses.whyCN: 理想化的乡野变成有固定套路的体裁，形容词便用来命名这一体裁。

senses.title: Care of a congregation
senses.definition: in religion, relating to the guidance and care a minister gives to people
senses.definitionCN: 宗教中指牧师对人所给予的引导与照顾
senses.example: Pastoral care includes visiting the sick and the lonely.
senses.exampleCN: 牧灵关怀包括探访病人与孤独者。
senses.why: the Latin shepherd was applied to clergy, so the same adjective covers looking after a flock of people.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语「牧人」被用在神职人员身上，因此同一个形容词也指照料一群「羊」。

senses.title: A bishop's letter to the faithful
senses.definition: a formal letter from a bishop or church leader to the people of a diocese
senses.definitionCN: 主教或教会领袖写给教区信众的正式书信
senses.example: The pastoral letter asked parishes to shelter refugees.
senses.exampleCN: 这封牧函要求各堂区收容难民。
senses.why: a letter that shepherds the readers borrows the adjective of shepherding.
senses.whyCN: 一封「牧养」读者的信，借用了牧养的形容词。

senses.title: A grazing lease in Australian usage
senses.titleCN: 澳大利亚用法中的牧区租地
senses.definition: in Australia, land leased from the state for grazing livestock
senses.definitionCN: 澳大利亚指从国家租来放牧牲畜的土地
senses.example: The family held a pastoral lease of forty thousand hectares.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人持有一份四万公顷的牧区租地。
senses.why: Australian land law named vast dry grazing blocks pastoral, and the adjective became a legal category.
senses.whyCN: 澳大利亚土地法把大片干旱牧地称作 pastoral，形容词于是成了法律类别。

senses.title: Herding that moves with the seasons
senses.definition: describing a herding system that moves animals between seasonal pastures
senses.definitionCN: 形容在季节草场之间移动牲畜的畜牧制度
senses.example: Pastoral nomadism survives where fields cannot be irrigated.
senses.exampleCN: 在无法灌溉的地方，畜牧游牧仍然存续。
senses.why: the adjective combines with nomadism to name the oldest form of livestock keeping.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词与 nomadism 组合，用来命名最古老的养畜形式。

senses.title: A poem about shepherd life
senses.definition: a poem or musical piece in the shepherd convention
senses.definitionCN: 采用牧人套路的诗或乐曲
senses.example: He wrote three pastorals before he ever saw a sheep.
senses.exampleCN: 他还没见过一只羊，就写了三首牧歌。
senses.why: the adjective became a noun for the work itself, a common shift in the language of genres.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词变成指作品本身的名词，这在体裁语汇里很常见。

intro.en: Pastoral comes from Latin pastoralis, from pastor 'shepherd', built on pascere 'to feed, graze'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pastoral 出自拉丁 pastoralis，再上为 pastor「牧人」，建于 pascere「喂养、放牧」之上。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pascere meant 'to feed, graze'. Its deeper origin is not fully established; the usual link to a root meaning 'to feed' is reconstructed.
items.cn: pascere 意为「喂养、放牧」。其更深来源未有定论；通常与意为「喂养」的词根相联系，那属重构。

items.en: Pastor meant 'herdsman, shepherd', literally 'one who feeds'.
items.cn: pastor 意为「牧人、牧羊人」，字面是「喂养者」。

items.en: Pastoralis meant 'of a shepherd or of shepherding', used of songs, gifts and duties connected with herds.
items.cn: pastoralis 意为「牧人的、牧养的」，用于与牲畜相关的歌、礼物与职责。

items.en: The image of the shepherd was applied to clergy, so pastoral acquired the sense of caring for a congregation.
items.cn: 牧人的意象被用在神职人员身上，pastoral 因此获得「照料会众」的意思。

items.en: English poets of the sixteenth century took pastoral for the shepherd genre, and the idealised countryside followed.
items.cn: 16 世纪英语诗人用 pastoral 指牧歌体裁，理想化的乡野义随之而来。

items.en: Settler land law in Australia named large grazing leases pastoral; the legal sense is dated to the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 澳大利亚移民土地法把大片放牧租地称作 pastoral；这一法律义可定在 19 世纪。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin shepherd and grazing words; the second names the rural and literary qualities pastoral suggests.
note.cn: 第一组共用拉丁「牧人」「放牧」词；第二组是 pastoral 所暗示的田园与文学品质。

entries.definition: A minister or, literally, a shepherd; the noun for the person where pastoral is the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指牧师，字面为牧人；是指人的名词，pastoral 是对应的形容词。

entries.definition: Grassland used for grazing, or to graze it; it names the place or the act, not the style.
entries.definitionCN: 指用于放牧的草地，或放牧这块地；指地点或动作，而非风格。

entries.definition: The branch of farming based on grazing herds; a noun for the economy, not an adjective for a scene.
entries.definitionCN: 指以放牧畜群为基础的农业分支；是经济的名词，不是景象的形容词。

entries.definition: A person who keeps grazing livestock; the human noun, not the literary genre.
entries.definitionCN: 指养放牧牲畜的人；是指人的名词，不是文学体裁。

entries.definition: Charmingly rural in a literary way, from Greek for a herdsman; it is almost always a stylistic word.
entries.definitionCN: 指带文学味的迷人乡野，出自希腊语「牧人」；几乎总是风格用词。

entries.definition: Describing a scene of perfect peace and simplicity; it can apply to any place, not only herding country.
entries.definitionCN: 形容完美宁静朴素的景象；可用于任何地方，不限牧区。

entries.definition: Of the countryside; a neutral word with no idealisation and no herds.
entries.definitionCN: 指乡下的；中性词，不含理想化，也不含畜群。

entries.definition: Relating to land ownership or farming, usually crops; it is about tenure and production, not scenery.
entries.definitionCN: 指与土地所有权或农耕（通常指作物）相关的；讲的是权属与生产，不是风景。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin grazing verb, the family it built and the double life of the word in church and literature.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁「放牧」动词、它构成的词族，以及这个词在教会与文学中的双重生活。

normal.en: pascere 'to graze' + -tor 'one who' = pastor, a feeder of animals; pastoral is its adjective.
normal.cn: pascere「放牧」+ -tor「做……的人」= pastor，喂养牲畜的人；pastoral 是其形容词。

normal.en: The family runs pastor, pasture, pastoral, pastoralism and pastoralist.
normal.cn: 词族包括 pastor、pasture、pastoral、pastoralism、pastoralist。

normal.en: The church sense keeps the sheep metaphor: pastoral care, pastoral letter, pastoral visit.
normal.cn: 教会义保留羊的比喻：牧灵关怀、牧函、牧灵探访。

normal.en: The literary sense keeps the golden weather: pastoral poetry, pastoral scene, pastoral elegy.
normal.cn: 文学义保留金色天气：田园诗、田园场景、田园挽歌。

normal.en: In Australia a pastoral lease is a legal category of grazing land.
normal.cn: 在澳大利亚，「牧区租约」是放牧土地的一个法律类别。

abstract.en: Picture a stone wall that exists only to keep sheep in and the city out.
abstract.cn: 想象一道石墙，唯一的作用是把羊拦住、把城市挡在外面。

abstract.en: Picture a shepherd's crook that is also a bishop's staff.
abstract.cn: 想象一根牧羊杖，同时也是主教的手杖。

abstract.en: Picture a poem written about a field the poet has never walked.
abstract.cn: 想象一首诗写的是诗人从未走过的田野。

examples.en: The region shifted from pastoral use to irrigated horticulture.
examples.cn: 该地区从畜牧用地转为灌溉园艺。

examples.en: Pastoral novels rarely mention the smell of a wet fleece.
examples.cn: 田园小说很少提到湿羊毛的气味。

examples.en: The bishop's pastoral letter was read from every pulpit.
examples.cn: 主教的牧函在每个讲道坛上被宣读。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「帕斯托罗」听成「怕石多罗」——坡上石头多，羊却偏要在石缝里找草，这就是牧羊的田园。pastor 是牧人，pastoral 是牧人的。

root: 拉丁 pastor「牧人」出自 pascere「喂养、放牧」，加 -alis 成 pastoralis「牧人的」；经法语进入英语。基督教把牧人意象用于神职，文学把它用于牧歌体裁，澳大利亚土地法把它用于牧区租地。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses divide between the working herd and the imagined countryside, then add church care, a bishop's letter, a grazing lease, seasonal herding and the poem itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分布在「干活的畜群」与「想象中的乡野」两侧，再加教会牧养、主教书信、牧区租地、季节畜牧与诗作本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dry stone wall holding sheep inside and the city outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道干砌石墙，把羊拦在里面，把城市挡在外面。

branches.en: WORKING HERD: settled pasture and seasonal movement are the two practical forms of the same grazing economy.
branches.cn: 干活的畜群：定居牧场与季节移动，是同一畜牧经济的两种实际形态。

branches.en: THE IMAGINED COUNTRY: the idealised scene, the genre and the poem are one literary construction at three stages.
branches.cn: 想象的乡野：理想景象、体裁与诗作，是同一文学建构的三个阶段。

branches.en: THE FLOCK OF PEOPLE: clergy inherit the shepherd image and care for a congregation instead of sheep.
branches.cn: 人的羊群：神职继承了牧人意象，照料的是会众而非羊。

branches.en: THE LETTER: a bishop writes to shepherd his readers.
branches.cn: 书信：主教写信以牧养他的读者。

branches.en: THE LEASE: colonial land law turns the adjective into a legal category of vast dry grazing blocks.
branches.cn: 租地：殖民地土地法把这个形容词变成大片干旱牧地的法律类别。

intro.en: Pastoral is a Latin noun of the shepherd plus a Latin adjective ending; the same stem also built pasture and pastor.
intro.cn: pastoral 是拉丁「牧人」名词加拉丁形容词词尾；同一词干还构成 pasture 与 pastor。

latinIntro.en: Latin pascere 'to graze' also gives pasture, repast and pabulum, all connected with feeding.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pascere「放牧」还给出 pasture、repast、pabulum，都与喂养有关。

items.example: The stem supplies the feeding image behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干提供整个词族背后的「喂养」意象。

items.example: The word moved from sheep to souls.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从羊群移到了灵魂。

items.example: The ending makes pastoralis 'of the shepherd'.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾构成 pastoralis「牧人的」。

items.example: Pastoral scenes filled the gallery.
items.exampleCN: 画廊里挂满了田园场景。

items.example: The herd moved to summer pasture.
items.exampleCN: 畜群转到夏季牧场。

items.meaning: a herding economy or its advocacy
items.example: Pastoralism shaped the region's law.
items.exampleCN: 畜牧经济塑造了该地区的法律。

items.example: Pastoralists moved before the rains.
items.exampleCN: 畜牧者在雨季前迁移。

items.meaning: in a rural or shepherd manner
items.example: The valley is pastorally quiet.
items.exampleCN: 这座山谷有田园式的安静。

items.example: The word literally meant feeding again.
items.exampleCN: 这个词字面意为「再喂一次」。

derivatives.meaning: the quality of being rural and calm

definition_zh: 外国市场；境外市场；他国需求与交易环境
definition_en: a market in a country other than one's own, seen from the standpoint of a home-based seller
core_image: 一道海关线把地图分成两半，本国的工厂在线的这一侧，线的另一侧是挂着不同旗子的店铺
scene: 出口部门的会议上，经理摊开地图，指着海外的几座城市说下一年要先去那里试销。 The team chose three foreign markets for the first year of sales.
sceneCN: 这里指「本国之外的市场」，对应第 1 个义项：相对于本国而言的其他国家市场；句意为团队选定了三个外国市场作为第一年的销售目标。画面要点：摊开的地图、海关线、不同旗帜的店铺标记。

pos.zh: 外国市场；境外市场（可数，复数 foreign markets）

derivatives.zh: 外国人（foreign 加表示人的后缀，语义从「境外的」转为「境外之人」）
陌生感；异域性（foreign 加名词后缀，指不属于本地的性质）
在国外出生的（foreign 加 born 构成的复合形容词）
市场；推销（短语的另一半，语义为交易场所或交易行为）
营销（market 加动名词后缀，语义从「市场」转为「开拓市场的工作」）

senses.title: A market outside one's own country
senses.definition: a market located in another country, considered in contrast to the home market
senses.definitionCN: 位于另一国的市场，与本国市场相对而言
senses.example: The team chose three foreign markets for the first year of sales.
senses.exampleCN: 团队选定了三个外国市场作为第一年的销售目标。
senses.why: Foreign comes from Latin foris 'outside', so a foreign market is literally the market outside the gate of one's own country.
senses.whyCN: foreign 出自拉丁 foris「门外」，因此外国市场字面上就是本国大门之外的市场。

senses.title: The market of one specific country
senses.titleCN: 某一个具体国家的市场
senses.definition: the market of a named country, with its own buyers, rules and habits
senses.definitionCN: 某个具名国家的市场，有其自身的买方、规则与习惯
senses.example: The German foreign market proved harder to enter than expected.
senses.exampleCN: 德国这一外国市场比预想的更难进入。
senses.why: The phrase can be counted, so each national market becomes a separate foreign market with its own features.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语可以计数，于是每个国家市场都成为一个具有自身特点的外国市场。

senses.title: Foreign demand for a product
senses.definition: the demand for a product that comes from buyers in other countries
senses.definitionCN: 来自他国买方对某产品的需求
senses.example: Foreign market demand for the vaccine outstripped supply.
senses.exampleCN: 境外市场对这种疫苗的需求超过了供给。
senses.why: Market also means the buyers themselves, so foreign market demand is demand located beyond the border.
senses.whyCN: market 也可指买方本身，因此境外市场需求就是位于边界之外的需求。

senses.title: The act of entering a foreign market
senses.titleCN: 进入外国市场这一动作
senses.definition: the process of establishing sales in a country other than one's own
senses.definitionCN: 在本国之外的国家建立销售的过程
senses.example: Foreign market entry usually begins with a local partner.
senses.exampleCN: 进入外国市场通常从本地伙伴开始。
senses.why: From a firm's viewpoint the market is a door, and the phrase becomes a stage in an expansion plan.
senses.whyCN: 从企业视角看，市场是一道门，这个短语于是成为扩张计划中的一个阶段。

senses.title: Share held in markets abroad
senses.titleCN: 在境外市场所占的份额
senses.definition: the portion of sales in other countries held by a firm or country
senses.definitionCN: 某企业或某国在他国销售中所占的部分
senses.example: The brand holds a tenth of the foreign market in cosmetics.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌在化妆品境外市场中占十分之一。
senses.why: Share language turns the market into a pie, and the foreign adjective marks which pie is being divided.
senses.whyCN: 份额说法把市场变成一块饼，foreign 这个形容词标明被分的是哪一块饼。

senses.title: The rules and conditions abroad
senses.titleCN: 境外的规则与经营条件
senses.definition: the legal, tariff and commercial conditions that govern trade in another country
senses.definitionCN: 管束他国贸易的法律、关税与商业条件
senses.example: Tariffs and labelling rules shape each foreign market differently.
senses.exampleCN: 关税与标签规则使每个外国市场各不相同。
senses.why: A market is not only buyers but also the rules around them, so the phrase often appears beside regulation and risk.
senses.whyCN: 市场不只是买方，还包括围绕他们的规则，因此这个短语常与监管、风险并置。

senses.title: Foreign buyers as a customer group
senses.titleCN: 作为客户群的境外买方
senses.definition: the group of customers abroad that a seller treats as one audience
senses.definitionCN: 境外被卖方当作一个客户群体对待的买方
senses.example: The catalogue was rewritten for a foreign market.
senses.exampleCN: 这份产品目录为外国市场重新编写。
senses.why: Marketing treats the foreign market as an audience with shared tastes, which is why catalogues and campaigns are adapted.
senses.whyCN: 营销把外国市场当作有共同口味的受众，因此目录与推广都要改写。

senses.title: Any unfamiliar arena outside one's own
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：自己圈子之外的陌生场域
senses.definition: an unfamiliar external setting in which one must compete or prove oneself
senses.definitionCN: 必须在其间竞争或证明自己的陌生外部场域
senses.example: For a local painter, the capital was a foreign market in every sense.
senses.exampleCN: 对一位本地画家来说，首都在任何意义上都是一个陌生的外部市场。
senses.why: The abstract sense drops trade and keeps only outsideness: any field where one is an outsider qualifies.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义去掉贸易，只保留「在外」：任何自己是外人的领域都符合。

intro.en: Foreign market joins foreign, from Latin foris 'outside', with market, from Latin mercatus 'trade'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: foreign market 把出自拉丁 foris「门外」的 foreign，与出自拉丁 mercatus「交易」的 market 组合起来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Foris meant 'outside, out of doors', and it built adjectives about what lies beyond a boundary.
items.cn: foris 意为「在外、门外」，构成一批表示「边界之外」的形容词。

items.en: Foranus 'outside, exterior' passed through Old French as forain, giving English foreign in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: foranus「外部的、外面的」经古法语 forain 传入，在 15 世纪形成英语 foreign。

items.en: Mercatus meant trade or a marketplace, from mercari 'to trade' and merx 'merchandise'.
items.cn: mercatus 意为交易或市场，出自 mercari「做买卖」与 merx「货物」。

items.en: English borrowed market through Latin and French, and it soon covered both the place and the demand found there.
items.cn: 英语经拉丁语与法语借入 market，很快既指地点，也指那里出现的需求。

items.en: Foreign market became standard in export practice, usually in contrast with the home or domestic market.
items.cn: foreign market 在出口实务中成为标准说法，通常与本国市场或国内市场相对。

note.en: The first group shares the outside root or looks close to it; the second group names markets that differ by whose viewpoint is taken.
note.cn: 第一组共享「在外」词根或与之外形相近；第二组是按立场区分的不同市场。

entries.definition: A person from another country; the root describes outsideness, but the word names a human, not a market.
entries.definitionCN: 来自另一国的人；词根表示「在外」，但这个词指人，不指市场。

entries.definition: A large wooded area, from medieval Latin forestis silva 'the wood outside', built on foris; it shares the root but means woodland.
entries.definitionCN: 大片林地，出自中世纪拉丁 forestis silva「外面的林子」，由 foris 构成；同根但指树林。

entries.definition: To lose something as a penalty, from foris 'outside' plus facere 'do', originally to do something outside the law.
entries.definitionCN: 因受罚而失去某物，出自 foris「在外」加 facere「做」，原指做了法外之事。

entries.definition: A public square or debate setting, from Latin forum; it looks like foreign but has no connection to foris.
entries.definitionCN: 公共广场或讨论场所，出自拉丁 forum；它与 foreign 形近，却与 foris 无关。

entries.definition: A market across the sea from the seller's country; foreign market is wider because a neighbour across a land border also counts.
entries.definitionCN: 从卖方国家隔海相望的市场；foreign market 范围更宽，因为陆上邻国也算。

entries.definition: The foreign market viewed as a destination for exports; it stresses the trade flow rather than the market itself.
entries.definitionCN: 作为出口目的地看待的外国市场；它强调贸易流向，而不是市场本身。

entries.definition: Trade conducted across national borders; it is neutral, while foreign market is always seen from one country's side.
entries.definitionCN: 跨国家进行的贸易；它保持中性，而 foreign market 始终从某一国的立场看。

entries.definition: The market where currencies are traded; it contains the same adjective but the trade is money, not goods or services.
entries.definitionCN: 交易货币的市场；它带同一个形容词，但交易对象是货币，不是货物或服务。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the outside root, the trade root and real export phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「在外」词根、交易词根与真实出口搭配。

normal.en: Foreign means outside the gate; market means trade; the phrase is trade beyond one's own gate.
normal.cn: foreign 意为大门之外，market 意为交易，短语就是本国大门之外的交易。

normal.en: The two halves have separate Latin sources: foris for outside, mercatus for trade.
normal.cn: 两半各有拉丁来源：foris 表「在外」，mercatus 表「交易」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the uses: enter a foreign market, foreign market share, foreign market entry.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示用法：进入外国市场、境外市场份额、外国市场进入。

normal.en: The phrase always implies a viewpoint: a market is foreign only relative to somebody's home.
normal.cn: 这个短语始终隐含一个立场：市场只有相对于某人的本国才叫外国市场。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with the currency market, which uses the same adjective but trades money.
normal.cn: 不要与货币市场混淆，后者带同一个形容词，却交易金钱。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn on a map with a gate in it, and the shops on the far side fly other flags.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上画着一条线，线上有一道门，线那侧的店铺挂着别的旗子。

abstract.en: Picture a merchant who must learn a new language before he can read the price tags.
abstract.cn: 想象一位商人必须先学会一门新语言，才看得懂价签。

abstract.en: Picture an artist whose own town is small, so every larger city feels like another country.
abstract.cn: 想象一位画家，自己的镇子很小，于是每座大城都像另一个国度。

examples.en: The firm opened a branch to serve the foreign market directly.
examples.cn: 这家公司开设分公司，直接服务外国市场。

examples.en: Local tastes forced a redesign for each foreign market.
examples.cn: 本地口味迫使公司为每个外国市场重新设计。

examples.en: Foreign market sales now exceed domestic ones.
examples.cn: 境外市场销售额如今超过了国内。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「门外的集市」——foris 是门外，market 是集市，本国门外的集市就是外国市场

root: foreign 出自拉丁 foris「门外」，经 foranus、古法语 forain 进入英语；market 出自拉丁 mercatus「交易」。合指「本国之外的市场」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all take a viewpoint: a market outside the home country, one named country's market, its demand, the act of entering it, a share of it, its rules, its buyers as an audience, and finally any unfamiliar arena.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都带一个立场：本国之外的市场、某一国的市场、其需求、进入它的动作、在其中所占份额、它的规则、作为受众的买方，最后是任何陌生的外部场域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a border line with shops on the far side flying other flags.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条边界线，线那侧的店铺挂着别的旗子。

branches.en: BASE OUTSIDENESS: the market lies beyond one's own border.
branches.cn: 基础的外在性：市场位于本国边界之外。

branches.en: NAMED AND COUNTED: each country is a market, and its buyers are demand.
branches.cn: 具名与计量：每个国家都是一个市场，其买方构成需求。

branches.en: FIRM ACTION: the market is entered, then measured by share.
branches.cn: 企业行动：先进入市场，再用份额衡量。

branches.en: RULES AND AUDIENCE: tariffs govern it, and buyers form an audience.
branches.cn: 规则与受众：关税管束它，买方构成受众。

branches.en: METAPHOR: any unfamiliar arena can be called foreign.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何陌生的场域都可以被称为「外国」。

intro.en: Foreign market is a phrase of two free words, one about outsideness and one about trade, each with its own Latin line.
intro.cn: foreign market 是由两个自由词构成的短语，一个讲「在外」，一个讲交易，各有拉丁线索。

latinIntro.en: Latin foris 'outside' gives foreign, foreigner and forest; Latin mercatus 'trade' gives market, marketing, marketplace and merchant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 foris「门外」衍生 foreign、foreigner 与 forest；拉丁 mercatus「交易」衍生 market、marketing、marketplace 与 merchant。

items.example: The element marks what lies beyond a boundary.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分标出边界之外的事物。

items.example: They studied foreign languages.
items.exampleCN: 他们学习外语。

items.example: A foreigner opened the shop.
items.exampleCN: 一位外国人开了这家店。

items.example: The accent gave a mild foreignness.
items.exampleCN: 这口音带来一丝异域感。

items.example: The forest lay beyond the river.
items.exampleCN: 森林在河的那一边。

items.meaning: a place or system of trade
items.example: The market opens early.
items.exampleCN: 市场开得早。

items.example: Marketing costs rose.
items.exampleCN: 营销成本上升了。

items.example: The marketplace was crowded.
items.exampleCN: 市场里很拥挤。

items.example: The merchant sold cloth.
items.exampleCN: 这位商人卖布。

items.example: They entered a foreign market.
items.exampleCN: 他们进入了一个外国市场。

definition_zh: 由于；因为；应付给（某人）的
definition_en: because of; on account of; (of a sum) owed and payable to someone
core_image: 渡轮停航，码头候船室里挤满滞留旅客，白浪一层层压向岸壁
scene: 暴雨冲断进山的公路，渡轮也停了，岛上游客在候船室过了一夜。 Ferry services were suspended owing to the storm.
sceneCN: 这里点明停航的原因（第 1 个义项：由于、因为）；句意为渡轮服务因风暴暂停。图中可辨识物件：白浪、码头、候船室、行李。

pos.zh: 介词短语：由于；因为（多作状语，可置于句首或句末）

collocations.phrase: owing to circumstances beyond our control
owing to a lack of funds

derivatives.zh: 由古英语动词直接演变成现代动词，义为「欠；应把……归功于」
由该动词加现在分词词尾构成，义为「欠着的；未付的」
由该动词加过去分词词尾构成，义为「被欠的；未偿还的」
由该动词的旧过去式演变而来，义为「应当」
由同一古英语动词的另一支演变而来，义为「拥有；自己的」
由「拥有」义加表示施动者的名词词尾构成，义为「所有者」

senses.title: Because of a cause
senses.definition: as a result of a cause that is named
senses.definitionCN: 由于句中已说明的原因而发生
senses.example: The game was postponed owing to fog.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛因大雾延期。
senses.why: Owing began as the participle of owe, so the phrase names what a result owes itself to.
senses.whyCN: 这个分词本是表示「欠」的动词的现在分词，因此短语说明结果欠了谁。

senses.title: Opening a clause with the cause
senses.definition: leading the sentence with the cause, a position the phrase takes freely as an adverbial
senses.definitionCN: 把原因放在句首，这是它作为状语可自由占据的位置
senses.example: Owing to the strike, buses stopped running.
senses.exampleCN: 由于罢工，公交车停运。
senses.why: Grown from a participle phrase, it behaves like an adverbial and can lead the clause.
senses.whyCN: 它由分词短语长成，像状语一样可以领起从句。

senses.title: Following a noun
senses.definition: placed after a noun in reports to explain that noun, like a shortened relative clause
senses.definitionCN: 在报告中置于名词之后解释该名词，相当于压缩的关系从句
senses.example: Losses owing to exchange rates were reported separately.
senses.exampleCN: 因汇率造成的损失另行报告。
senses.why: Financial writing packs the cause behind the noun it explains, keeping the sentence compact.
senses.whyCN: 财务文本把原因压在它所解释的名词之后，使句子紧凑。

senses.title: The padded connector owing to the fact that
senses.titleCN: 累赘连接语「由于……这一事实」
senses.definition: a wordy way of introducing a full clause as the cause
senses.definitionCN: 以冗长方式引出一个完整从句作为原因
senses.example: Output fell owing to the fact that two lines were idle.
senses.exampleCN: 产量下降是由于两条生产线停着。
senses.why: A full clause cannot follow the plain phrase, so writers pad it with a noun of fact.
senses.whyCN: 完整从句不能直接跟在短语后面，于是写作者用「事实」这个名词来撑开。

senses.title: Money still owed to someone
senses.definition: in accounts, an amount that is owed and payable to a person or estate
senses.definitionCN: 在账目中应付给个人或遗产的款项
senses.example: The statement lists the sums owing to the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 报表列出应付给遗产的款项。
senses.why: This is the oldest literal sense: the participle still means owed, and the phrase still takes a creditor.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的字面义：分词本义仍是「被欠的」，短语后面仍接收款方。

senses.title: In legal and procedural writing
senses.definition: used in formal notices to explain a procedural default
senses.definitionCN: 在正式通告中解释程序上的缺失
senses.example: Owing to the absence of a quorum, the vote was deferred.
senses.exampleCN: 由于不足法定人数，表决被推迟。
senses.why: Legal drafting prefers the phrase for a neutral, impersonal statement of cause.
senses.whyCN: 法律起草偏爱这个短语，因为它能中立而不带人称地交代原因。

senses.title: Standard excuse in business letters
senses.titleCN: 商务信函中的标准托辞
senses.definition: a set phrase in commercial correspondence for delays outside the seller's control
senses.definitionCN: 商务信函中说明卖方无法控制的延误的固定说法
senses.example: Owing to circumstances beyond our control, delivery is delayed.
senses.exampleCN: 由于无法控制的情况，交货延迟。
senses.why: Commercial letters turned the causal phrase into a polite formula for bad news.
senses.whyCN: 商务信函把这条因果短语变成了传达坏消息的礼貌套语。

senses.title: The traditional alternative to the other causal phrase
senses.titleCN: 另一个因果短语的传统替代说法
senses.definition: used as a free adverbial where older guidebooks reserved the other phrase for the position after be
senses.definitionCN: 作为自由状语使用，旧的语法书则把另一个因果短语留给系动词之后的位置
senses.example: Owing to staff shortages, the counter closed at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 由于人手不足，柜台中午就关了。
senses.why: Guidebooks once divided the labour: this phrase for adverbial positions, the other one for the verb be.
senses.whyCN: 旧语法书曾分工：这个短语用于状语位置，另一个用于系动词之后。

senses.title: Attribution in reporting style
senses.definition: used after the verb be in British reporting to attribute a change to a cause
senses.definitionCN: 英国报道文体中跟在系动词后，把变化归到某个原因
senses.example: The rise in cost was owing to higher freight charges.
senses.exampleCN: 成本上升是由于运费上涨。
senses.why: British journalism kept the phrase after the verb be long after American usage moved on.
senses.whyCN: 英国新闻写作在系动词后长期保留这一短语，美国用法则早已改换。

intro.en: Owing to joins the present participle of owe with the preposition to. Owe goes back to Old English agan, to own or have, whose past tense also produced ought. The participle meant what is owed, and from the eighteenth century the phrase came to mean because of.
intro.cn: 这条短语由表示「欠」的动词的现在分词与介词合成。该动词可追溯到古英语中表示「拥有、持有」的词，其过去式还演变出表示「应当」的情态动词。分词本义是「被欠着的」，从十八世纪起，整条短语转指「由于」。

items.en: The verb meant to own or possess, and its past tense also gave the modal of obligation.
items.cn: 这个动词意为拥有、持有，其过去式还演变出表示义务的情态动词。

items.en: By the fourteenth century the participle described a sum still owed to someone.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，这个分词已用来形容仍欠某人的款项。

items.en: In the eighteenth century the phrase began to introduce a cause rather than a creditor; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 十八世纪起，这条短语引出的是原因而非债主；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Because it grew out of a participle phrase, it moves freely to the front of a clause.
items.cn: 由于它从分词短语长成，位置可以自由移到从句开头。

items.en: Business letters and legal notices adopted the phrase for delays and procedural defaults.
items.cn: 商务信函与法律通告采用这条短语来说明延误与程序缺失。

items.en: British writing kept the phrase for formal causes while American usage leaned towards the rival form.
items.cn: 英国写作在正式原因上保留这条短语，美国用法则偏向另一个竞争形式。

note.en: The first group shares the root or the participle; the second group lists other causal expressions.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一词根或同一分词；第二组是其他因果表达。

entries.definition: Still owed; also the participle behind the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 仍欠着的；也是这条短语背后的分词。

entries.definition: To be under an obligation to pay or to credit someone.
entries.definitionCN: 指欠钱，或应把功劳归给某人。

entries.definition: The modal of obligation that grew from the old past tense.
entries.definitionCN: 由旧过去式演变来的表示义务的情态动词。

entries.definition: To possess, from the same Old English verb.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有，出自同一个古英语动词。

entries.definition: One who possesses something.
entries.definitionCN: 指拥有某物的人。

entries.definition: Because of; traditionally the attributive member of the pair.
entries.definitionCN: 由于；传统上这一对短语中的表语成员。

entries.definition: The plainest causal preposition with a noun object.
entries.definitionCN: 最朴素的因果介词，后接名词。

entries.definition: Because of, common in formal explanation.
entries.definitionCN: 由于，常见于正式解释。

entries.definition: Following from an earlier cause, with the outcome in view.
entries.definitionCN: 由于先前的原因，着眼于结果。

entries.definition: A legal and official way of saying because of.
entries.definitionCN: 法律与公文里表示「由于」的说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the participle of owing, its accounting sense and its freedom of position.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着「欠」的分词义，串起账目用法与位置自由。

normal.en: The participle means owed, so a result owing to a cause is a result in debt to it.
normal.cn: 分词意为「被欠的」，所以因某原因而发生的结果，就是欠那个原因一笔。

normal.en: This phrase may lead the sentence, which the rival causal phrase traditionally may not.
normal.cn: 这条短语可以领起句子，而另一个因果短语传统上不行。

normal.en: Sums owing to the estate is the literal accounting use, unchanged in meaning for centuries.
normal.cn: 「应付给遗产的款项」是字面账目用法，几个世纪意思都没变。

normal.en: Business letters use the phrase with circumstances beyond control, a polite formula for delay.
normal.cn: 商务信函把它与「无法控制的情况」连用，成为说明延误的礼貌套语。

normal.en: Legal notices use it for a missing quorum, where no person needs to be blamed.
normal.cn: 法律通告用它说明人数不足，不必归咎于任何个人。

abstract.en: A participle of debt turned into a preposition of cause: obligation became explanation.
abstract.cn: 「欠」的分词变成了因果介词：义务变成了解释。

abstract.en: To say owing to is to admit that the outcome was already owed to something else.
abstract.cn: 说「由于」，等于承认结果本来就该记在别的东西账上。

abstract.en: Freedom of position is freedom of blame: the cause can stand in front of the sentence.
abstract.cn: 位置自由就是归责自由：原因可以站到整句前面。

examples.en: Owing to a broken pump, the pool stayed closed all week.
examples.cn: 由于水泵损坏，泳池整周关闭。

examples.en: The order was delayed owing to a shortage of drivers.
examples.cn: 订单因司机短缺而延误。

examples.en: Owing to the chairman's illness, the meeting was moved online.
examples.cn: 由于主席生病，会议改为线上举行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「欧应」——欧洲的货应到未到，追问缘由就是「由于」：由于、因为

root: 这个现在分词出自古英语中意为「拥有、欠」的动词，其过去式演变为表「应当」的情态动词；这条短语自十八世纪起表示「由于」，确切首见年代不确定。纯英语本族来源，无拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow the participle from a literal debt to a free adverbial, and then to legal and commercial formulas.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿着这个分词从字面债务走到自由状语，再到法律与商务套语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stranded ferry queue, every passenger kept ashore by the same storm.
core.cn: 核心意象：滞留的渡轮队伍，每个旅客都被同一场风暴困在岸上。

branches.en: THE FREE CAUSE: the phrase names a cause and may lead the clause.
branches.cn: 自由原因：短语点明原因，并可领起从句。

branches.en: THE PACKED CAUSE: behind a noun, or padded with a noun of fact before a clause.
branches.cn: 压缩原因：压在名词之后，或用「事实」撑开再接从句。

branches.en: THE LITERAL DEBT: the same participle still points at a creditor in accounts.
branches.cn: 字面债务：同一个分词在账目里仍指向收款方。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTIONAL EXCUSE: procedural defaults and delays beyond control.
branches.cn: 机构式交代：程序缺失与无法控制的延误。

branches.en: THE STYLE CHOICE: a traditional adverbial and a British reporting habit.
branches.cn: 文体选择：传统状语用法与英国报道习惯。

intro.en: The phrase is built from an Old English verb of possession, so its parts are native rather than borrowed.
intro.cn: 这条短语由古英语的「拥有」动词构成，各部件都是本族成分而非借词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for this family: it comes from Old English, so the Latin list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这一族词没有拉丁语来源，出自古英语，因此拉丁词条留空。

items.example: The verb held both possession and obligation.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词同时含「拥有」与「应还」两层。

items.example: Its past tense later became the modal of obligation.
items.exampleCN: 它的过去式后来变成表义务的情态动词。

items.example: The modern verb keeps the debt sense.
items.exampleCN: 现代动词保留债务义。

items.example: It forms the participle meaning still owed.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「仍被欠着」的分词。

items.example: The past participle keeps the accounting sense.
items.exampleCN: 过去分词保留账目义。

items.example: It descends from the old past tense.
items.exampleCN: 它由旧过去式演变而来。

items.example: A second branch of the same old verb.
items.exampleCN: 同一个古动词的另一支。

items.example: The agent noun of the possession branch.
items.exampleCN: 「拥有」这一支的施动名词。

items.example: It carries the cause or the creditor after the participle.
items.exampleCN: 它在分词后接原因或收款方。

items.example: The whole phrase works as a causal adverbial.
items.exampleCN: 整条短语充当因果状语。
